SULAMI:v1p21/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p21/r5.claim: One unnamed view says al-Fātiḥa is named for opening the delight of intimate address, making it an opening to every good.
SULAMI:v1p21/r5.anchor: قيل : إنها سميت فاتحة الكتاب لأنه فتح عليك فاتحته لذيذ مناجاته فكانت فاتحة لكل خير

SULAMI:v1p21/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r6.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p21/r6.claim: Another view treats the title as God's first opening of discourse: proper conduct grants access to later subtleties, while failure bars them.
SULAMI:v1p21/r6.anchor: وقيل أيضا : فاتحة الكتاب ؛ أنه أوائل ما فتحناك من خطابنا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r8.claim: The critics say Ibn Masʿūd's codex differed from others, omitted the Opening, and erased the two protective sūras, which he denied belonged in the Book.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p24/r8.anchor: وكان يحذف من مصحفه أم الكتاب ويمحو المعوذتين ويقول: لم تزيدون في كتاب الله ما ليس فيه؟

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r18.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r18.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r18.claim: Abu Ubayda says the word اسم is added in بسم الله, whose intended meaning is بالله.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r18.anchor: و (الاسم) يزاد، قال: أبو عبيدة: بسم الله إنما هو بالله،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r3.claim: The hamza is omitted from باسم because it is hamzat waṣl, yielding the written and pronounced form بسم.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p644/r3.anchor: حذفت الهمزة في كلمة (باسم) للوصل فأصبحت تكتب وتلفظ (بسم) كما في (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r4.claim: The author derives الله from أل الإله, with the alif deleted, and links the name to worship in the Qur’an.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r4.anchor: أصلها من أل الإله حُذفت الألف فأصبحت (الله)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p811/r6.anchor: أما الشكر فهو مقابلة النعمة بالفعل. وكلمة الرحمن من الرحمة.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a divine hadith, transmitted by Muslim and the four Sunan collections, in which God answers the servant's phrases in al-Fatiha and shares the central petition between them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r2.anchor: رواه مسلم والأربعة عن أبي هريرة قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r3.claim: The hadith shows al-Fatiha is arranged in three sections, an instance of the rhetorical art of balanced division.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p108/r3.anchor: في هذا الحديث تنبيه على ما في نظم فاتحة الكتاب من خصوصية التقسيم إذ قسم الفاتحة ثلاثة أقسام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r10.claim: An authentic hadith calls al-Fatiha the seven oft-repeated, meaning its seven verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p74/r10.anchor: قلت وفي الحديث الصحيح أن فاتحة الكتاب السبع المثاني أي السبع الآيات

BURHAN:v1p29/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.claim: An ayah may descend twice to magnify its importance and recall it when a new cause arises; the Fatiha is said to have descended once in Mecca and once in Medina, and this resolves the report about the Makkan Hūd verse.
BURHAN:v1p29/r1.anchor: وقد ينزل الشىء مرتين تعظيما لشأنه وتذكيرا به عند حدوث سببه خوف نسيانه وهذا كما قيل فى الفاتحة نزلت مرتين

BURHAN:v1p100/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r2.claim: The basmala is counted differently because it came as part of a verse in some readings; readers of those modes count it, while others omit it and count a replacement after اهدنا to keep al-Fatiha seven verses.
BURHAN:v1p100/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ بحرف نزلت فيه عدها آية ولم يحتج إلى إثباتها بالقياس

BURHAN:v1p251/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r5.claim: The basmala is counted in readings where it descended with the sūra and omitted in readings where it did not.
BURHAN:v1p251/r5.anchor: وأيضا البسملة نزلت مع السورة فى بعض الأحرف السبعة فمن قرأ بحرف نزلت فيه عدها

BURHAN:v1p267/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p267/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
BURHAN:v1p267/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi cites reports that al-Fatiha has seven verses and al-Mulk thirty, and that the Prophet recited Aal Imran's final ten; verse counts should follow early Muslims' practice.
BURHAN:v1p267/r3.anchor: ذكر النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الفاتحة سبع آيات وسورة الملك ثلاثون آية وصح أنه قرأ العشر الآيات الخواتيم

ITQAN:v1p104/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p104/r3.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v1p104/r3.claim: Some authorities include al-Fātiḥa among verses revealed repeatedly.

ITQAN:v1p183/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ITQAN:v1p183/r3.claim: The majority count al-Fatiha as seven verses, with Kufan and Meccan counters counting the basmala but not “anʿamta ʿalayhim,” and others doing the reverse.
ITQAN:v1p183/r3.anchor: الفاتحة الجمهور سبع فعد الكوفي والمكي البسملة دون أنعمت عليهم وعكس الباقون

ITQAN:v1p183/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r4.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v1p183/r4.claim: Al-Hasan counts al-Fatiha as eight verses by including both the basmala and “anʿamta ʿalayhim.”
ITQAN:v1p183/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن ثمان فعدهما وبعضهم ست فلم يعدهما

ITQAN:v1p183/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p183/r5.claim: Some count al-Fatiha as six verses by counting neither the basmala nor “anʿamta ʿalayhim.”
ITQAN:v1p183/r5.anchor: وبعضهم ست فلم يعدهما وآخر تسع فعدهما و ﴿ إياك نعبد ﴾

ITQAN:v1p183/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r6.speaker: آخر
ITQAN:v1p183/r6.claim: Another view counts al-Fatiha as nine verses, including both the basmala and “iyyāka naʿbud.”
ITQAN:v1p183/r6.anchor: وآخر تسع فعدهما و ﴿ إياك نعبد ﴾

ITQAN:v1p183/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p183/r7.speaker: أم سلمة
ITQAN:v1p183/r7.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha verse by verse, counted the basmala as a verse, and did not count “ʿalayhim”; al-Suyuti says this supports the majority's seven-verse count.
ITQAN:v1p183/r7.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.claim: Al-Harali maps al-Fatiha's verses to the seven letters: praise, lawful and forbidden, command and prohibition, clear and ambiguous, then the corresponding petitions; its opening gathers all seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع

QASHANI:1:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r1.claim: Names are the determinate forms by which divine attributes and essence are known: their identities signify attributes and essence, existence signifies His face, and their individuation His unity.

QASHANI:1:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r2.claim: Allah names the divine essence absolutely, without reference either to its being qualified by attributes or to its lack of attributes.
QASHANI:1:1/r2.anchor: اسم للذات الإلهية من حيث هي هي على الإطلاق

QASHANI:1:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r3.claim: The All-Merciful grants existence and perfection universally according to wisdom and each recipient’s capacity at the beginning.
QASHANI:1:1/r3.anchor: هو المفيض للوجود والكمال على الكل بحسب ما تقتضي الحكمة

QASHANI:1:1/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r4.claim: The Especially Merciful grants the human kind its particular spiritual perfection at the end; the perfected human form gathers universal and special mercy and manifests the divine essence and all attributes.
QASHANI:1:1/r4.anchor: هو المفيض للكمال المعنوي المخصوص بالنوع الإنساني بحسب النهاية

QASHANI:1:1/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:1:1/r5.claim: The Prophet says he was given comprehensive speech and sent to complete noble character; existent things are realities, while noble character’s states and sources of action are gathered in the universal human being.
QASHANI:1:1/r5.anchor: أوتيت جوامع الكلم، وبعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق

QASHANI:1:1/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r6.claim: Prophets placed alphabet letters opposite levels of beings; existence emerged from bāʾ because it follows the alif symbolizing God’s essence, and bāʾ signifies the first intellect, God’s first creation.
QASHANI:1:1/r6.anchor: ظهرت الموجودات من باء بسم الله إذ هي الحرف الذي يلي الألف الموضوعة بإزاء ذات الله

QASHANI:1:1/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r7.claim: The first intellect is addressed in a report that God created no creature dearer or more honored, and acts of giving, taking, reward, and punishment occur through it.
QASHANI:1:1/r7.anchor: ما خلقت خلقا أحب إلي ولا أكرم علي منك

QASHANI:1:1/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r8.claim: The basmala has eighteen pronounced letters and nineteen written letters; when words are separated, the count becomes twenty-two.
QASHANI:1:1/r8.anchor: والحروف الملفوظة لهذه الكلمة ثمانية عشر، والمكتوبة تسعة عشر

QASHANI:1:1/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1/r9.claim: Eighteen signifies eighteen thousand worlds, whose principal realms are the dominion, kingdom, Throne, Footstool, heavens, elements, and three genera of offspring.
QASHANI:1:1/r9.anchor: فالثمانية عشر إشارة إلى العوالم المعبر عنها بثمانية عشر ألف عالم

QASHANI:1:1#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r1.claim: The nineteenth letter signifies the human world as a distinct realm because humanity’s nobility and comprehensiveness gather the whole cosmos, as Gabriel is distinguished among angels.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r1.anchor: والتسعة عشر إشارة إليها مع العالم الإنساني، فإنه وإن كان داخلا

QASHANI:1:1#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r2.claim: Three hidden alifs complete the twenty-two letters and signify the divine world in respect of essence, attributes, and acts: three in detailed consideration, one in realization.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r2.anchor: والألفات الثلاثة المحتجبة التي هي تتمة الاثنين والعشرين عند الانفصال

QASHANI:1:1#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r3.claim: The three written alifs signify those worlds appearing in the supreme human manifestation while the divine world remains veiled.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r3.anchor: والثلاثة المكتوبة إشارة إلى ظهور تلك العوالم على المظهر الأعظمي الإنساني ولاحتجاب العالم الإلهي

QASHANI:1:1#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QASHANI:1:1#2/r4.claim: Asked where the alif of the basmala went, the Messenger replies that Satan stole it; he orders the bāʾ lengthened in its place.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r4.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ألف الباء من أين ذهبت؟ قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " سرقها الشيطان "

QASHANI:1:1#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r5.claim: Lengthening bāʾ compensates for the hidden alif: divinity is concealed in diffusive mercy and appears in human form, knowable only to its people, hence the indefinite form.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r5.anchor: وأمر بتطويل باء بسم الله تعويضا عن ألفها إشارة إلى احتجاب ألوهية الإلهية في صورة الرحمة الانتشارية

QASHANI:1:1#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r6.claim: A hadith says God created Adam in His image; the author explains a hierarchy of veils from essence by attributes, from attributes by acts, and from acts by beings and effects.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r6.anchor: إن الله تعالى خلق آدم على صورته

QASHANI:1:1#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r7.claim: Disclosure of acts beyond the veil of created effects yields trust; disclosure of attributes beyond acts yields contentment and surrender; disclosure of essence beyond attributes yields annihilation in unity and absolute unification.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r7.anchor: فمن تجلت عليه الأفعال بارتفاع حجب الأكوان توكل، ومن تجلت عليه الصفات بارتفاع حجب الأفعال رضي وسلم

QASHANI:1:1#2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:1#2/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:1#2/r8.claim: Unification of acts precedes unification of attributes, which precedes unification of essence; the three are reflected in the Prophet’s prostration supplication seeking refuge in pardon, pleasure, and God Himself.
QASHANI:1:1#2/r8.anchor: فتوحيد الأفعال مقدم على توحيد الصفات وهو على توحيد الذات وإلى الثلاثة أشار صلوات الله عليه في سجوده

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r1.claim: The Fatiha is called the Mother of the Book because it commands servanthood and praises God's lordship; the report of prayer divided between God and servant refers to reciting it, making it the basis of subtle gifts and nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r1.anchor: وتسمى هذه السورة أيضا أم الكتاب ، وأم الشيء أصله ، وإمام كل شيء مقدمه . وهذه السورة

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r2.claim: The opening “in the name” means events appear and creatures exist through God; everything created begins from Him and returns to Him, and acts of belief, denial, recognition, and sin all occur through Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r2.anchor: الباء في بسم الله حرف التضمين ؛ أي بالله ظهرت الحادثات ، وبه وجدت المخلوقات ، فما من

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r3.claim: One explanation for saying “in the name of God” rather than “by God” is to seek blessing by mentioning the name.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r3.anchor: وقال : { بسم الله } ولم يقل بالله على وجه التبرك بذكر اسمه عند قوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r4.claim: Another explanation distinguishes the phrase from an oath.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r4.anchor: وللفرق بين هذا وبين القسم عند الآخرين

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r5.claim: The theologians say that the name is the named one.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r5.anchor: ولأن الاسم هو المسمى عند العلماء

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r6.claim: The gnostics intend to clear hearts of attachments and secrets of obstacles so that the name Allah arrives to a purified heart and secret.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r6.anchor: ولاستصفاء القلوب من العلائق ولاستخلاص الأسرار عن العوائق عند أهل العرفان ، ليكون ورود قوله { الله }

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r7.speaker: قوم
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r7.claim: One group reads the letters bāʾ, sīn, and mīm as God's kindness to His friends, secret with intimates, and favor to those under His protection.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r7.anchor: قوم عند ذكر هذه الآية يتذكرون من الباء ( بره ) بأوليائه ومن السين سره مع أصفيائه ومن

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r8.speaker: قوم
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r8.claim: Another group takes the letters to signify God's freedom from evil, safety from defect, and glory in His attributes.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r8.anchor: وقوم عند سماع بسم الله تذكروا بالباء براءة الله سبحانه وتعالى من كل سوء ، وبالسين سلامته سبحانه

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r9.speaker: آخرون
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r9.claim: Others associate the letters with His radiance, sublimity, and dominion.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r9.anchor: وآخرون يذكرون عند الباء بهاءه ، وعند السين سناءه ، وعند الميم ملكه

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r10.claim: Since the basmala recurs at the beginning of each surah and is established as part of it, Qushayri gives distinct, non-repeated allusions in each surah and treats this one at length here.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r10.anchor: فلما أعاد الله سبحانه وتعالى هذه الآية أعني بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في كل سورة وثبت أنها منها

QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r11.claim: The lover finds blame for loving the beloved pleasurable; Qushayri reads the command in 15:97 as listening to what is said with praise of God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p8/r11.anchor: والحق سبحانه يقول ) : ^ ( ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون فسبح بحمد ربك

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم الحكيم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r1.claim: The opening formula signals love as the beginning.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الحكيم : ' بسم الله

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r2.speaker: العباس بن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r2.claim: The letters signify God's inspiration of prophecy to prophets, nearness and intimacy to knowers, and enduring compassionate attention to seekers.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r2.anchor: حكي عن العباس بن عطاء أنه قال : الباء بره لأرواح الأنبياء بإلهام الرسالة والنبوة

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r3.claim: He reads bism as divine awe, al-Rahman as aid, and al-Rahim as affection and love.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r3.anchor: وقال الجنيد في ' بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ' : بسم الله هيبته

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r4.claim: The prophets appear and pass away through God; His manifestation beautifies beauty, and His illumination opens and makes things generous.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r4.anchor: وقيل الباء في ' بسم الله ' بالله ظهرت الأنبياء

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r5.claim: Knowers empty and purify their hearts for God; their first gift is annihilation of all besides Him and exclusive affiliation to Him rather than Adam.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r5.anchor: إن أهل المعرفة نفوا عن قلوبهم كل شيء سوى الله عز وجل ، وصفوا قلوبهم لله

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r6.claim: The formula preserves created forms: opening by God's essence would dissolve creation, except prophets and saints; the name illuminates knowers' hearts.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r6.anchor: وقيل أيضا : إن ' بسم ' لبقاء هياكل الخلق

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r7.claim: Bismillah marks the people of reality, who adorn themselves only with the Real and swear only by Him.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r7.anchor: وقيل في ' بسم الله ' : إنه صفاة أهل الحقيقة

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r8.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r8.claim: He assigns the letters the meanings of God's secret among knowers, peace upon them, and His love for them.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : الباء سر الله بالعارفين ، والسين السلام عليهم

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r9.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet, explicitly qualified as possibly unauthentic, maps the letters to God's splendor, radiance, and majesty.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r9.anchor: وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن صح هذا ، الباء بهاؤه والسين سناؤه

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r10.claim: The bāʾ is the means by which they reach God's name.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : إن الباء في ' بسم الله ' إلينا وصلهم

SULAMI:v1p24#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r11.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r11.claim: The letters mean God's abiding, names, and sovereignty; faith recalls His abiding, service recalls His names, and gnosis leaves the kingdom for its owner.
SULAMI:v1p24#2/r11.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام قال : ' بسم ' الباء بقاؤه

SULAMI:v1p26/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p26/r1.claim: The letters are the gate of prophecy, the prophetic secret entrusted to the Prophet's close followers, and the kingdom of the religion given to all peoples.
SULAMI:v1p26/r1.anchor: فالباء باب النبوة ، والسين سر النبوة الذي أسر بها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SULAMI:v1p26/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r2.speaker: محمد بن موسى الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p26/r2.claim: Invoking any divine name gives the invoker some personal share, but the name Allah calls only to oneness and contains no deficiency.
SULAMI:v1p26/r2.anchor: فإن محمد بن موسى الواسطي قال : ما دعى الله أحد باسم من أسمائه ، إلا ولنفسه في ذلك نصيب

SULAMI:v1p26/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p26/r3.claim: Unlike other names, which imply compensation when invoked, Allah is a name reserved uniquely for the Real.
SULAMI:v1p26/r3.anchor: وقيل : كل أسمائه تقتضي عوضا عند الدعاء إلا ' الله '

SULAMI:v1p26/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p26/r4.claim: Ordinary utterance of Allah is habitual; when God takes charge of a speaker who is veiled from self-awareness, faults and slips disappear.
SULAMI:v1p26/r4.anchor: وقيل : كل من قال : ' الله ' فمن عادة قالها

SULAMI:v1p26/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r5.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p26/r5.claim: Saying Bismillah resembles God's creative command Be: with acknowledgment of God's favor, things become actual through the formula.
SULAMI:v1p26/r5.anchor: وقال الحسين : بسم الله منك منزلة ' كن ' منه

SULAMI:v1p26/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r6.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p26/r6.claim: No one truly says Allah except God, since every other speaker says it from a personal share and shares cannot reach realities.
SULAMI:v1p26/r6.anchor: وحكي عن الشبلي أنه قال : ما قال الله أحد سوى الله ، فإن كل من قاله قاله بحظ

SULAMI:v1p26/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p26/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v1p26/r7.claim: He describes a seeker who has forgotten personal interests and needs, loses ordinary self-description, becomes filled with hidden divine light, and ultimately cannot utter the name in the limit of nearness.
SULAMI:v1p26/r7.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخراز في كتاب درجات المريدين : ومنهم من جاوز نسيان حظوظ نفسه

SULAMI:v1p28/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r1.speaker: الحسين بن منصور
SULAMI:v1p28/r1.claim: No one can remember God in His reality: He has no limit or cause, while letters and breaths are created and intellect cannot grasp Him.
SULAMI:v1p28/r1.anchor: وسئل الحسين بن منصور هل ذكره أحد على الحقيقة فقال : كيف يذكر على الحقيقة من لا أمد لكونه

SULAMI:v1p28/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p28/r2.claim: The letters of Allah signify beginning, recognition, blessings, the meanings of commands and prohibitions, and the ultimate hidden reality beyond worship's grasp.
SULAMI:v1p28/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الألف الأول من اسمه الله ابتداؤه ، واللام الأول لام المعرفة

SULAMI:v1p28/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p28/r3.claim: Another letter reading makes alif God's favors, the lām His gentleness and encounter, and hāʾ the awe that leaves lovers unable to know Him.
SULAMI:v1p28/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن الألف آلاء الله ، واللام لطف الله واللام الثاني لقاء الله

SULAMI:v1p28/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p28/r4.claim: Junayd checks that Nuri still observes prayer, then challenges whether God or Nuri himself says Allah; Nuri answers that it is love, and his ecstasy subsides.
SULAMI:v1p28/r4.anchor: فقال له الجنيد : انظر هل قولك الله الله أم قولك قولك إن كنت القائل الله

SULAMI:v1p28/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r5.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p28/r5.claim: Al-Shibli says Allah alone, rather than There is no god but God, because he will not use the latter to negate a rival.
SULAMI:v1p28/r5.anchor: فكان الشبلي يقول : الله فقيل له لم لا يقول لا إله إلا الله ؟ فقال : لا أنفي به ضدا

SULAMI:v1p28/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p28/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p28/r6.claim: Because the name itself is inaccessible in reality, pleasures are even more inaccessible, teaching creatures their inability to name God's essence.
SULAMI:v1p28/r6.anchor: وقيل في قوله : الله هو المانع الذي يمنع الوصول إليه

SULAMI:v1p30/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r1.claim: The letters signify oneness, then the erasure of indication and of that erasure in the disclosure of hāʾ.
SULAMI:v1p30/r1.anchor: وقيل في قوله الله : الألف إشارة إلى الوحدانية واللام إشارة إلى محو الإشارة

SULAMI:v1p30/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r2.claim: Alif signifies God's self-subsistence and separation from creation; letters depend upon it, while it depends on none.
SULAMI:v1p30/r2.anchor: إن الإشارة في الألف هو قيام الحق بنفسه وانفصاله عن جميع خلقه ولا اتصال له بشيء

SULAMI:v1p30/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r3.claim: Dropping letters from Allah leaves successive divine indications—lillah, lahu, then hāʾ—which is the utmost signification.
SULAMI:v1p30/r3.anchor: فإذا أسقطت منه الألف يكون ' لله ' فإذا أسقطت إحدى لاميه يكون ' له '

SULAMI:v1p30/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r4.claim: Created beings are enraptured variously: their secret by divine majesty, heart by forms of gnosis, or tongue by constant remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p30/r4.anchor: وأما وله الخلق في تولهم فمنهم من وله سره في عظمة جلاله

SULAMI:v1p30/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p30/r5.claim: Junayd tells Ibn Shibli that mentioning an absent God is backbiting; if one is absent it is such mention, while witnessing Him makes speech a breach of reverence.
SULAMI:v1p30/r5.anchor: وحكي عن ابن الشبلي قال في تجلي الجنيد في ولهه : الله فقال له الجنيد

SULAMI:v1p30/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r6.claim: Uttering Allah through letters cannot truly name Him, since He exceeds letters, concepts, and imaginings; the formula is accepted because no other mode of affirming oneness is possible.
SULAMI:v1p30/r6.anchor: من قال الله بالحروف ، فإنه لم يقل الله لأنه خارج عن الحروف والخصوص والأوهام

SULAMI:v1p30/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p30/r7.claim: All names' meanings are contained in Allah, but Allah's name derives from none; God alone bears it, though creatures share derivations of other names.
SULAMI:v1p30/r7.anchor: وقيل إن معنى قول الله : إن الأسماء كلها داخل في هذا الاسم

SULAMI:v1p30/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r8.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p30/r8.claim: The visible letters are not God Himself; when the letters disappear, the indication is that He is God.
SULAMI:v1p30/r8.anchor: وقال بعض البغدادين : ليس الله ما يبدو لكم وبكم

SULAMI:v1p30/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r9.speaker: أبو العباس بن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p30/r9.claim: The name Allah manifests divine awe and majesty.
SULAMI:v1p30/r9.anchor: وقال أبو العباس بن عطاء : قوله : ' الله ' هو إظهار هيبته

SULAMI:v1p30/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p30/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v1p30/r10.claim: Only God can name, see, or know God; before servant and creation there was only God, and all existence is through and for Him.
SULAMI:v1p30/r10.anchor: هل هو إلا الله ، وهل يقدر أحد أن يقول الله إلا الله ، وهل يرى الله إلا الله

SULAMI:v1p31/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p31/r1.speaker: حكيم من الحكماء
SULAMI:v1p31/r1.claim: The ultimate goal is God; the supplication asks for guidance to Him, steadfastness in His presence, freedom from substitutes, and settlement at the encounter.
SULAMI:v1p31/r1.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز : رأيت حكيما من الحكماء فقلت له : ما غاية هذا الأمر قال : الله

SULAMI:v1p31/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p31/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v1p31/r2.claim: God first called servants to the single name Allah; people of realities need that name, while further descriptions in the chapter serve successively lower ranks.
SULAMI:v1p31/r2.anchor: إن الله عز وجل أول ما دعا عباده دعاهم إلى كلمة واحدة فمن فهمها فقد فهم ما وراءها

SULAMI:v1p31/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p31/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p31/r3.claim: Every divine name may be emulated except Allah, which is for attachment to God rather than taking on His name.
SULAMI:v1p31/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن كل أسمائه تتهيىء أن يتخلق به إلا قوله الله

SULAMI:v1p31/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p31/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p31/r4.claim: In Allah, the two lām letters and hāʾ are connected while alif is separate, indicating that the reference to God is not made through the servant's own self.
SULAMI:v1p31/r4.anchor: وقيل : إن الإشارة في ' الله ' هو اتصال اللامين والهاء

SULAMI:v1p31/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p31/r5.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p31/r5.claim: The four letters form a complete, unique name: alif is the pillar of oneness, the two lām letters signify the Tablet of the Pen and of Prophecy, and hāʾ is the utmost indication; God exceeds apprehension.
SULAMI:v1p31/r5.anchor: سمعت منصورا بإسناده عن جعفر أنه قال في قوله ' الله ' : إنه اسم تام

SULAMI:v1p32/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p32/r1.claim: All enduring graces for believers issue through al-Rahman, and no creature can bear that name because creatures cannot give what lasts.
SULAMI:v1p32/r1.anchor: باسم الرحمن خرجت جميع الكرامات للمؤمنين مثل الإيمان والطاعات والولاية

SULAMI:v1p32/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p32/r2.claim: Al-Rahman's mercy lets seekers detach from everything below Him; its worldly bounty reaches friend and enemy alike.
SULAMI:v1p32/r2.anchor: وأيضا فإن رحمة الرحمانية للمريدين بها ينفصلون عما دون الرحمن

SULAMI:v1p32/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p32/r3.claim: Al-Rahman signifies the sweetness of benefaction, witnessed nearness, and careful service.
SULAMI:v1p32/r3.anchor: وقيل في اسمه الرحمن : حلاوة المنة ومشاهدة القربة ومحافظة الخدمة

SULAMI:v1p32/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p32/r4.claim: Lovers, the fearful, repentant, and sinners each receive a distinct spiritual fruit from the meanings of al-Rahman: intimacy, security, purification, or remorse and seeking forgiveness.
SULAMI:v1p32/r4.anchor: والخائفون يتلذذون في قلوبهم في معاني اسمه الرحمن ويتزودون منها حلاوة السكون

SULAMI:v1p32/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p32/r5.claim: Al-Rahman means God's aid and victory.
SULAMI:v1p32/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : في اسمه الرحمن عونه ونصرته

SULAMI:v1p32/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p32/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p32/r6.claim: One approaches al-Rahman only through His all-encompassing mercy, while al-Rahim is approached through obedience; the Prophet also bears the latter name (9:128).
SULAMI:v1p32/r6.anchor: وقال الواسطي : الرحمن لا يتقرب إليه أحد إلا بصرف رحمانيته

SULAMI:v1p33/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p33/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p33/r1.claim: Al-Rahim denotes mercy for creatures' livelihood and bodily welfare, so creatures may be called rahim, unlike the uniquely divine Rahman.
SULAMI:v1p33/r1.anchor: يقال : إن معنى الرحيم هو ما يخرج من الرحمة الرحيمية لمعاش الخلق

SULAMI:v1p33/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p33/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p33/r2.claim: The Prophet, called compassionate and merciful toward believers, is a means by which people reach God and the two divine names; the Merciful accepts the returning person despite faults and preserves even one who turns away.
SULAMI:v1p33/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن معنى الرحيم أي بالرحيم وصلتم إلى الله وإلى الرحمن

SULAMI:v1p33/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p33/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p33/r3.claim: Al-Rahim signifies God's affection and mercy.
SULAMI:v1p33/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : في اسمه ' الرحيم ' مودته ورحمته

SULAMI:v1p33/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p33/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p33/r4.claim: Al-Rahman suits those sought by God, immersed in lights and realities; al-Rahim suits seekers remaining with themselves and tending outward practice.
SULAMI:v1p33/r4.anchor: هو واقع على المريدين والمرادين ، فاسم الرحمن للمرادين لاستغراقهم في الأنوار

SULAMI:v1p33/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p33/r5.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p33/r5.claim: Al-Rahman's mercy reaches back into pre-eternity and has no endpoint, whereas al-Rahim connects mercy with worldly life, guidance, and provisions.
SULAMI:v1p33/r5.anchor: والرحمن المنتهى بكرامته إلى ما غاية له لأنه قد أوصل الرحمة بالأزل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the first revelation began with the command to say the basmala and to read by remembering God, rising and sitting in His remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : اول ما انزل جبريل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak assigns the letters of bism to God's splendor, sublime glory, and dominion, and glosses Allah as God of creation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : بسم الله قال : الباء من بهاء الله والسين من سناء الله والميم من ملك الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r3.speaker: أبو الشعثاء جابر بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r3.claim: Jabir ibn Zayd says Allah is the Greatest Name because every Qur'anic sura begins with it before any other name.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r3.anchor: عن أبي الشعثاء جابر بن زيد في قوله : بسم الله قال : اسم الله الاعظم هو الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-Rahman as the Arabic intensive form of mercy and says it is an Arabic expression.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : اول ما انزل جبريل على محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال له جبريل قل يا محمد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r5.claim: The Prophet calls the basmala one of God's names and compares its nearness to Allah's name with the closeness of the eye's black and white.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r5.anchor: عن طاووس ، عن ابن عباس ان عثمان بن عفان سال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فقال : هو اسم من اسماء الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-Rahim as gentle and caring toward those God wills to show mercy, and severe toward those He wills to chastise.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p25/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : اول ما نزل جبريل على النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له جبريل : قل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p26/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p26/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p26/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says al-Rahman is a name people cannot appropriate for themselves; it belongs to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p26/r1.anchor: عن الحسن ، قال : الرحمن اسم لا يستطيع الناس ان ينتحلوه ، تسمى به تبارك وتعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r1.claim: Agreement that everything between the covers is Qur'an establishes that the basmala is Qur'an, which is undisputed, but does not establish that it must be recited at each written location.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r1.anchor: فالجواب أنه لا يقتضي إلا أن البسملة قرآن وهذا لانزاع فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r2.claim: Whether the basmala at a given sura opening must be recited depends instead on transmitted recitation and sound Sunna reports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r2.anchor: فذلك أمر يتبع رواية القراء وأخبار السنة الصحيحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r3.speaker: عبد الحكيم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r3.claim: Abd al-Hakim treats sura names and Meccan or Medinan labels in the codex as later additions, assuming the Companions did not write them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r3.anchor: وكونها مكية أو مدنية في المصحف وأن ذلك من صنع المتأخرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r4.claim: If some early authorities wrote those labels, as al-Qastallani and other scholars suggest, later copyists' basmala evidence fails; the claim that labels used different ink is contradicted by old one-color codices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r4.anchor: المشاهد في مصاحف السلف أن حبرها بلون واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r5.speaker: أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r5.claim: A Bukhari report says Anas demonstrated the Prophet's measured reading by stretching the basmala, but Ibn Ashur says the pronouns refer to Anas, who merely used the familiar formula as an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r5.anchor: وإنما جاء بالبسملة على وجه التمثيل لكيفية القراءة لشهرة البسملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r6.speaker: أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r6.claim: A Muslim report from Anas says the Prophet announced a newly revealed sura and recited the basmala before al-Kawthar; Ibn al-Mubarak and a second Shafi'i position cite it for the basmala.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r6.anchor: فقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم { إنا أعطيناك الكوثر } ( الكوثر : 1 ) السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r7.claim: Supporters also argue that the Companions' inclusion of the basmala in codices proves it belongs, since they were so careful not to add non-Qur'anic words that they omitted “Amen.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p142#2/r7.anchor: ولإثبات الصحابة إياها في المصاحف مع حرصهم على أن لا يدخلوا في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r1.claim: The omitted complement of “in the name of God” is, here, “I read”; it is conventionally omitted when beginning a good action and recovered from context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r1.anchor: واعلم أن متعلق المجرور في { بسم الله } محذوف تقديره هنا أقرأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r2.claim: The genitive phrase is an adverbial complement attached to an omitted verb, not a stable predicate; the action being begun identifies the verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r2.anchor: فالمجرور ظرف لغو معمول للفعل المحذوف ومتعلق به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r3.claim: The estimated verb names the particular action being started, rather than a generic “I begin,” because that action supplies the contextual clue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r3.anchor: أن يكون فعلا خاصا من النوع الدال على معنى العمل المشروع فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r4.claim: This differs from the grammarians' debate about estimating a noun or verb after stable adverbials used as predicates or circumstances; a loose adverbial normally attaches to an action verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r4.anchor: ولا يجري في هذا الخلاف الواقع بين النحاة في كون متعلق الظروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r5.claim: A specific action verb extends the blessing of God's name across the action's parts; the omission also makes the formula usable before any action without altering Qur'anic wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r5.anchor: صلوحية البسملة ليبتدىء بها كل شارع في فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r6.claim: This is concise ellipsis, unlike stable adverbial predicates such as “good is with you,” whose complement is not normally made explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p146/r6.anchor: والحذف من قبيل الإيجاز لأنه حذف ما قد يصرح به في الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r1.claim: The word “name” is inserted to mark an action as belonging to monotheists and performed under God's name; God's name can accompany actions, whereas His essence cannot be paired with them in the same way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r1.anchor: لأن المقصود أن يكون الفعل المشروع فيه من شؤون أهل التوحيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r2.claim: The wording is used for ritual slaughter and blessing or aid, as in verses 6:118–119 and “Read in the name of your Lord.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r2.anchor: وكالأفعال التي يقصد بها التيمن والتبرك وحصول المعونة مثل : { اقرأ باسم ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r3.claim: “Glorify in the name of your Lord” means to say “Glory be to God,” while the command “glorify Him” directs praise to God's essence and attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r3.anchor: فقوله تعالى : { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } ( الواقعة : 74 ) أمر بأن يقول سبحان الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r4.claim: When requesting enablement or help, the verb may instead be attached to God's essential name as Creator; the basmala means that the recitation accompanies the blessing of His blessed name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p149/r4.anchor: فمعنى ( بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ) أقرأ قراءة ملابسة لبركة هذا الاسم المبارك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r1.claim: Arabic may use “name” for the named thing itself, as al-Nabigha's verse uses it for foolishness, but this is not the sense of “name” in the basmala.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r2.claim: Arabic may insert “name” redundantly, as Labid's line means “peace be upon you”; Qur'anic “word” and Bashshar's “expression” offer similar usages that should not be confused with the basmala.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r2.anchor: يعني ثم السلام عليكما وليس هذا خاصا بلفظ الاسم بل يجىء فيما يرادفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r3.claim: “Name them” can serve as a challenge to establish that supposed partners exist, using a name metonymically for the named one's existence; Ibn Ashur says this is likewise not the basmala's usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r3.anchor: والأمر للتعجيز أي أثبتوا وجودهم ووضع أسماء لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r4.claim: He conjectures that the Companions lengthened the basmala's letter in al-Naml to mark the opening of Solomon's quoted letter, then retained the form as a marker of new suras or topics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p150/r4.anchor: لما كتبوا المصحف طولوها في سورة النمل للإشارة إلى أنها مبدأ كتاب سليمان

TUSTARI:1:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:1/r1.claim: Sahl assigns the letters of basmala to the majesty, radiance, and glory of God.
TUSTARI:1:1/r1.anchor: الباء بهاء الله عز وجل: والسين سناء الله عز وجل. والميم مجد الله عز وجل.

TUSTARI:1:1/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:1/r2.claim: Allah is the greatest name encompassing all names; its veiled inner reality is accessible only to the purified who live on lawful sustenance through faith.
TUSTARI:1:1/r2.anchor: هو الاسم الأعظم الذي حوى الأسماء كلها، وبين الألف واللام منه حرف مكنى غيب

TUSTARI:1:1/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:1/r3.claim: Al-Rahman has a distinctive connection to the veiled letter between alif and lam.
TUSTARI:1:1/r3.anchor: والرحمن: اسم فيه خاصية من الحرف المكنى بين الألف واللام.

TUSTARI:1:1/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:1:1/r4.claim: Al-Rahim shows mercy through provision in descendants and origin, in accordance with God's prior eternal knowledge.
TUSTARI:1:1/r4.anchor: هو العاطف على عباده بالرزق في الفرع والابتداء في الأصل رحمة لسابق علمه القديم.

TUSTARI:1:1/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
TUSTARI:1:1/r5.claim: Abu Bakr says God creates from the breath of His spirit whatever He wills in His kingdom as mercy because He is merciful.
TUSTARI:1:1/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر: أي بنسيم روح الله اخترع من ملكه ما شاء رحمة لأنه رحيم.

TUSTARI:1:1/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:1:1/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TUSTARI:1:1/r6.claim: Ali says the two tender names differ in tenderness and remove despair from God's believing servants.
TUSTARI:1:1/r6.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: " الرحمن الرحيم " اسمان رقيقان أحدهما أرق من الآخر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.claim: Jaʿfar calls the basmala the crowns of the suras.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.anchor: روي عن جعفر بن محمد الصادق رضي الله عنه أنه قال: «البسملة تيجان السور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.claim: The Prophet told a man to invoke the basmala instead of cursing Satan, because it makes Satan shrink to less than a fly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.anchor: ولكن قل: «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» فإنه يصغر حتى يصير أقل من ذباب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.speaker: علي بن الحسين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.claim: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn explains mentioning God alone in 17:46 as saying the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.anchor: قال علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه في تفسير قوله تعالى: وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.claim: In a report from Jabir, the Prophet instructs him to begin the prayer with the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: «كيف تفتتح الصلاة يا جابر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet prayer and recited the basmala aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أتاني جبريل فعلمني الصلاة فقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يجهر بها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.claim: The Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports would imply that the basmala is a verse of al-Fatiha if sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.anchor: وهذان الحديثان يقتضيان أنها آية من الحمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.claim: The sound report of Ubay ibn Kaʿb undermines counting the basmala as part of al-Fatiha: the Prophet elicited the sura beginning with al-hamdu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.anchor: ويرد ذلك حديث أبي بن كعب الصحيح إذ قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.claim: The sound hadith describing prayer as divided between God and the servant begins its quoted recitation with praise, not the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.anchor: ويرده الحديث الصحيح بقوله عز وجل: «قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي، يقول العبد الحمد لله رب العالمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.claim: No basmala recitation in prayer is preserved from the Prophet or the first three caliphs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.anchor: ويرده أنه لم يحفظ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولا عن أبي بكر، ولا عن عمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.claim: Seven verses is the agreed count; the six-verse count from Husayn al-Juʿfi and eight-verse count from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd are anomalous, with 15:87 decisive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.anchor: لأن الإجماع أنها سبع آيات، إلا ما روي عن حسين الجعفي أنها ست آيات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r1.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the basmala as a verse of al-Fatiha; many Meccan and Kufan readers do not count “those whom You favored.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r1.anchor: والشافعي- رحمه الله- يعد «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم» آية من الحمد، وكثير من قراء مكة والكوفة لا يعدون أنعمت عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r2.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وجمهور الفقهاء والقراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r2.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa, and most jurists and readers do not count the basmala as a verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r2.anchor: ومالك- رحمه الله-، وأبو حنيفة، وجمهور الفقهاء، والقراء، لا يعدون البسملة آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r3.claim: The Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports can be reconciled as instructional recitations rather than proof that the basmala belongs to the sura.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r3.anchor: رأى قراءة جابر وحكايته أمر الصلاة قراءة في غير صلاة على جهة التعلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r4.claim: The Prophet omitted the basmala when teaching Ubay because he was identifying the sura's contents, whereas that aim was absent in the other two reports.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r4.anchor: فلم يدخل معها ما ليس منها، وليس هذا القصد في حديث جابر وأبي هريرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r5.speaker: ابن المبارك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak says the basmala is a verse in every sura; the author calls this anomalous and rejected.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r5.anchor: وقال ابن المبارك: «إن البسملة آية في كل سورة» ، وهذا قول شاذ رد الناس عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r6.speaker: الشعبي والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and al-Aʿmash report a history of the basmala's written form: from “in Your name, O God” to “in the name of God,” then “the Merciful,” and finally its complete wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r6.anchor: وروى الشعبي والأعمش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكتب «باسمك اللهم» ، حتى أمر أن يكتب «بسم الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r7.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r7.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil reports that Gabriel first came to the Prophet and told him to say the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r7.anchor: وروى عمرو بن شرحبيل: أن جبريل أول ما جاء النبي عليه السلام قال له: قل: «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the first words Gabriel brought were the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r8.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أن أول ما نزل به جبريل: «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r9.claim: A report in some versions of Khadija's account also has Gabriel tell the Prophet to say the basmala before commanding him to recite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r9.anchor: وفي بعض طرق حديث خديجة وحملها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ورقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r10.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r10.claim: Some connect the basmala's nineteen letters with the nineteen guardians of Hell, assigning one angel to each letter as a source of their strength.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61/r10.anchor: إنما ترتب عددهم على حروف بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، لكل حرف ملك، وهم يقولون في كل أفعالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r1.claim: Letter-count correspondences are entertaining but not solid scholarship, like assigning Laylat al-Qadr to the twenty-seventh night by counting words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r1.anchor: وهذه من ملح التفسير، وليست من متين العلم، وهي نظير قولهم في ليلة القدر: «إنها ليلة سبع وعشرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r2.claim: The claim that angels competed to write the praise because its words total thirty-some letters is another numerological analogy, not firm exegesis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r2.anchor: ونظير قولهم في عدد الملائكة الذين ابتدروا قول القائل: «ربنا ولك الحمد حمدا كثيرا طيبا مباركا فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r3.speaker: نحاة البصرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r3.claim: Basran grammarians attach the preposition to an implied noun, approximately “an established beginning,” placing the phrase in the nominative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r3.anchor: والباء في: بسم الله متعلقة عند نحاة البصرة باسم تقديره ابتداء مستقر أو ثابت بسم الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r4.speaker: نحاة الكوفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r4.claim: Kufan grammarians attach the preposition to an implied verb, “I begin,” and place the phrase in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r4.anchor: وعند نحاة الكوفة بفعل تقديره ابتدأت بسم الله، فبسم الله في موضع رفع على مذهب البصريين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r5.claim: The author reads Sibawayh as attaching the preposition to a noun, with the phrase accusative through attachment to an implied “established” or “fixed.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر من مذهب سيبويه أن الباء متعلقة باسم كما تقدم، وبسم الله في موضع نصب تعلقا بثابت أو مستقر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r6.claim: The kasra on the preposition suits its grammatical government, or distinguishes it because it attaches only to nouns, or separates it from homographic nominal particles.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r6.anchor: وكسرت باء الجر ليناسب لفظها عملها، أو لكونها لا تدخل إلا على الأسماء فخصت بالخفض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r7.claim: The poet al-Aʿsha's line illustrates a particle such as kāf that can itself be a noun, explaining the proposed distinction for the kasra.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r8.claim: The written alif is dropped from “in the name of God” as a shortening made possible by frequent use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r8.anchor: وحذفت الألف من بسم الله في الخط اختصارا وتخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r9.speaker: الكسائي وسعيد الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r9.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and Saʿid al-Akhfash say to omit the alif when writing “in the name of the Merciful” and “in the name of the Omnipotent.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r10.speaker: يحيى بن زياد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Ziyad says the alif is omitted only with “the name of God,” where usage is especially frequent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r10.anchor: وقال يحيى بن زياد: «لا تحذف إلا مع بسم الله فقط، لأن الاستعمال إنما كثر فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r11.claim: Outside the name of God, there is no disagreement that the alif remains written.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r11.anchor: فأما في غير اسم الله تعالى فلا خلاف في ثبوت الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r12.claim: Basran etymology derives ism from sumu, “elevation”; the alternative vowels follow whether one derives from yasmū or yasmī, with the wāw omitted in the form cited.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p61#2/r12.anchor: واسم أصله سمو بكسر السين أو سمو بضمها، وهو عند البصريين مشتق من السمو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r1.claim: The diminutive samiyy and plurals asmāʾ and asāmī support the proposed original form of ism.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r1.anchor: وإنما استدل على هذا الأصل الذي ذكرناه بقولهم في التصغير سمي، وفي الجمع أسماء، وفي جمع الجمع أسامي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r2.claim: Kufans derive ism from wasm, “mark,” because a name marks its bearer, but this would predict forms that the attested diminutive and plurals contradict.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r2.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: أصل اسم وسم من السمة، وهي العلامة. لأن الاسم علامة لمن وضع له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r3.claim: The Kufan derivation has a good semantic fit, but its predicted forms fail because diminutives and plurals restore words to their roots.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r3.anchor: والتصغير والجمع المذكوران يردان هذا المذهب الكوفي. وأما المعنى فيه فجيد لولا ما يلزمهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says this is not the place for debating whether a name and its named referent are identical, criticizing theologians who pursue such questions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري رحمه الله: إنه ليس بموضع للمسألة، وأنحى في خطبته على المتكلمين في هذه المسألة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r5.claim: A name such as Zayd can refer either to its bearer or to the name as a word; in the first use name and named are identical in reference, in the second they are distinct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r5.anchor: قد يرد في الكلام ويراد به الذات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r6.claim: Arab usage can make ism itself mean the essence; this reading underlies interpretations of several verses and the hadith of God's ninety-nine names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r6.anchor: وأما اسم الذي هو ألف وسين وميم، فقد يجري في لغة العرب مجرى الذات. يقال: ذات، ونفس، واسم، وعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r7.claim: Malik reportedly answered that the name is neither the named referent nor other than it in every possible context, matching the author's contextual distinction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r7.anchor: ومر بي أن مالكا رحمه الله سئل عن الاسم أهو المسمى؟ فقال: «ليس به ولا هو غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r8.claim: The written name Allah is the most striking and most frequently used of God's names, usually preceding the others, which tend to function as attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p62/r8.anchor: والمكتوبة التي لفظها الله أبهر أسماء الله تعالى وأكثرها استعمالا، وهو المتقدم لسائرها في الأغلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r1.speaker: فرقة من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r1.claim: One group holds that Allah is an un-derived name specially coined for God, with the article integral to its form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r1.anchor: هو اسم مرتجل، لا اشتقاق له من فعل، وإنما هو اسم موضوع له تبارك وتعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r2.speaker: كثير من أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r2.claim: Many scholars derive Allah from alaha, “worship,” and taʾallaha, “worship devotedly”; the author adduces a poetic use and a reading of 7:127 glossed by Ibn ʿAbbas as worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r2.anchor: وذهب كثير من أهل العلم إلى أنه مشتق من أله الرجل إذا عبد، وتأله إذا تنسك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r3.claim: Several analyses explain the development from ilah to Allah through deletion or movement of the hamza and attachment of the article; the author judges the first explanation strongest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r3.anchor: واختلف كيف تعلل إله حتى جاء الله، فقيل: حذفت الهمزة حذفا على غير قياس ودخلت الألف واللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r4.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r4.claim: Al-Khalil reports that ilah/walah began with wāw, with hamza substituted as in ishaḥ/wishaḥ and isādah/wisādah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r4.anchor: وروي عن الخليل أن أصل إله ولاه وأن الهمزة مبدلة من واو كما هي في إشاح ووشاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r5.claim: Another explanation derives walah from bewilderment: minds are bewildered by the realities of God's attributes and by thought about knowing him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r5.anchor: إلا أنها مأخوذة من وله الرجل إذا تحير، لأنه- تعالى- تتحير الألباب في حقائق صفاته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r6.claim: Explanations for omitting the final alif in Allah include avoiding confusion with al-Lat, lightening, or dialect; a verse by Ibn al-Aʿrabi illustrates the form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r6.anchor: وحذفت الألف الأخيرة من «الله» لئلا يشكل بخط اللات، وقيل طرحت تخفيفا، وقيل هي لغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r7.claim: Rahman marks mercy at its utmost limit, is used only of God, and is more emphatic than rahim, which is more emphatic than rāḥim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r7.anchor: والرحمن صفة مبالغة من الرحمة، ومعناها أنه انتهى إلى غاية الرحمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r8.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r8.claim: Some say Rahman and Rahim have one meaning, like nadmān and nadīm, with one form more emphatic than the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63/r8.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: «الرحمن الرحيم» بمعنى واحد، كالندمان والنديم، وزعم أنهما من فعل واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.speaker: العرزمي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.claim: Al-ʿArzamī distinguishes Rahman as merciful to all creation through rain, senses, and universal favors, and Rahim as merciful to believers through guidance and kindness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.anchor: معناه: الرحمن بجميع خلقه في الأمطار، ونعم الحواس، والنعم العامة، الرحيم بالمؤمنين في الهداية لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and Ibn Masʿud report the Prophet's distinction: Rahman is merciful in this world and the next, while Rahim is merciful in the next.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.anchor:
أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
«الرحمن رحمن الدنيا والآخرة، والرحيم رحيم الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi says Rahman covers all kinds of mercy and is unique to God, while Rahim concerns believers, as in 33:43; the author says these views reinforce one another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.anchor: الرحمن اسم عام في جميع أنواع الرحمة يختص به الله تعالى، والرحيم إنما هو في جهة المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.claim: ʿAta al-Khurasani claims Rahman was paired with Rahim after Musaylima adopted the name Rahman, making the pairing exclusive to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.anchor: كان الرحمن فلما اختزل وسمي به مسيلمة الكذاب قال الله- سبحانه- لنفسه: «الرحمن الرحيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.claim: The author rejects ʿAta's chronology because the basmala predates Musaylima's rise and his naming was not firmly established.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.anchor: وهذا قول ضعيف، لأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم كان قبل أن ينجم أمر مسيلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.claim: Some say Arabs did not know the word Rahman, citing their question about the one to whom they were commanded to prostrate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: إن العرب كانت لا تعرف لفظة الرحمن، ولا كانت في لغتها، واستدلوا على ذلك بقول العرب: «وما الرحمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.claim: The author says the Arabs' question showed ignorance of which deity was intended, not ignorance of the word Rahman itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.anchor: وإنما وقفت العرب على تعيين الإله الذي أمروا بالسجود له، لا على نفس اللفظة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وموسى بن جعفر عن أبيه وعلي بن الحسين وقتادة وأبو العالية ومحمد بن يحيى بن حبان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.claim: These authorities say the sura was revealed in Mecca; its linkage with Meccan al-Hijr and the identification of the seven oft-repeated verses support that view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس، وموسى بن جعفر عن أبيه، وعلي بن الحسين، وقتادة، وأبو العالية، ومحمد بن يحيى بن حبان: إنها مكية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r12.claim: The author adds that prayer was prescribed in Mecca and no prayer in Islam is known to have been performed without al-hamdu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p63#2/r12.anchor: ولا خلاف أن فرض الصلاة كان بمكة، وما حفظ أنها كانت قط في الإسلام صلاة بغير الحمد لله رب العالمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r1.speaker: عطاء بن يسار وسوادة بن زياد والزهري وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r1.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar, Sawada ibn Ziyad, al-Zuhri, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say al-Fatiha was revealed in Medina.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r1.anchor: وروي عن عطاء بن يسار، وسوادة بن زياد، والزهري محمد بن مسلم، وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير أن سورة الحمد مدنية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r2.claim: The sura is uncontroversially called the Opening of the Book because of its position at the start.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r2.anchor: وأما أسماؤها فلا خلاف أنها يقال لها فاتحة الكتاب، لأن موضعها يعطي ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r3.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r3.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan dislikes calling it the Mother of the Book, reserving that designation for the decisive verses that contain lawful and unlawful rulings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r3.anchor: فكره الحسن بن أبي الحسن ذلك وقال: «أم الكتاب والحلال والحرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others do call al-Fatiha the Mother of the Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: «يقال لها أم الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r5.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r5.claim: Al-Bukhari explains “Mother of the Book” by its being written first in the codex and recited first in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r5.anchor: وقال البخاري: سميت أم الكتاب لأنها يبدأ بكتابتها في المصحف وبقراءتها في الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r6.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin dislikes the title Mother of the Qur'an, while most scholars allow it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r6.anchor: واختلف هل يقال لها أم القرآن؟ فكره ذلك ابن سيرين وجوزه جمهور العلماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r7.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar gives geographic analogies for “mother” and says al-hamdu is the Mother of the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r7.anchor: قال يحيى بن يعمر: «أم القرى مكة، وأم خراسان مرو، وأم القرآن سورة الحمد» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r8.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r8.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan also calls the sura the Mother of the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: اسمها أم القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r9.claim: The name al-Mathani is explained either by its repetition in every prayer cycle or because this sura was reserved as a treasure for this community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r9.anchor: وأما المثاني فقيل سميت بذلك لأنها تثنى في كل ركعة وقيل سميت بذلك لأنها استثنيت لهذه الأمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r10.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r10.claim: The Prophet says no equivalent to al-Fatiha was revealed in the Torah, Gospel, or Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r10.anchor: إنها لم ينزل في التوراة ولا في الإنجيل ولا في الفرقان مثلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r11.claim: A report says al-Fatiha equals two-thirds of the Qur'an; this may reflect its meanings or an unreasoned divine preference, like the reported merit of al-Ikhlas and al-Zalzala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p65/r11.anchor: ويروى أنها تعدل ثلثي القرآن، وهذا العدل إما أن يكون في المعاني، وإما أن يكون تفضيلا من الله تعالى

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r1.claim: In the basmala, ism is an added connective that shifts the phrase from the force of an oath to seeking blessing; the underlying wording is billāh.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r1.anchor: صلة زائدة، زيدت ليخرج بذكرها من حكم القسم الى قصد التبرك

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r2.claim: The alif is omitted in writing bism because the phrase is frequent and the prefixed bāʾ already supplies the linkage; it remains in bismi al-Raḥmān and similar phrases.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r2.anchor: من الخط تخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال واستغناء عنها بباء الالصاق في اللفظ

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r3.claim: The initial alif in ism is hamzat waṣl: the form sumayy shows that it is not pronounced and is dropped.

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r4.claim: Hamzat waṣl is supplied to let speech begin despite an initial sukūn, then becomes unnecessary when the word is joined to what precedes it.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r4.anchor: وانما زيدت لسكون الحرف الذي بعدها لما ارادوا استئنافه فلم يصلوا الى الابتداء بساكن

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r1.claim: The surah is called al-Fatiha because it opens the written Book and begins recitation in prayer.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r2.claim: The majority call it Umm al-Kitab; Anas is cited for this name.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r2.anchor: ويقال لها أيضا : أم الكتاب عند الجمهور ، ذكره أنس

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r3.claim: Hasan and Ibn Sirin dislike the name Umm al-Kitab, taking it to refer to the Preserved Tablet; Hasan also calls the clear verses Umm al-Kitab.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r3.anchor: والحسن وابن سيرين كرها تسميتها بذلك ، قال الحسن وابن سيرين : إنما ذلك اللوح المحفوظ

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r4.claim: Hasan also objects to calling the surah Umm al-Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن : الآيات المحكمات : هن أم الكتاب

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r5.claim: In a hadith graded sound by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet calls it Umm al-Qur'an, Umm al-Kitab, the seven oft-repeated, and the great Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «الحمد لله أم القرآن وأم الكتاب والسبع المثاني والقرآن العظيم

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r6.claim: Al-Hamd is another name for the surah.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r7.claim: It is also called al-Salah because the divine hadith names recitation of al-Hamd as the servant's praise, and the surah is a condition of prayer.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r7.anchor: فسميت الفاتحة : صلاة ؛ لأنها شرط فيها

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r8.claim: A report from Abu Saʿid calls the Fatiha a healing from every poison.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r8.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب شفاء من كل سم

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r9.claim: The surah is called a ruqya because the Prophet affirmed its use in healing a stung man and asked how the companion knew it was a ruqya.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r9.anchor: فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «وما يدريك أنها رقية

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas calls the surah the foundation of the Qur'an and says its foundation is the basmala.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سماها : أساس القرآن

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r11.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r11.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna calls the surah al-Waqiya, the protecting one.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r12.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r12.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir calls it al-Kafiya: it suffices in place of other surahs, while none can replace it; this is also stated in a mursal report.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r12.anchor: وسماها يحيى بن أبي كثير : الكافية ؛ لأنها تكفي عما عداها ولا يكفي ما سواها عنها

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also records the names Surat al-Salah and al-Kanz.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r13.anchor: ويقال لها : سورة الصلاة والكنز ذكرهما الزمخشري

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, and Abu al-ʿAliya hold that the surah was revealed in Mecca.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار والزهري
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r15.claim: Abu Hurayra, Mujahid, ʿAta ibn Yasar, and al-Zuhri hold that the surah was revealed in Medina.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r15.anchor: أبو هريرة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار والزهري

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r16.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r16.claim: A third report says it was revealed twice, but Ibn Kathir prefers the Meccan account, connecting it with the seven oft-repeated in 15:87.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r17.speaker: أبو الليث السمرقندي
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r17.claim: Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi says half the surah was revealed in Mecca and half in Medina; Ibn Kathir calls this very strange, as transmitted by al-Qurtubi.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r17.anchor: وحكى أبو الليث السمرقندي أن نصفها نزل بمكة ونصفها الآخر نزل بالمدينة ، وهو غريب جدًا

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r18.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r18.claim: There is no disagreement that the surah has seven verses; reports of eight from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and six from Husayn al-Juʿfi are aberrant.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r19.claim: Scholars differ over whether the basmala is an independent opening verse, part of a verse, or not counted as part of the Fatiha.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r19.anchor: هل هي آية مستقلة من أولها

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r20.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r20.claim: The surah has twenty-five words and one hundred thirteen letters.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r20.anchor: كلماتها خمس وعشرون كلمة ، وحروفها مائة وثلاثة عشر حرفًا

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r21.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r21.claim: Al-Bukhari explains Umm al-Kutub by its being written first in Qur'anic codices and recited first in prayer.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r21.anchor: وسميت أم الكتب ، أنه يبدأ بكتابتها في المصاحف ، ويبدأ بقراءتها في الصلاة

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r22.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r22.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r22.claim: Another explanation of Umm al-Kitab is that the meanings of the whole Qur'an return to what the Fatiha contains.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r22.anchor: سميت بذلك لرجوع معاني القرآن كله

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r23.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r23.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r23.claim: Ibn Jarir says Arabs call a comprehensive or leading thing with dependent parts an umm, such as the head's covering or an army's banner.

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r24.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r24.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r24.claim: Ibn Jarir cites Dhu al-Rumma's verse calling a spear an umm, a focal point followed in affairs.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r24.anchor: على رأسه أم لنا نقتدي به

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r25.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r25.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r25.claim: Mecca is called Umm al-Qura because it precedes and gathers the other settlements, or because the earth was spread from it.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r25.anchor: وسميت مكة : أم القرى لتقدمها أمام جميعها وجمعها ما سواها ، وقيل : لأن الأرض دحيت منها

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r26.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r26.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r26.claim: The Fatiha opens recitation and was placed first when the Companions wrote the master codex.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r26.anchor: ويقال لها أيضًا : الفاتحة ؛ لأنها تفتتح بها القراءة ، وافتتحت الصحابة بها كتابة المصحف الإمام

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r27.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r27.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r27.claim: The title al-Sabʿ al-Mathani is explained by its repetition in every prayer unit, though Ibn Kathir notes another meaning will follow.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r27.anchor: قالوا : لأنها تثنى في الصلاة ، فتقرأ في كل ركعة ، وإن كان للمثاني معنى آخر

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r28.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r28.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r28.claim: Reports from Abu Hurayra identify Umm al-Qur'an as the Fatiha and the seven oft-repeated; al-Daraqutni says its transmitters are trustworthy.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r28.anchor: هي أم القرآن ، وهي فاتحة الكتاب ، وهي السبع المثاني

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r29.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r29.speaker: علي وابن عباس وأبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r29.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports that ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Abu Hurayra interpret the seven oft-repeated in 15:87 as the Fatiha, with the basmala its seventh verse.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r29.anchor: وروى البيهقي عن علي{[31]} وابن عباس{[32]} وأبي هريرة{[33]} أنهم

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r30.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r30.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r30.claim: Ibn Masʿud explains that he omitted the Fatiha from his codex because he would have written it at the start of every surah where it is recited in prayer; Muslims' memorization sufficed.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r30.anchor: لو كتبتها لكتبتها في أول كل سورة

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r31.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r31.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r31.claim: One view makes the Fatiha the first revelation, based on a report in al-Bayhaqi and listed by al-Baqillani among three views.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r31.anchor: وقد قيل : إن الفاتحة أول شيء نزل من القرآن ، كما ورد في حديث رواه البيهقي

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r32.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r32.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r32.claim: A second view makes “O you wrapped up” the first revelation, based on Jabir's sound hadith.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r32.anchor: وقيل : { يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ } كما في حديث جابر في الصحيح

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r33.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r33.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r33.claim: Ibn Kathir says the correct view is that “Read in the name of your Lord” was first revealed.
IBNKATHIR:1:1/r33.anchor: وقيل : { اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ } [ العلق : 1 ] وهذا هو الصحيح

IBNKATHIR:1:1/r34.author: Ibn Kathīr
