RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r7.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r7.claim: They argue an eternally receptive essence would have to be capable of receiving originated events in eternity, which they deem impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r7.anchor: ذاته لو كانت قابلة للحوادث لكانت قابلية تلك الحوادث من لوازم ذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r8.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r8.claim: If attributes originated, God existed as God before they appeared, showing that they are unnecessary for divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r8.anchor: الإله الموصوف بصفات الإلهية كان موجودا قبل حدوث هذه الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r9.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r9.claim: They argue attributes are either dispensable additions or necessities that make God dependent on something else.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r9.anchor: إن كان الأول كان وجودها فضلا زائدا فوجب نفيها وإن كان الثاني كان الإله مفتقرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r10.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r10.claim: They argue a self-complete essence needs no attributes, while an incomplete essence perfected by another cannot be divine.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r10.anchor: ذاته تعالى إما أن تكون كاملة في جميع الصفات المعتبرة في المدائح والكمالات

RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r11.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r11.claim: They say a God composed of essence and attributes would be divided and composite, hence possible rather than necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r11.anchor: لما كان الإله هو مجموع الذات والصفات فحينئذ يكون الإله مجزأ مبعضا منقسما

RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r12.speaker: المعتزلة والفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r12.claim: They infer from God's condemnation of Christian trinitarianism that affirming attributes is unbelief, since Christians combine one essence with attributes rather than affirming three gods.
RAZI-FULL:v1p112/r12.anchor: أن الله تعالى كفر النصارى في التثليث فلا يخلو إما أن يكون لأنهم قالوا بإثبات ذوات ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r1.claim: God must be knowing, powerful, and living; the necessary conceptual distinction between God's essence and His being knowing or powerful shows these are not identical.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r1.anchor: ثبت أن إله العالم يجب أن يكون عالما قادرا حيا فنقول يمتنع أن يكون علمه وقدرته نفس تلك الذات

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r2.claim: We can conceive God as existent while not attending to His power or knowledge, and conceive power without knowledge, showing distinct concepts.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r2.anchor: يمكن العلم بكونه موجودا مع الذهول عن كونه قادرا وعالما

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r3.claim: Knowledge concerns necessary, impossible, and possible things, while power concerns only possible things, proving their difference.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r3.anchor: كونه عالما عام التعلق بالنسبة إلى الواجب والممتنع والممكن وكونه قادرا ليس عام التعلق

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r4.claim: Power brings the possible into existence but knowledge does not, so the two attributes differ.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r4.anchor: كونه تعالى قادرا يؤثر في وجود المقدور وكونه عالما لا يؤثر

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r5.claim: Not existent contradicts existent, whereas not knowing does not; what is negated by existence and knowledge claims is therefore distinct, likewise for power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r5.anchor: قولنا : موجود يناقضه قولنا : ليس بموجود ولا يناقضه قولنا : ليس بعالم

RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r6.claim: These arguments establish that God has attributes, but they might be relational: power is capacity to produce, and knowledge is awareness, each grounded in the divine essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p113/r6.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن تكون هذه الصفات صفات نسبية وإضافية فالمعنى من كونه قادرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r1.claim: Knowledge and power are real attributes whose relations to known things and possible effects are concomitant; life alone is a real divine attribute without relation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r1.anchor: أما الصفة الحقيقية العارية عن النسبة والإضافة في حق الله تعالى فليست إلا صفة الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r2.claim: Philosophers define living as perceiving and acting, but both are relational, so life on their account is not distinct from knowledge and power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r2.anchor: قالت الفلاسفة : الحي هو الدراك الفعال ؛

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r3.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r3.claim: Theologians define life as an attribute that makes knowing and having power possible; they argue differing capacities among essences require an additional life attribute.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r3.anchor: قال المتكلمون إنها صفة باعتبارها يصح أن يكون عالما قادرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r4.claim: Razi rejects that proof: God's essence is distinct from other essences in itself, and differences in receptivity would require another attribute without end.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r4.anchor: قد دللنا على أن ذات الله تعالى مخالفة لسائر الذوات لذاته المخصوصة فسقط هذا الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r5.claim: A third group defines living as not being unable to know and have power; Razi accepts that this negates a negation, but asks why the resulting positive cannot be the essence itself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r5.anchor: معنى كونه حيا أنه لا يمتنع أن يقدر ويعلم فهذا عبارة عن نفي الامتناع

RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r6.claim: The argument that one can conceive God's essence while doubting that He is living fails because the divine essence is known only indirectly, not in itself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114/r6.anchor: لا نعقل ذات الله تعالى تعقلا ذاتيا وإنما نتعقل تلك الذات تعقلا عرضيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.claim: The Quran calls God the Living and Sustainer; these names combine to provide the full praise.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.anchor: لفظ الحي وارد في القرآن قال الله تبارك وتعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.claim: Hayy alone, meaning perceiving and acting or able to know and act, seems insufficiently praiseworthy; the praise lies in its combination with qayyum.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.anchor: الحي معناه الدراك الفعال أو الذي لا يمتنع أن يعلم ويقدر وهذا القدر ليس فيه مدح عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.claim: Qayyum means sustaining and setting right everything else, which requires complete knowledge and power; thus Hayy qayyum means knowing every possible and acting on every originated thing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.anchor: القيوم هو القائم بإصلاح حال كل ما سواه وذلك لا يتم إلا بالعلم التام والقدرة التامة

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r1.speaker: المعتزلة والأشعرية
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r1.claim: Mu'tazilites and Ash'arites say God's act of bringing something into being is identical with the thing brought into being.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r1.anchor: قالت المعتزلة والأشعرية : التكوين نفس المكون

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r2.claim: Those who deny a separate attribute of bringing into being argue that if it acts contingently it is simply power, while necessary effect would make God act by nature rather than choice.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r2.anchor: الصفة المسماة بالتكوين إما أن تؤثر على سبيل الصحة أو على سبيل الوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r3.claim: They argue an eternal creating attribute entails eternal effects, while a created one needs another act of creation and an infinite regress.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r3.anchor: إن كانت قديمة لزم من قدمها الآثار وإن كانت محدثة افتقر تكوينها إلى تكوين آخر

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r4.claim: They say power alone either suffices to produce effects once knowledge and will are present, making another attribute needless, or lacks efficacy and is not power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r4.anchor: إن كان الأول فحينئذ تكون القدرة كافية في خروج الأثر من العدم إلى الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r5.claim: Proponents of an eternal creating attribute point out that an able agent may act or refrain; God's ability to make a thousand suns does not mean He did so.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r5.anchor: القادر على الفعل قد يوجده وقد لا يوجده ألا ترى أن الله تعالى قادر على خلق ألف شمس

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r6.claim: Being an agent who produces cannot mean merely that the effect exists, or explaining an effect by saying God produced it would explain it by itself; therefore producing differs from both power and effect.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r6.anchor: فثبت أن تعليل الموجدية بوجود الأثر كلام باطل فوجب أن يكون كون الموجد موجدا أمرا مغايرا

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r7.claim: Those identifying creation with its effect interpret Creator, Provider, Giver of life, and Giver of death as specific relations of God's power to outcomes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r7.anchor: معنى كونه تعالى خالقا رازقا محييا مميتا ضارا نافعا عبارة عن نسبة مخصوصة

RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r8.claim: Those distinguishing the creative act from its effect say being Creator is a real attribute qualified by a relation, not a relation alone.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115/r8.anchor: ليس عبارة عن الصفة الإضافية فقط بل هو عبارة عن صفة حقيقية موصوفة بصفة إضافية

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r1.claim: One class of relational names describes God as known, remembered, praised, and glorified; infinitely many such relations yield infinitely many possible names.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r1.anchor: كونه معلوما مذكورا مسبحا ممجدا فيقال : يا أيها المسبح بكل لسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r2.claim: If bringing things into being is not an additional attribute, acting is a purely relational attribute; names can describe creating in general or creating a specific kind for a wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r2.anchor: كونه تعالى فاعلا للأفعال صفة إضافية محضة بناء على أن تكوين الأشياء ليس بصفة زائدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r3.claim: Mujid means an agent affecting existence; muhdith more narrowly brings something into existence after nonexistence; mukawwin nearly means mujid.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r3.anchor: الموجد والمحدث والمكون والمنشئ والمبدع والمخترع والصانع والخالق والفاطر والبارئ

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r4.claim: Munshi derives from growth and denotes gradual production, while mubdi denotes bringing something forth all at once; they are two kinds of general creation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r4.anchor: المنشئ فاشتقاقه من النشوء والنماء وهو الذي يكون قليلا قليلا على التدريج

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r5.claim: Mukhtari is close to mubdi, while sani suggests effortful making.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r5.anchor: والمخترع قريب من المبدع وأما الصانع فيقرب أن يكون اسما لمن يأتي بالفعل على سبيل التكلف

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r6.claim: Khaliq means measuring or determining, which in God returns to knowledge; fatir derives from splitting and appears to mean originating at once.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r6.anchor: الخالق فهو عبارة عن التقدير وهو في حق الله تعالى يرجع إلى العلم وأما الفاطر فاشتقاقه من الفطر

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r7.claim: Bari means bringing into being in a way suited to benefit, like shaping a pen to suit its purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r7.anchor: البارئ فهو الذي يحدثه على الوجه الموافق للمصلحة يقال : برى القلم إذا أصلحه

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r8.claim: Creating benefit or pain yields the names Benefiter or Harmful; creating life or death yields Giver of life or Giver of death.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r8.anchor: إذا خلق النافع سمي نافعا وإذا خلق المؤلم سمي ضارا

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r9.claim: Granting honor yields Kind and Gentle, while imposing subjugation yields Overpowering and Compeller.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r9.anchor: إذا خصهم بالإكرام سمي برا لطيفا وإذا خصهم بالقهر سمي قهارا جبارا

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r10.claim: Giving little or much yields Withholder or Expander; punishing sins yields Avenger, while foregoing punishment yields Pardoner, Forgiver, Merciful, or Compassionate.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r10.anchor: إذا قلل العطاء سمي قابضا وإذا أكثره سمي باسطا

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r11.claim: Withholding or granting wealth yields Withholder and Expander, while lowering or raising status yields Abaser and Exalter.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r11.anchor: إن حصل المنع والإعطاء في الأموال سمي قابضا باسطا وإن حصلا في الجاه والحشمة سمي خافضا رافعا

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r12.claim: Because God's possible creations across kinds and species are limitless, the names derived from creating specific things are limitless too.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r12.anchor: أقسام مقدورات الله تعالى بحسب الأنواع والأجناس غير متناهية فلا جرم يمكن أن يحصل لله تعالى أسماء غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r13.claim: Some oppositions are contraries, such as exalting and humiliating or giving life and death; others are presence and absence, such as withholding versus extending or lowering versus raising.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r13.anchor: مقابل الشيء تارة يكون ضده وتارة يكون عدمه فقولنا : المعز المذل وقولنا المحيي المميت

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r14.claim: Not honoring someone differs from actively humiliating them; the contrast between honor and abasement is a pair of opposites.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r14.anchor: فرق بين أن لا يعزه وبين أن يذله

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r15.claim: Ra'uf and Rahim are close, but Ra'uf leans toward conferring benefit whereas Rahim leans toward removing harm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r15.anchor: الرؤوف الرحيم يقرب من هذا الباب إلا أن الرؤوف أميل إلى جانب إيصال النفع

RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r16.claim: Fatih suggests creating the means of good; Wahib suggests conveying that good; Nafi suggests conveying benefit with the recipient's benefit in view.
RAZI-FULL:v1p115#2/r16.anchor: الفاتح يشعر بإحداث سبب الخير والواهب يشعر بإيصال ذلك الخير إليه والنافع يشعر بإيصال ذلك النفع

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r1.claim: Quranic negations concern God's essence, attributes, or actions; negating every unlike essence or attribute yields an unlimited number of negative descriptions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r1.anchor: ذلك السلب إما أن يكون عائدا إلى الذات أو إلى الصفات أو إلى الأفعال

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r2.claim: God is not a substance, body, in a place or space, or an indwelling subject or substrate; He is unlike other essences by His own specific essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r2.anchor: ليس جوهرا ولا جسما ولا في المكان ولا في الحيز ولا حالا ولا محلا

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r3.claim: God's self-sufficiency means He needs nothing in His essence or real and negative attributes; the Lord is rich, possessed of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r3.anchor: كونه غنيا أنه لا يحتاج في ذاته ولا في صفاته الحقيقية ولا في صفاته السلبية إلى شيء غيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r4.claim: God neither begets nor is begotten.

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r5.claim: Defects to be negated fall under the opposites of knowledge, power, self-sufficiency, and unity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r5.anchor: كل صفة تكون من صفات النقائص فإنه يجب تنزيه الله تعالى عنها

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r6.claim: God neither sleeps nor forgets nor is ignorant, and knowledge of one thing never distracts Him from another.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r6.anchor: رابعها أن علمه ببعض المعلومات لا يمنعه عن العلم بغيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r7.claim: God's acts involve no fatigue, tools, material, or duration, and creating much or little takes no more time than an instant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r7.anchor: أحدها : أنه منزه في أفعاله عن التعب والنصب

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r8.claim: God's power does not end and He is not impoverished, contrary to the claim that God is poor and humans rich.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r8.anchor: رابعها نفي انتهاء القدرة وحصول الفقر

RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r9.claim: The discussion also includes negating partners, opposites, and peers under divine unity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117/r9.anchor: ومنها ما يكون من باب أضداد الوحدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.claim: God feeds but is not fed and protects others while none can overrule Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.anchor: ^ { وهو يطعم ولا يطعم } ^ [ الأنعام : 14 ] ^ { وهو يجير ولا يجار عليه } ^

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.claim: Among negations of divine acts: God creates neither falsehood nor play nor purposelessness, but creates in truth.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه لا يخلق الباطل قال تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.claim: God is not pleased with unbelief, does not will injustice, and does not love corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.anchor: ورابعها أنه لا يرضى بالكفر قال تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.claim: He does not punish without prior wrongdoing; believers' gratitude and faith leave no need for punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.anchor: وسابعها أنه لا يعاقب من غير سابقة جرم قال تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.claim: People's obedience benefits themselves and their wrongdoing harms themselves; God gains or loses nothing from them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.anchor: أنه لا ينتفع بطاعات المطيعين ولا يتضرر بمعاصي المذنبين

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.claim: No one may question God's actions and judgments; He does whatever He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r6.anchor: وتاسعها : أنه ليس لأحد عليه اعتراض في أفعاله وأحكامه

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r7.claim: God does not break His word or promise and threat.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r7.anchor: وعاشرها : أنه لا يخلف وعده ووعيده قال تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r8.claim: Since negations across God's essence, attributes, and actions are limitless, names arising from this class are limitless too.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r8.anchor: أقسام السلوب بحسب الذات وبحسب الصفات وبحسب الأفعال غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r9.claim: Quddus describes God's essence as unlike deficient natures; Salam describes His freedom from deficient attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r9.anchor: القدوس عبارة عن كون حقيقة ذاته مخالفة للماهيات التي هي نقائص

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r10.claim: Aziz means God has no equal; Ghaffar removes punishment from sinners; Halim does not hasten punishment and still grants mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r10.anchor: العزيز وهو الذي لا يوجد له نظير وثالثها الغفار وهو الذي يسقط العقاب عن المذنبين

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r11.claim: Wahid means none shares God's unique essence or rivals Him in ordering the world and the affairs of the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r11.anchor: الواحد ومعناه أنه لا يشاركه أحد في حقيقته المخصوصة ولا يشاركه أحد في نظم العالم

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r12.claim: Ghani means free of needs and necessities.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r12.anchor: الغني : ومعناه كونه منزها عن الحاجات والضرورات

RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r13.claim: Sabur does not punish an offender despite power to do so; Halim does likewise while continuing to bestow blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p117#2/r13.anchor: الصبور هو الذي لا يعاقب المسيء مع القدرة عليه والحليم هو الذي يكون كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r1.claim: The Quran affirms God's knowledge and uses forms including knower, all-knowing, most knowing, and past and future verbs of knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r1.anchor: إثبات العلم لله تعالى قال تعالى : ^ { ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r2.claim: Although the Quran says God teaches, do not call Him Teacher, because that name suggests deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r2.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقال إن الله معلم مع كثرة هذه الألفاظ ؛ لأن لفظ المعلم مشعر بنوع نقيصة

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r3.claim: Do not call God al-Allama: although intensive, the form suggests that knowledge was gained through effort and strain.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r3.anchor: لا يجوز إطلاق لفظ العلامة على الله تعالى ؛ لأنها وإن أفادت المبالغة لكنها تفيد أن هذه المبالغة

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r4.claim: Khabar and khibra nearly mean knowledge; some define knowledge as report, and the frequent divine name Khabir also indicates knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r4.anchor: لفظ الخبر والخبرة وهو كالمرادف للعلم حتى قال بعضهم في حد العلم : إنه الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r5.claim: Shahid means witness and knower when derived from seeing; if it means testimony, it belongs to speech instead.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r5.anchor: الشهيد في حق الله تعالى إذا فسرناه بكونه مشاهدا لها عالما بها أما إذا فسرناه بالشهادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r6.claim: Hikma can mean knowledge or refraining from what is unsuitable and doing what is suitable.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r6.anchor: الحكمة وهذه اللفظة قد يراد بها العلم وقد يراد بها أيضا ترك ما لا ينبغي وفعل ما ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r7.claim: Latif can mean knowledge of subtle matters or conveying benefits to people through a hidden, wondrous means.
RAZI-FULL:v1p118#2/r7.anchor: اللطيف وقد يراد به العلم بالدقائق وقد يراد به إيصال المنافع إلى العباد بطريق خفية عجيبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Razi groups divine speech under the noun kalām, citing the command to shelter a polytheist until he hears God's speech.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: He also counts past-tense forms of divine speech, citing God's direct address to Moses on two occasions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: قال تعالى ﴿ وكلم الله موسى تكليما

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: He records the future-tense form of speaking, in the statement that God speaks to a human only by revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r4.claim: Razi lists divine saying in past, future, and verbal-noun forms, with Qur'anic examples for each.

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: The future form of saying is illustrated by God's instruction that the cow is such-and-such.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r5.anchor: قال تعالى ﴿ إنه يقول إنها بقرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: Razi includes both qīl and qawl among forms of divine saying, citing God's most truthful speech and His unalterable word.

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r7.claim: He cites command as a divine word, including God's ownership of command and His order to sacrifice a cow.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r7.anchor: لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r8.claim: Promise is another divine word, attested as a binding promise in scripture and as God's promise to begin and restore creation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r8.anchor: وعدا عليه حقا في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r9.claim: Razi includes revelation among divine words, citing revelation to God's servant and revelation as a mode of speaking.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r9.anchor: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r10.claim: He lists God's being grateful to His servants, supported by the promise that their efforts are appreciated and the description “grateful, knowing.”
RAZI-FULL:v1p120/r10.anchor: ﴿ فأولئك كان سعيهم مشكورا ﴾ [ الإسراء : 19 ] ﴿ وكان الله شاكرا عليما

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r1.claim: Razi treats will, pleasure, love, and aversion as divine qualities related to volition, citing Qur'anic examples.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r1.anchor: يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد بكم العسر

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r2.claim: He cites divine approval both of gratitude and of believers, and also God's refusal to approve disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r2.anchor: لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r3.claim: Love is included among these qualities, with verses saying God loves His people and loves the purified.

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r4.speaker: الأشعرية
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r4.claim: The Ashʿarites define aversion as willing that an act not occur.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r4.anchor: قالت الأشعرية : الكراهة عبارة عن يريد أن لا يفعل

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites hold that aversion is a distinct quality besides will.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r5.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : بل هي صفة أخرى سوى الإرادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r6.claim: Razi gives no adjudication between these accounts, ending the report with “God knows best.”
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r6.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : بل هي صفة أخرى سوى الإرادة والله أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r7.claim: He establishes God's hearing and sight through verses that call Him the Hearing, the Seeing, and say He hears and sees.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r7.anchor: ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r8.claim: Other cited verses contrast God with an idol that neither hears nor sees and say that sight cannot encompass Him, though He encompasses sight.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r8.anchor: لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r9.claim: “First” and “last” each combine a relation with a negation: precedence without a predecessor, and persistence without a successor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r9.anchor: فلفظ الأول يفيد حالة متركبة من إضافة وسلب والآخر هو الذي يبقى بعد غيره ولا يبقى بعده غيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r10.claim: The apparent is purely relational, meaning manifest through proofs, while the hidden is purely negative, meaning unknowable in essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r10.anchor: أما لفظ الظاهر فهو إضافة محضة لأن معناه كونه ظاهرا بحسب الدلائل وأما لفظ الباطن فهو سلب محض

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r11.claim: The name al-Qayyūm combines two features: absolute independence from anything else and the dependence of everything else on Him as its source.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r11.anchor: أحدهما أن لا يكون محتاجا إلى شيء سواه البتة وذلك لا يحصل إلا إذا كان واجب الوجود في ذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r12.claim: Razi says the first feature is a negation and the second a relation; together they constitute al-Qayyūm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p120#2/r12.anchor: أن يكون كل ما سواه محتاجا إليه في ذواتها وفي جملة صفاتها وذلك بأن يكون مبدأ لكل ما سواه

RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: The name ilāh encompasses existence, necessary and eternal being, freedom from defects, and the relational acts of creating and bringing things into being.
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: موجودا وعلى كيفيات ذلك الوجود أعني كونه أزليا أبديا واجب الوجود لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: Quraysh applied ilāh to idols; the better-known Islamic ruling forbids this application, while some permit it based on a devotional formula Razi calls remote.
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: أما كفار قريش فكانوا يطلقونه في حق الأصنام وهل يجوز ذلك في دين الإسلام ؟ المشهور أنه لا يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: Some allow calling another being ilāh because a transmitted invocation says “O God of gods,” though Razi regards that argument as far-fetched.
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه يجوز ؛ لأنه ورد في بعض الأذكار : يا إله الآلهة وهو بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r4.claim: Razi says Allah is a proper name, then asks whether that name itself signifies the divine attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r4.anchor: فسيأتي بيان أنه اسم علم لله تعالى فهل يدل هذا الاسم على هذه الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: Proper names function as signs for a particular essence; in God's case the sign is intellectual, and intellectual indication can encompass negative attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p121/r5.anchor: الإشارة في حق الله إشارة عقلية منزهة عن العلائق الحسية والإشارة العقلية قد تتناول السلوب

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r1.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r1.claim: The anthropomorphists argue that every existent is either spatially extended or inheres in something extended; what is neither, they say, is sheer nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r1.anchor: أهل التشبيه يقولون : الموجود إما أن يكون متحيزا وإما أن يكون حالا في

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r2.speaker: أهل التوحيد والتقديس
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r2.claim: The theologians of transcendence argue that anything spatial is divisible and needy, and anything inhering in it is even more dependent; the Necessary Existent can be neither.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r2.anchor: أهل التوحيد والتقديس ؛ فيقولون : أما المتحيز ؛ فهو منقسم وكل منقسم ؛ فهو محتاج

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r3.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r3.claim: Anthropomorphists read “great” as bodily size greater than the Throne and everything beneath it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r3.anchor: أهل التشبيه قالوا : معناه أن ذاته أعظم في الحجمية والمقدار

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r4.claim: Razi distinguishes al-kibriyāʾ from al-ʿaẓama: a divine report makes the former the cloak and the latter the waist-wrap, implying higher rank for the former.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r4.anchor: في الأخبار الإلهية أنه تعالى يقول : الكبرياء ردائي والعظمة إزاري

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r5.claim: The ritual formula says “God is greater,” never “God is more magnificent,” which Razi treats as evidence that the terms differ.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r5.anchor: الشريعة فرقت بين الحالين ؛ فإن المعتاد في دين الإسلام أن يقال في تحريمة الصلاة : الله أكبر

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r6.claim: Words from k-b-r, including “greater” and “the Magnificent,” are used of God, unlike the unattested “self-magnifying” form from ʿ-ẓ-m.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r6.anchor: الألفاظ المشتقة من الكبير مذكورة في حق الله تعالى ؛ كالأكبر والمتكبر بخلاف العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r7.claim: Although the Qur'an uses “great” and “greatest” in parallel ways, Razi says earlier evidence suggests a distinction and seeks to resolve the tension.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r7.anchor: ولا يؤوده حفظهما وهو العلي العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r8.claim: Razi proposes that greatness is intrinsic whether or not anyone recognizes it, whereas magnificence means being regarded as great and is therefore accidental.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r8.anchor: يشبه أن يكون الكبير في ذاته كبيرا سواء استكبره غيره أم لا وسواء عرف هذه الصفة أحد أو لا

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r9.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r9.claim: Those who place God in a location interpret His exaltedness as being above in space; some say He sits on the Throne, others posit a finite or infinite distance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r9.anchor: فالقائلون بأنه في الجهة والمكان قالوا : معنى علوه وتعاليه كونه موجودا في جهة فوق

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r10.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r10.claim: Some who place God in space say He sits above the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r10.anchor: فالقائلون بأنه في الجهة والمكان قالوا : معنى علوه وتعاليه كونه موجودا في جهة فوق ثم هؤلاء منهم من قال إنه جالس فوق العرش

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r11.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r11.claim: Others among them say God is separated from the Throne by a finite distance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r11.anchor: فالقائلون بأنه في الجهة والمكان قالوا : معنى علوه وتعاليه كونه موجودا في جهة فوق

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r12.speaker: أهل التشبيه
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r12.claim: A further group says God is separated from the Throne by an infinite distance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r12.anchor: فالقائلون بأنه في الجهة والمكان قالوا : معنى علوه وتعاليه كونه موجودا في جهة فوق

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r13.speaker: أهل التنزيه والتقديس
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r13.claim: The transcendentists interpret divine greatness without corporeality: through eternal duration, knowledge and action, mercy and wisdom, and complete power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r13.anchor: وأما أهل التنزيه والتقديس ؛ فإنهم حملوا العظيم والكبير على وجوه لا تفيد الجسمية والمقدار

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r14.speaker: أهل التنزيه والتقديس
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r14.claim: They interpret divine exaltedness as God's purity from defects and needs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r14.anchor: وأما العلو ؛ فأهل التنزيه يحملون هذا اللفظ على كونه منزها عن صفات النقائص والحاجات

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r15.claim: Razi summarizes that anthropomorphists treat great and greatest as names of the essence, while transcendence theologians treat them as attribute names.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r15.anchor: فلفظ العظيم والكبير عند المشبهة من أسماء الذات وعند أهل التوحيد من أسماء الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r16.claim: Both camps count al-ʿAlī among the attribute names, but anthropomorphists mean spatial height and theologians of unity mean freedom from what is unbefitting to divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p122/r16.anchor: وأما لفظ العلي ؛ فعند الكل من أسماء الصفات إلا أنه عند المشبهة يفيد الحصول في الحيز

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r1.claim: The pronouns rank “I” highest, “you” midway, and “he” lowest: self-reference is most immediate, while direct address requires presence and third-person reference does not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r1.anchor: فثبت أن أعلى الأقسام هو قوله : أنا وأوسطها : أنت وأدناها : هو

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r2.claim: The Qur'an states the oneness formula with each pronoun: “I” in verses about God's warning and Moses, “you” in Jonah's prayer, and “He” in many passages.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r2.anchor: وكلمة التوحيد وردت بكل واحدة من هذه الألفاظ

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r3.claim: Only God may say “There is no god but I” as a declaration, since it asserts divinity of its speaker; others may quote it, and full knowledge of “I” belongs only to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r3.anchor: هذا الكلام لا يجوز أن يتكلم به أحد إلا الله أو من يذكره على سبيل الحكاية عن الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r4.claim: A servant may say “There is no god but You” only while present; Jonah attained this when detached from every personal interest, a sign that witnessing requires such detachment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r4.anchor: بشرط أن يكون حاضرا لا غائبا

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r5.claim: The third formula, “There is no god but He,” is appropriate for those who are absent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r5.anchor: لا إله إلا هو ؛ فهذا يصح من الغائبين

RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r6.claim: Presence varies endlessly by nearness and degree of manifestation; every degree is absence relative to a fuller one, so presence and absence are both unbounded.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123/r6.anchor: ولما كانت درجات الحضور غير متناهية كانت مراتب الكمالات والنقصانات غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r1.claim: An unnamed poet captures the paradox of being absent yet present in the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r1.anchor: أيا غائبا حاضرا في الفؤاد … سلام على الغائب الحاضر

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r2.speaker: الشبلي
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r2.claim: As al-Shiblī neared death, a bystander asked him to say the testimony; he answered with two verses addressing the ever-present beloved, not the requested formula.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r2.anchor: يحكى أن الشبلي لما قربت وفاته قال بعض الحاضرين : قل لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r3.claim: Razi says the pronoun Hu has ineffable secrets; his written account feels paltry beside the joy and happiness he experiences in the heart when saying it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r3.anchor: أجد المكتوب بالنسبة إلى تلك الأحوال المشاهدة حقيرا فعند هذا عرفت أن لهذه الكلمة تأثيرا عجيبا

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r4.claim: Calling “O He” acknowledges the servant's lowliness and the absence of any fitting relation between created humanity and the eternal Lord, hence the third-person address.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r4.anchor: من أنا حتى أعرفك ومن أنا حتى أكون مخاطبا لك وما للتراب ورب الأرباب

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r5.claim: “O He” also declares that everything besides God is sheer nonbeing; Razi links this annihilation to the verse that all things perish except His Face.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r5.anchor: فقد حكم على كل ما سوى الله تعالى بأنه عدم محض ونفي صرف

RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r6.claim: Other divine names recall particular attributes and incline the speaker to seek the corresponding benefit, while Hu refers to God alone and leaves remembrance's light undimmed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p123#2/r6.anchor: فإنه يعرف أنه هو وهذا الذكر لا يدل على شيء غيره البتة

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r1.claim: Known divine descriptions fall into negative attributes that deny created defects and positive attributes that affirm the Creator's acts and ordering of creation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r1.anchor: أن جميع الصفات المعلومة عند الخلق إما صفات الجلال وإما صفات الإكرام

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r2.claim: Negating defects in a ruler's presence can be insulting; likewise, describing God's perfection by created qualities is poor etiquette because creaturely perfection is infinitely lower.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r2.anchor: من خاطب السلطان فقال : أنت لست أعمى ولست أصم

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r3.claim: Calling a sovereign great because he gave someone bread or water merits rebuke; created beings are even more negligible beside God's inexhaustible power.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r3.anchor: السلطان القاهر بأنه أعطى الفقير الفلاني كسرة خبز أو قطرة ماء

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r4.claim: People nevertheless need negative and positive attributes at first, because sensual minds can be redirected toward holiness only through accessible descriptions of divine perfection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r4.anchor: إلا أن ههنا سببا يرخص في ذكر هذه المدائح وهو أن النفس صارت مستغرقة في عالم الحس والخيال

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r5.claim: Once the soul turns from sense to holiness, it recognizes the shortcomings in both description types and leaves them for the name Hu.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r5.anchor: هذه الحالة ؛ فعند ذلك يتنبه لما في ذينك النوعين من الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r6.claim: The servant chooses Hu rather than “You” because it avoids claiming to have reached God's presence; it acknowledges that God is praised by and for Himself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r6.anchor: ولا أخاطبك أيضا بلفظة أنت ؛ لأن تلك اللفظة تفيد التيه والكبر

RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r7.claim: Thus Hu is the noblest remembrance in states of divine manifestation and unveiling, provided the reciter understands these subtleties.
RAZI-FULL:v1p125/r7.anchor: فلا جرم كان هذا الذكر أشرف الأذكار لكن بشرط التنبيه لهذه الأسرار

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r1.claim: Razi's fifth benefit is that sustained recitation of Hu produces longing for God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r1.anchor: أن المواظبة على هذا الذكر تورث الشوق إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r2.claim: The pronoun “He” marks the speaker's distance from God through created defects and contingency, not through place; all contingent beings are absent from divine perfection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r2.anchor: علم أنه غائب عن الحق ثم يعلم أن هذه الغيبة ليست بسبب المكان والجهة

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r3.claim: Awareness of divine perfections is partial because their degrees cannot be encompassed; this partial awareness generates endless longing, intensified by each advance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r3.anchor: فصارت تلك الكمالات مشعورا بها من وجه دون وجه والشعور بها من بعض الوجوه يشوق

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r4.claim: Longing is the greatest station because it alternates pain at delay with pleasure in arrival, and relief from pain deepens joy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r4.anchor: الشوق يفيد حصول آلام ولذات متوالية متعاقبة ؛ لأن بقدر ما يصل يلتذ

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r5.claim: Razi concludes that persevering in Hu yields the highest stations, happiness, and bliss.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r5.anchor: المواظبة على ذكر هذه الكلمة تفيد أعلى المقامات وأسنى الدرجات

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r6.claim: He begins a sixth benefit by distinguishing conception, which forms an idea without judgment, from assent, which affirms existence or nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r6.anchor: فهو أن تحصل في النفس صورة من غير أن تحكم النفس عليها بحكم البتة

RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r7.claim: Razi identifies conception with unity and assent with multiplicity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126/r7.anchor: التصور مقام التوحيد وأما التصديق فإنه مقام التكثير

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.claim: Conceiving a compound requires attending to its parts, but a simple noncomposite essence cannot be brought before the mind through an operation; hence simple conception is pure unity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r1.anchor: وأما القسم الثاني فهو تصور الماهيات البسيطة المنزهة عن جميع جهات التركيبات

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.claim: Saying “O He” is pure conception of the divine reality, free of composition and multiplicity, and therefore the highest form of unity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r2.anchor: قولنا في الحق سبحانه وتعالى يا هو هذا تصور محض خال عن التصديق

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.claim: God cannot be defined through Himself, constituent parts, or external things: the first is circular, the second assumes composition, and creation is unlike the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r3.anchor: فقد انسدت أبواب التعريفات بالنسبة إلى هويته المخصوصة وماهيته المعينة فلم يبق طريق إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.claim: Because no definition reaches God's essence, “O He” directs mind and spirit toward its light in hope of a glimpse.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r4.anchor: فقول الذاكر يا هو توجيه لحدقة العقل والروح إلى الحضرة القدسية

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r5.claim: Awe of a mighty king can erase awareness of hunger, pain, and even family; a glimpse of divine majesty similarly leaves only Hu and makes its recitation an imitation of that state.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r5.anchor: فكذلك العبد إذا قال يا هو وتجلى لعقله وروحه ذرة من نور جلال تلك الهوية

RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r6.claim: Razi asks God to grant the reciter the state toward which this remembrance points.
RAZI-FULL:v1p126#2/r6.anchor: فنسأل الله تعالى الكريم أن يسعدنا بها

RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever makes his concerns one will be spared the concerns of this world and the next; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r1.anchor: من جعل همومه هما واحدا كفاه الله هموم الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r2.claim: The servant's needs are endless, so only God, whose power, mercy, and wisdom are endless, can meet them; the servant should devote concern and speech to His remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r2.anchor: الحاجات التي هي غير متناهية لا يقدر عليها إلا الموصوف بقدرة غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r3.claim: The tenth benefit is that thought cannot attend to one thing while absorbed in another, so the worshipper should devote mind and tongue to the noblest object and remembrance: Hu.
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r3.anchor: فالأولى أن أجعل قلبي وفكري مشغولا بمعرفة أشرف المعلومات وأجعل لساني مشغولا بذكر أشرف المذكورات

RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r4.claim: Razi calls remembrance one of the noblest stations and cites a divine report that God remembers a servant who remembers Him, privately or in a better gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r4.anchor: إذا ذكرني عبدي في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي وإذا ذكرني في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير من ملئه

RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r5.claim: Razi calls praise without asking the best form of remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p127/r5.anchor: أفضل الأذكار ذكر الله بالثناء الخالي عن السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r1.claim: A report in which the Prophet speaks on God's authority promises the best gift to the one whom remembrance keeps from asking; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r1.anchor: من شغله ذكري عن مسألتي أعطيته أفضل ما أعطي السائلين

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r2.claim: A needy servant vocative signals a request: calling God generous, beneficent, or merciful implicitly asks for favor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r2.anchor: فإذا قال الفقير للغني يا كريم كان معناه أكرم وإذ قال له يا نفاع كان معناه طلب النفع

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r3.claim: Because Hu carries no implication of asking or seeking, Razi concludes it is the greatest remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r3.anchor: أما إذا قال يا هو كان معناه خاليا عن الإشعار بالسؤال والطلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r4.claim: Razi closes the chapter by recording a litany he saw in a book: “O He,” “O He beyond whom there is no He,” and other names.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r4.anchor: يا هو يا من لا هو إلا هو يا من لا إله إلا هو يا أزل يا أبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r5.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r5.claim: Al-Ghazālī calls “There is no god but God” the common people's monotheism and “There is no god but He” the elect's monotheism; Razi approves this distinction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r5.anchor: الشيخ الغزالي رحمة الله عليه كان يقول : لا إله إلا الله توحيد العوام

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r6.claim: Razi supports the elect's formula through the sequence in Qasas: the verse says “no god but He,” then “all things perish except His Face,” which he interprets as “except Him.”
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r6.anchor: معناه إلا هو فذكر قوله إلا هو بعد قوله لا إله

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r7.claim: He argues against denying that an efficient cause acts on essences: if it only bestows existence, existence itself is an essence, producing regress or denying causation altogether.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r7.anchor: القول بأن المؤثر لا تأثير له في الماهيات ينفي التأثير والمؤثر وينفي الصنع والصانع بالكلية

RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r8.claim: Every contingent essence depends on its cause even to be an essence; without God's effect there is no essence, existence, reality, or fixed status.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128/r8.anchor: فكل ما بالغير فإنه يرتفع بارتفاع الغير فلولا المؤثر لم تكن تلك الماهية ماهية ولا حقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.claim: One position makes divine names strictly revelatory: no name or attribute may be applied unless it occurs in the Qur'an or an authentic hadith.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم لا يجوز إطلاق شيء من الأسماء والصفات على الله تعالى إلا إذا كان واردا في القرآن والأحاديث الصحيحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.claim: The opposing position permits any expression whose meaning befits God's majesty and attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : كل لفظ دل على معنى يليق بجلال الله وصفاته فهو جائز

RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.claim: Al-Ghazālī distinguishes names from descriptions: names of God require textual warrant, but descriptive attributes do not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r3.anchor: فاسمي محمد واسمك أبو بكر فهذا من باب الأسماء وأما الصفات فمثل وصف هذا الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.speaker: أصحاب التوقيف
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.claim: Proponents of strict textual warrant argue that some apparently laudatory human labels, such as physician or jurist, are not used for God, so naming is restricted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r4.anchor: إن العالم له أسماء كثيرة ثم إنا نصف الله تعالى بكونه عالما ولا نصفه بكونه طبيبا

RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.claim: Razi begins answering the example of “physician,” “jurist,” “certain,” and “clarifying,” arguing that each term has a meaning that makes it unsuitable for God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p128#2/r5.anchor: وأجيب عنه فقيل : أما الطبيب فقد ورد

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r1.claim: A report says that when Abū Bakr fell ill and someone offered to bring a physician, he replied that the physician had made him ill.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r1.anchor: أبا بكر لما مرض قيل له : نحضر الطبيب

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r2.claim: “Jurist” entails understanding a speaker's purpose after ambiguity enters his speech, a condition impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r2.anchor: وأما الفقيه فهو عبارة عن فهم غرض المتكلم من كلامه بعد دخول الشبهة فيه

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r3.claim: “Certain” derives from water settling in a basin and refers to knowledge reached after repeated indications; such acquisition is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r3.anchor: فاليقين هو العلم الذي حصل بسبب تعاقب الأمارات الكثيرة وترادفها

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r4.claim: “Clarifying” implies appearance after obscurity or separating confused things, which cannot apply to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r4.anchor: وأما التبيين فهو عبارة عن الظهور بعد الخفاء وذلك لأن التبيين مشتق من البينونة

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r5.speaker: القائلون بأنه لا حاجة إلى التوقيف
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r5.claim: Opponents of strict warrant note that Muslims use divine names in Persian, Turkish, and Indian languages although scripture does not list those words.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r5.anchor: أن أسماء الله وصفاته مذكورة بالفارسية وبالتركية وبالهندية وأن شيئا منها لم يرد في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r6.speaker: القائلون بأنه لا حاجة إلى التوقيف
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r6.claim: They cite “God's are the beautiful names, so call upon Him by them”: every name denoting praise and majesty is beautiful and permitted.

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r7.speaker: القائلون بأنه لا حاجة إلى التوقيف
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r7.claim: They argue that valid meanings matter more than particular words, so forbidding a suitable expression is pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r7.anchor: لا فائدة في الألفاظ إلا رعاية المعاني فإذا كانت المعاني صحيحة كان المنع من إطلاق اللفظة المعينة عبثا

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r8.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r8.claim: Al-Ghazālī reasons that if giving someone a name can be poor etiquette, naming God is even more sensitive, whereas varied descriptive expressions are permitted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r8.anchor: وضع الاسم في حق الواحد منا يعد سوء أدب ففي حق الله أولى أما ذكر الصفات بالألفاظ المختلفة فهو جائز

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r9.claim: Razi lists scriptural terms whose literal senses imply defects: mockery, scheming, anger, wonder, arrogance, and modesty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r9.anchor: اعلم أنه قد ورد في القرآن ألفاظ دالة على صفات لا يمكن إثباتها في حق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r10.claim: The verse “rather, I wondered, while they scoff” assigns wonder to God according to a reading with ḍamma on the tāʾ; Razi explains wonder as an ignorant reaction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r10.anchor: فمن قرأ عجبت بضم التاء كان التعجب منسوبا إلى الله والتعجب عبارة عن حالة تعرض في القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r11.claim: Razi's rule is to apply these words to their final effects in God's case, not to the initial bodily or emotional states that ordinarily cause them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r11.anchor: فإذا سمعت الغضب في حق الله تعالى فأحمله على نهايات الأعراض لا على بدايات الأعراض

RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r12.claim: He illustrates the rule with anger: its ordinary beginning is heated blood and temperament, while its final effect is harm to the one who incurs anger.
RAZI-FULL:v1p129/r12.anchor: مثاله أن الغضب حالة تحصل في القلب عند غليان دم القلب وسخونة المزاج والأثر الحاصل منها في النهاية

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r1.speaker: بعض كتب التذكير
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r1.claim: A devotional book claims God has four thousand names, one thousand each in the Qur'an and authentic reports, Torah, Gospel, and Psalms, plus a hidden thousand in the Preserved Tablet.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r1.anchor: رأيت في بعض كتب التذكير أن لله تعالى أربعة آلاف اسم : ألف منها في القرآن والأخبار الصحيحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r2.claim: Razi finds innumerable names plausible because divine attributes based on negation and relation are unlimited.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r2.anchor: هذا غير مستبعد فإنا بينا أن أقسام صفات الله بحسب السلوب والإضافات غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r3.claim: The more one observes God's governance and wisdom in the upper and lower worlds, the more divine names expressing praise and exaltation one recognizes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r3.anchor: كل من كان اطلاعه على آثار حكمة الله تعالى في تدبير العالم الأعلى وتدبير العالم الأسفل أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r4.claim: Studying human anatomy reveals about ten thousand kinds of mercy and wisdom, each suggesting a name of God; uncounted anatomical divisions signal still more wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r4.anchor: فمن طالع تشريح بدن الإنسان ووقف فيه على ما يقرب من عشرة آلاف نوع من أنواع الرحمة والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r5.claim: Razi cites the verse that God's blessings cannot be counted and concludes that every newly recognized wisdom yields another divine name, with no end to the names.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r5.anchor: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها

RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r6.speaker: جالينوس
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r6.claim: Galen says an angel visited in a dream after he withheld a discussion of the benefits of the eye, asking why he hid God's wisdom; Galen then wrote a separate, detailed treatise.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130/r6.anchor: وقال جالينوس إن إلهك يقول : لم أخفيت حكمتي عن عبادي

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r1.claim: Written talismanic formulas point to words, which point to mental meanings; if they mean nothing they are useless, while meaningful formulas must concern God rather than something else.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r1.anchor: لا شك أن الكتابة دالة على الألفاظ ولا شك أن الألفاظ دالة على الصور الذهنية

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r2.claim: Since meaningful remembrance of God is already delimited, familiar supplications should be more effective than unknown formulas; differences among languages matter little.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r2.anchor: ولما كانت أقسام ذكر الله مضبوطة ولا يمكن الزيادة عليها كان أحسن أحوال تلك الكلمات أن تكون من جنس هذه الأدعية

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r3.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r3.claim: An objection says weak souls gain little from known prayers, but mysterious words may inspire awe and fear, detach them from the bodily world, and strengthen spiritual influence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r3.anchor: أما إذا قرؤا تلك الألفاظ المجهولة ولم يفهموا منها شيئا وحصلت عندهم أوهام أنها كلمات عالية

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r4.claim: Razi presents that objection as the reason unknown incantations might affect ordinary people, though his initial reasoning favors known supplications.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r4.anchor: فحصل لهم بهذا السبب نوع من التجرد عن عالم الجسم وتوجه إلى عالم القدس

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r5.claim: His fifth discussion says human rational souls differ in their natures, with some bright and noble, some low and dark, some compassionate, some harsh, and varied worldly desires.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r5.anchor: ثبت عندنا أن النفوس الناطقة البشرية مختلفة بالجوهر والماهية فبعضها إلهية مشرقة حرة كريمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r6.claim: These dispositions are rooted in each soul; spiritual discipline can weaken a trait's dominance but cannot change the soul's original nature.
RAZI-FULL:v1p130#2/r6.anchor: وأن الرياضة والمجاهدة لا تقلب النفوس عن أحوالها الأصلية ومناهجها الطبيعية وإنما تأثير الرياضة في أن تضعف تلك الأخلاق

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r1.claim: Razi cites the Prophet's saying that people are like mines of gold and silver; he gives no chain or grading.

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r2.claim: He also cites the Prophet's saying that spirits are troops joined in affinity; no chain or grading is supplied.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r2.anchor: الأرواح جنود مجندة إذا عرفت هذا فنقول : الجنسية علة الضم

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r3.claim: Similarity causes attachment: a soul dominated by the meaning of a particular divine name is especially suited to that name and quickly benefits from remembering it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r3.anchor: فكل اسم من أسماء الله تعالى دال على معنى معين فكل نفس غلب عليها ذلك المعنى كانت تلك النفس شديدة المناسبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r4.speaker: أبو النجيب البغدادي السهروردي
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r4.claim: Al-Suhrawardī reportedly had a disciple undertake one or two forty-day retreats, recited the ninety-nine names to him, then assigned a name-based remembrance if one especially moved him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r4.anchor: كان يأمر المريد بالأربعين مرة أو مرتين بقدر ما يراه من المصلحة ثم كان يقرأ عليه الأسماء التسعة والتسعين

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r5.speaker: أبو النجيب البغدادي السهروردي
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r5.claim: If a disciple showed no response, al-Suhrawardī told him to return to worldly duties because he was not made for this path.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r5.anchor: فإن رآه عديم التأثر عند قراءتها عليه قال له اخرج إلى السوق واشتغل بمهمات الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r6.claim: Razi calls this sensible: differing souls each suit a particular state, and a matching practice readily brings that soul from potentiality into actuality.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r6.anchor: هذا هو المعقول فإنه لما كانت النفوس مختلفة كان كل واحد منها مناسبا لحالة مخصوصة

RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r7.claim: Razi closes his survey of divine names and opens a new chapter on the name Allah.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131/r7.anchor: وليكن هذا آخر كلامنا في البحث عن مطلق الأسماء والله الهادي . الباب التاسع

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.claim: Razi's chosen view is that Allah is a proper name for God, not a derivative; he attributes it to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, and most legal theorists and jurists.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r1.anchor: المختار عندنا أن هذا اللفظ اسم علم لله تعالى وأنه ليس بمشتق البتة وهو قول الخليل وسيبويه وقول أكثر الأصوليين

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.claim: If Allah were derived, it would denote a general concept open to many bearers, making “There is no god but Allah” fail to establish exclusive monotheism; its established force proves it is a proper name.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r2.anchor: لو كان لفظا مشتقا لكان معناه معنى كليا لا يمنع نفس مفهومه من وقوع الشركة فيه

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.claim: A proper name normally precedes descriptive predicates; likewise speakers say “Allah, the Knowing, the Powerful,” not the reverse.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r3.anchor: كل من أراد أن يذكر الله تعالى بالصفات المقدسة فإنه يذكر أولا لفظة الله ثم يذكر عقيبه صفات المدائح

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.claim: The apparent counterexample in Ibrahim 14:1 has two readings: nominative makes Allah a new subject, while genitive identifies which praised one is meant rather than making a proper name into an adjective.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r4.anchor: منهم من قرأ الله بالرفع وحينئذ يزول السؤال ؛ لأنه لما جعله مبتدأ فقد أخرجه عن جعله صفة

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.claim: The question “Do you know of any namesake for Him?” concerns a proper namesake rather than a shared attribute; Razi says that name is Allah.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r5.anchor: وليس المراد من الاسم في هذه الآية الصفة وإلا لكذب قوله هل تعلم له سميا

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.speaker: القائلون بأنه ليس اسم علم
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.claim: Opponents argue that “He is Allah in the heavens” and “He is Allah” use Allah predicatively, unlike a proper name such as Zayd.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r6.anchor: قوله الله لا بد وأن يكون صفة ولا يجوز أن يكون اسم علم

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r7.speaker: القائلون بأنه ليس اسم علم
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r7.claim: They also say a proper name functions like pointing, which is impossible for God, and distinguishes one individual from another similar in essence, which God cannot have.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r7.anchor: أن اسم العلم قائم مقام الإشارة فلما كانت الإشارة ممتنعة في حق الله تعالى كان اسم العلم ممتنعا

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r8.claim: Razi answers that a sentence such as “He is Zayd unrivaled in learning” shows a proper name can follow a pronoun without being an adjective.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r8.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك جاريا مجرى أن يقال : هذا زيد الذي لا نظير له في العلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r9.claim: A proper name designates a particular essence without requiring sensory pointing or a second similar being; neither objection rules out applying one to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p131#2/r9.anchor: الاسم العلم هو الذي وضع لتعيين الذات المعينة ولا حاجة فيه إلى كون ذلك المسمى مشارا إليه بالحس

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: The first derivation says ilāh means one worshipped, rightly or wrongly, though religious usage narrows it to the true object of worship; on the literal definition God would not be ilāh eternally.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r1.anchor: أن الإله هو المعبود سواء عبد بحق أو بباطل ثم غلب في عرف الشرع على المعبود بالحق

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r2.claim: God alone deserves worship because He bestows every blessing, directly or through intermediaries, as all possible things exist through Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r2.anchor: وذلك لأنه تعالى هو المنعم بجميع النعم أصولها وفروعها وذلك لأن الموجود إما واجب وإما ممكن

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r3.claim: Since worship is the utmost reverence, only the source of utmost benefaction deserves it; Razi concludes that God alone is worthy of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r3.anchor: العبادة غاية التعظيم فإذا ثبت هذا فنقول : إن غاية التعظيم لا يليق إلا لمن صدرت عنه غاية الإنعام

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r4.claim: Razi condemns worship motivated by reward: the reward becomes the actual object of worship and God merely a means to it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r4.anchor: أن من عبد الله ليتوصل بعبادته إلى شيء آخر كان المعبود في الحقيقة هو ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r5.claim: He says a prayer performed to gain reward or avoid punishment is invalid, and that alternate access to the reward would make such a worshipper abandon God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r5.anchor: لو قال : أصلي لطلب الثواب أو للخوف من العقاب لم تصح صلاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r6.claim: Reward-seeking does not constitute love for God or desire to worship Him, since worship would cease if the same reward were available another way.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r6.anchor: فمن عبد الله للأجر والثواب كان بحيث لو وجد الأجر والثواب بطريق آخر لم يعبد الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r7.claim: A higher aim is the honor of serving God: prayer joins awareness of the Lord's majesty and the servant's lowliness, verbal remembrance, and bodily service.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r7.anchor: أن يتشرف بخدمة الله لأنه إذا شرع في الصلاة حصلت النية في القلب وتلك النية عبارة عن العلم بعزة الربوبية

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r8.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r8.claim: Critics object that idols are worshipped although they are not gods.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r8.anchor: أن الأوثان عبدت مع أنها ليست آلهة

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r9.claim: They object that God is God of inanimate beings and animals even though these cannot worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r9.anchor: أنه تعالى إله الجمادات والبهائم مع أن صدور العبادة منها محال

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r10.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r10.claim: They also object that God is God of children and the insane, from whom worship does not issue.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r10.anchor: أنه تعالى إله المجانين والأطفال مع أنه لا تصدر العبادة عنها

RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r11.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r11.claim: A final objection is that being worshipped is not an attribute of God, but only means being mentioned, known, and intended by servants.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133/r11.anchor: أن المعبود ليس له بكونه معبودا صفة

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.claim: The fifth objection is that defining ilāh as the actually worshipped means God was not ilāh from eternity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.anchor: الخامس يلزم أن يقال : إنه تعالى ما كان إلها في الأزل

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.claim: Defining ilāh as one deserving worship still excludes inanimate beings, animals, children, the insane, and God's eternal status.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.anchor: الإله ليس عبارة عن المعبود بل الإله هو الذي يستحق أن يكون معبودا

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.claim: A third definition is one capable of acts that would make a worship-capable agent deserving of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.anchor: ومنهم من قال : إنه القادر على أفعال لو فعلها لاستحق العبادة ممن يصح صدور العبادة عنه

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.claim: Razi says the first two definitions fail to make God ilāh eternally, while the third preserves His eternal divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.anchor: إن فسرنا الإله بالتفسيرين الأولين لم يكن إلها في الأزل ولو فسرناه بالتفسير الثالث كان إلها في الأزل

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.claim: A second etymology derives ilāh from taking refuge or finding rest in someone: minds find rest only in God's remembrance, and souls rise only through knowing Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.anchor: الإله مشتق من ألهت إلى فلان أي : سكنت إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.claim: First proof: perfection is loved for itself; every other being is essentially contingent and deficient, while God is perfect in Himself, so He must be loved for Himself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.anchor: الكمال محبوب لذاته وما سوى الحق فهو ناقص لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.claim: Second proof: possible beings cannot stand independently and need the Necessary Existent to exist; minds likewise depend on divine mercy and grace.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.anchor: كل ممكن فإنه لا يقف عند نفسه بل ما لم يتعلق بالواجب لذاته لم يوجد

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.claim: Razi connects these arguments to the verse that hearts find rest in remembering God.

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.claim: A third etymology links ilāh with bewilderment: the deprived remain lost in ignorance, while those who attain knowledge become bewildered by divine oneness and majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.anchor: أنه مشتق من الوله وهو ذهاب العقل واعلم أن الخلق قسمان : واصلون إلى ساحل بحر معرفته

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.claim: Razi restates the idea as souls racing in monotheism: laggards remain in dark dust, while those who arrive are lost in the lights of honor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.anchor: فبعضها تخلفت وبعضها سبقت فالتي تخلفت بقيت في ظلمات الغبار والتي سبقت وصلت إلى عالم الأنوار

RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r11.claim: A fourth derivation from lāha, “to rise,” means God transcends possible beings and created things, since only He is necessary, perfect, one, and the source of all.
RAZI-FULL:v1p133#2/r11.anchor: أنه مشتق من لاه إذا ارتفع والحق سبحانه وتعالى وهو المرتفع عن مشابهة الممكنات ومناسبة المحدثات

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
