RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r1.claim: Divine exaltedness cannot be spatial: a place-based elevation would belong essentially to the place and only incidentally to its occupant, making the place nobler than God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r1.anchor: لأن كل ارتفاع حصل بسبب المكان فهو للمكان بالذات وللمتمكن بالعرض

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r2.claim: A fifth derivation connects ilāh with bewilderment: every imagined conception differs from God, yet denying Him is impossible because contingent things require a necessary source.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r2.anchor: فالعبد إذا تفكر فيه تحير ؛ لأن كل ما يتخيله الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r3.claim: The intellect can only affirm divine existence and perfection while admitting its inability to comprehend Him; this incapacity is itself insight and leaves the mind perplexed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r3.anchor: فههنا العجز عن درك الإدراك إدراك ولا شك أن هذا موقف عجيب تتحير العقول فيه

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r4.claim: A sixth etymology from lāha yalūhu means concealment: God's essence is hidden from intellects by its very perfection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r4.anchor: من لاه يلوه إذا احتجب ومعنى كونه محتجبا من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r5.claim: Razi compares divine existence to sunlight: if the sun never set, people would mistake its light on walls as inherent; because God cannot disappear, some mistakenly think creatures exist by themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r5.anchor: فلو قدرنا أنه كان يصح على الله تعالى الطلوع والغروب والغيبة والحضور لكان عند غروبه يزول ضوء الوجود عن الممكنات

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r6.claim: A discerning thinker says God is hidden from intellects by the intensity of His manifestation and concealed by the fullness of His light.
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r6.anchor: سبحان من احتجب عن العقول بشدة ظهوره واختفى عنها بكمال نوره

RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p134/r7.claim: The essence of divine self-sufficiency is concealed from intellects; God is hidden through power, while creatures are veiled as the overpowered.

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r1.claim: One derivation of al-ilāh comes from a young camel clinging to its mother: servants cling to God in supplication in every state.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r1.anchor: اشتقاقه من أله الفصيل إذا ولع بأمه والمعنى أن العباد مولهون

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r2.claim: People remember only God in severe distress, then credit weak causes after rescue; consistency requires turning to God in ease as well as hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r2.anchor: أن الإنسان إذا وقع في بلاء عظيم وآفة قوية فهنالك ينسى كل شيء إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r3.claim: Goodness and relief are sought from God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r3.anchor: أن الخير والراحة مطلوب من الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r4.claim: Any apparent human benefactor can give only because God creates the impulse to give, so God is the true benefactor to whom people return.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r4.anchor: فإن كان غيره فذلك الغير لا يحسن إلا إذا خلق الله في قلبه داعية الإحسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r5.claim: A spiritual master describes purifying the heart like working iron: fear softens it, remembrance cleans it, and persistent renunciation empties it of love besides God until divine love and light fill it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r5.anchor: ثم بعد ذلك شرعت في غسله عن الأوضار والأقذار عشر سنين ثم بعد هذه الأحوال جلست على باب حجرة القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r6.claim: Al-ilāh can derive from fleeing in fear and seeking refuge; God alone protects all creatures from harm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r6.anchor: أن اشتقاق لفظ الإله من أله الرجل يأله إذا فزع من أمر نزل به فألهه أي أجاره

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r7.claim: God alone is the true source of blessing, food, and existence, subduing nonexistence through creation; therefore He alone is truly God.

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r8.claim: God calls sinners His debtors but tells them to flee to Him, since He repays their debts and forgives them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r8.anchor: عبادي ! أنتم غرمائي بكثرة ذنوبكم ولكن لا تفروا مني بل أقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r9.claim: Unlike kings who close their doors to the poor, God opens His door to them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p135/r9.anchor: الملوك يغلقون أبوابهم عن الفقراء دون الأغنياء وأنا أفعل ضد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r1.claim: A report says God distributed one mercy among all earthly creatures and reserved ninety-nine mercies for His servants on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r1.anchor: إن لله تعالى مائة رحمة أنزل منها رحمة واحدة بين الجن والإنس والطير والبهائم والهوام

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r2.claim: Rāzī says the report was for instruction: divine mercy is an unbounded sea and cannot literally be limited to a number.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r2.anchor: إنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما ذكر هذا الكلام على سبيل التفهيم وإلا فبحار الرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r3.claim: God asks sinners whether they hoped to meet Him; they say they hoped for pardon, and He promises them forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r3.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن الله عز وجل يقول يوم القيامة للمذنبين

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar describes ninety-nine huge records of sins outweighed by a card bearing the testimony of faith; nothing outweighs remembrance of God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r4.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : إن الله عز وجل ينشر

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r5.claim: Seeing a woman protect her child from heat, the Prophet tells the onlookers that God is more merciful to them than she is to her child.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r5.anchor: فأقبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى وقف عليهم فأخبروه الخبر فقال

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r6.claim: Some say al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are non-Arabic, perhaps Hebrew or Syriac forms later Arabized.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم هذه اللفظة ليست عربية بل عبرانية أو سريانية فإنهم يقولون إلها رحمانا ومرحيانا

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects foreign origin as an inference from resemblance alone, noting that Arabs identify God as creator and recognize no namesake for Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r7.anchor: وهذا بعيد ولا يلزم من المشابهة الحاصلة بين اللغتين الطعن في كون هذه اللفظة عربية أصلية

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r8.claim: Most accept the word as Arabic; those who deny that Allah is a proper name divide between Kufan and Basran derivations.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r8.anchor: وأما الأكثرون فقد سلموا كونها لفظة عربية أما القائلون بأن هذا اللفظ اسم علم لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r9.claim: The Kufans derive Allah from ilāh with the article for glorification, then explain loss of hamza and assimilation of the two lām letters.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r9.anchor: قال الكوفيون : أصل هذه اللفظة إلاه

RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r10.speaker: البصريون
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r10.claim: The Basrans derive Allah from lāh with the article and cite a poem for the original form.
RAZI-FULL:v1p136/r10.anchor: وقال البصريون أصله لاه فألحقوا بها الألف واللام فقيل الله وأنشدوا

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r1.claim: The quoted poetic fragment preserves lāh as the underlying form cited for the Basran derivation; the poet is unnamed here.

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r2.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl says Allah and al-ilāh are specific to God; other uses are either in a construct phrase or indefinite, as in the Israelites’ request for idols.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r2.anchor: قال الخليل : أطبق جميع الخلق على أن قولنا الله مخصوص بالله

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r3.claim: Removing the initial alif from Allah yields lillāh, attested in Qur’anic phrases about God’s armies and treasuries.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r3.anchor: أنك إذا حذفت الألف من قولك الله بقي الباقي على صورة لله

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r4.claim: Further deletion yields lahu and then huwa; the wāw is extra because it drops in the dual and plural forms.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r4.anchor: وإن حذفت عن هذه البقية اللام الأولى بقيت البقية على صورة له

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r5.claim: The name Allah encompasses all divine attributes, whereas calling God by a specific name such as al-Raḥmān or al-ʿAlīm identifies one attribute.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r5.anchor: وأما إذا قلت يا الله فقد وصفته بجميع الصفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r6.claim: The testimony of faith uniquely uses Allah: replacing it with another divine name would not, in Rāzī’s account, take a non-Muslim into Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137/r6.anchor: أما إذا قال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله فإنه يخرج من الكفر ويدخل في الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r1.claim: Rāzī classifies things as useful and necessary, useful but unnecessary, necessary but harmful, or neither useful nor necessary, with worldly and afterlife examples.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الأشياء على أربعة أقسام : الذي يكون نافعا

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r2.claim: Breath is useful and necessary in worldly life, while knowledge of God is necessary for the afterlife; losing it kills the heart and entails endless punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r2.anchor: وإما أن يكون كذلك في الآخرة وهو معرفة الله تعالى فإنها إن زالت عن القلب لحظة واحدة مات القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r3.claim: Money in this world and other kinds of knowledge in the afterlife are useful without being necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r3.anchor: فهو كالمال في الدنيا وكسائر العلوم والمعارف في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r4.claim: Worldly illness, death, poverty, and aging are necessary harms, while the afterlife has no such necessary harm; worldly poverty and afterlife punishment are neither useful nor necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r4.anchor: كالمضار التي لا بد منها في الدنيا : كالأمراض والموت والفقر والهرم

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r5.claim: Loss of bodily life lasts only a moment, but loss of knowledge of God brings pain that endures forever.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r5.anchor: لكن الموت الأول أسهل من الثاني ؛ لأنه لا يتألم في الموت الأول إلا ساعة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r6.claim: Thought functions like breathing: proof preserves balanced faith and knowledge, while reflection expels corrupt doubts from the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r6.anchor: كذلك الفكر له أثران : أحدهما : إيصال نسيم الحجة

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r7.claim: Recognizing that sensible things are finite and eventually perish helps a person remain safe from harm and reach good outcomes.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r7.anchor: هذه المحسوسات متناهية في مقاديرها منتهية بالآخرة إلى الفناء بعد وجودها

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r8.claim: Everything attained is only a drop from God’s seas of mercy and a speck of His beneficence, revealing the meaning of al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r8.anchor: كل ما وجدته ووصلت إليه فهو قطرة من بحار رحمة الله وذرة من أنوار إحسانه

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r9.claim: The human soul begins ignorant, as stated in the Qur’an, and can develop through its sensory, moving, perceptive, and rational powers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r9.anchor: أما نفسك فلا شك أنها كانت جاهلة في مبدأ الفطرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r10.claim: Rational objects are limitless: even endless study at the speed of lightning would yield finite knowledge beside the infinite unknown.
RAZI-FULL:v1p137#2/r10.anchor: لكانت المعلومات التي ما عرفها ولم يصل إليها أيضا غير متناهية والمتناهي في جنب غير المتناهي قليل في كثير

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r1.claim: Inspecting the body’s four humors, organs, and benefits reveals God’s mercy in creating and guiding people and illuminates al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r1.anchor: أما بدنك فاعلم أنه جوهر مركب من الأخلاط الأربعة فتأمل كيفية تركيبها وتشريحها

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r2.claim: Rāzī’s primary position is that true mercy belongs only to God; even if others are called merciful, God’s mercy is more complete.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r2.anchor: الحق أن الرحمة ليست إلا لله ثم بتقدير أن تكون لغير الله رحمة إلا أن رحمة الله أكمل من رحمة غيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r3.claim: Only God gives without compensation: all other givers seek material or spiritual return, while God is complete in Himself and gains no perfection from giving.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r3.anchor: فكل أحد غير الله فهو إنما يعطي ليأخذ عوضا إلا أن الأعواض أقسام

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r4.claim: Anything contingent exists only through the Necessary Existent, so any mercy coming through another creature is created by God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r4.anchor: كل من سوى الله فهو ممكن لذاته والممكن لذاته لا يوجد إلا بإيجاد واجب الوجود لذاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r5.claim: A human act of mercy occurs only when a decisive motive is present, and God creates that motive in the heart; He is the true merciful agent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r5.anchor: يمتنع رجحان الفعل على الترك إلا عند حصول داعية جازمة في القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r6.claim: A gift benefits its recipient only through God-given capacities and protection from harm, so God is the real giver and merciful benefactor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r6.anchor: بل الحق أن خالق تلك الحنطة وذلك البستان هو الله تعالى والممكن من الانتفاع بهما هو الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r7.claim: If creatures also show mercy, God’s gift is better because it humbles the recipient before God rather than before another creature.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r7.anchor: فإذا حصل التواضع بالنسبة إلى حضرة الله فذاك خير من حصول هذه الحالة بالنسبة إلى بعض الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r8.claim: God’s gifts direct people toward earning eternal happiness, while a creature’s gift usually obliges the recipient to serve that creature’s aims.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r8.anchor: أما غير الله فإنه إذا أنعم عليك بنعمة أمرك بالاشتغال بخدمته والانصراف إلى تحصيل مقصوده

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r9.claim: Servitude to God is preferable to becoming like a servant of a human benefactor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r9.anchor: أن المنعم عليه يصير كالعبد للمنعم وعبودية الله أولى من عبودية غير الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r10.claim: God knows every need and can fulfill every possible request, unlike human benefactors who may not know or meet a person’s needs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r10.anchor: أما الحق تعالى فإنه عالم بجميع المعلومات قادر على كل الممكنات فإذا ظهرت بك حاجة عرفها

RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r11.claim: Receiving favor from God is preferable to accepting a human benefactor’s claim of favor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p139/r11.anchor: الإنعام يوجب المنة وقبول المنة من الحق أفضل من قبولها من الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r1.claim: Moses first healed his stomach illness after seeking God’s guidance for a plant, but worsened when he later credited the plant itself; God’s name is the world’s antidote.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r1.anchor: لأنك في المرة الأولى ذهبت مني إلى الكلأ فحصل فيه الشفاء وفي المرة الثانية ذهبت منك إلى الكلأ

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r2.claim: In a tale about Rābiʿa, a thief cannot find the door while she sleeps; a voice says that if the beloved sleeps, the Sovereign remains awake.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r2.anchor: ضع القماش واخرج فإن نام الحبيب فالسلطان يقظان

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r3.claim: A shepherd says wolves leave his flock alone since the shepherd reconciled himself with God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r3.anchor: فقال الراعي : من حين اصطلح الراعي مع الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r4.claim: Bismillah means I begin in God’s name, with the verb omitted for brevity; its opening position signals ease, lenience, pardon, and beneficence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r4.anchor: معناه أبدأ باسم الله فأسقط منه قوله أبدأ تخفيفا فإذا قلت بسم الله فكأنك قلت أبدأ باسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r5.claim: A tale says God spared Pharaoh because Moses saw his disbelief while God saw Bismillah written on his palace door; the author infers that inner inscription is more consequential.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r5.anchor: يا موسى لعلك تريد إهلاكه أنت تنظر إلى كفره وأنا أنظر إلى ما كتبه على بابه

RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r6.claim: Since God named Himself al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm, the author asks rhetorically how He could fail to show mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p140/r6.anchor: سمى نفسه رحمانا رحيما فكيف لا يرحم

RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r1.claim: A beggar’s parable asks God to make His gift match His vast door of mercy, and not to deprive worshipers of that mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r1.anchor: إما أن يجعل الباب لائقا بالعطية أو العطية لائقة بالباب

RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r2.claim: Placing al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm after the name signifying power and exaltedness indicates that mercy is greater and more complete than wrath.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r2.anchor: الله إشارة إلى القهر والقدرة والعلو ثم ذكر عقيبه الرحمن الرحيم وذلك يدل على أن رحمته أكثر وأكمل من قهره

RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r3.claim: As a royal mark protects property from enemies, beginning an act with God’s name marks it against Satan, the enemy of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r3.anchor: إن لطاعتك عدوا وهو الشيطان فإذا شرعت في عمل فاجعل عليه سمتي وقل

RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r4.claim: A person should keep company with remembrance of God so as not to be separated from Him in either world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r4.anchor: اجعل نفسك قرين ذكر الله تعالى حتى لا تبعد عنه في الدارين

RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r5.claim: In a report, Abu Bakr refuses to separate Muhammad’s name from God’s on a ring; Gabriel says God likewise honored Abu Bakr’s wish, teaching the value of constant remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141/r5.anchor: أما اسم أبي بكر فكتبته أنا لأنه ما رضي أن يفرق اسمك عن اسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r1.claim: Noah found rescue using half the formula on the ark, so the author hopes lifelong recitation of the whole formula also brings salvation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r1.anchor: أن نوحا عليه السلام لما ركب السفينة

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r2.claim: Solomon gained worldly and otherworldly kingship through Bismillah, so a servant who recites it may gain both.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r2.anchor: أن سليمان عليه السلام نال مملكة الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r3.claim: One explanation is that Bilqīs herself says the letter is from Solomon, then identifies Bismillah after opening it; thus Solomon did not place himself before God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r3.anchor: من كلام بلقيس لا كلام سليمان

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that Solomon wrote his name on the letter’s outside and began the inside with Bismillah, which Bilqīs read in that order.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r4.anchor: لعل سليمان كتب على عنوان الكتاب إنه من سليمان وفي داخل الكتاب ابتدأ

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r5.claim: A third explanation says Solomon put his name first because he feared the unbelieving Bilqīs might insult God if His name appeared first.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r5.anchor: أن بلقيس كانت كافرة فخاف سليمان أن تشتم الله إذا نظرت في الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r6.claim: The initial bāʾ is linked to al-Barr: God’s greatest beneficence is granting believers the vision of Him on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r6.anchor: الباء من بسم مشتق من البر فهو البار على المؤمنين بأنواع الكرامات في الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r7.claim: A story tells of a Jewish neighbor who accepted Islam because he longed to see God; in a dream he says God forgave him for converting out of that longing.

RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r8.claim: The letter sīn is linked to God’s name al-Samīʿ, who hears every creature’s prayer from the Throne to beneath the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v1p141#2/r8.anchor: وأما السين فهو مشتق من اسمه السميع يسمع دعاء الخلق من العرش إلى ما تحت الثرى

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r1.claim: A tale says Zayd ibn Ḥāritha called on al-Raḥmān when a hypocrite bound him to kill him; successive warnings culminated in Gabriel freeing Zayd and killing the attacker.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r1.anchor: يا رحمن أغثني فسمع المنافق صوتا

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r2.claim: The mīm is associated with God’s dominion extending from the Throne to everything beneath the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r2.anchor: وأما الميم فمعناه أن من العرش إلى ما تحت الثرى ملكه وملكه

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r3.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r3.claim: During drought under Solomon, an ant prayed for God’s favor for His creatures, rain came, and Solomon told people to return because another’s prayer had been answered.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r3.anchor: قال السدي : أصاب الناس قحط على عهد سليمان

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r4.claim: A devotee says he will call on God throughout life, in the grave, at resurrection, while receiving the record, at the scales and bridge, in Paradise, and on seeing God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r4.anchor: أما قوله الله فاعلموا أيها الناس أني أقول طول حياتي الله فإذا مت أقول الله وإذا سئلت في القبر أقول الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r5.claim: The three names correspond to three Qur’anic classes: Allah for those foremost in good, al-Raḥmān for the moderate, and al-Raḥīm for the self-wronging.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r5.anchor: فقال أنا الله للسابقين الرحمن للمقتصدين الرحيم للظالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r6.claim: Another gloss says Allah gives gifts, al-Raḥmān overlooks the slips of the saints, and al-Raḥīm overlooks their discourtesy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r6.anchor: الله هو معطي العطاء والرحمن هو المتجاوز عن زلات الأولياء والرحيم هو المتجاوز عن الجفاء

RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r7.claim: God knows hidden faults that would alienate family, spouse, servant, or neighbor, yet conceals them through His generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p142/r7.anchor: وأنا أعلم كل ذمك وأستره بكرمي لتعلم أني إله كريم

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r1.claim: A report promises that honoring a paper bearing Bismillah earns the rank of the truthful and lightens one’s parents’ burden even if they were polytheists.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r1.anchor: من رفع قرطاسا من الأرض فيه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم إجلالا له تعالى كتب عند الله من الصديقين

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits instructions to say Bismillah at ablution, intercourse, mounting, and boarding a ship, with good deeds counted through each act and even descendants’ breaths.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r2.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r3.claim: Anas reports that saying Bismillah al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm while undressing shields people from jinn; Rāzī asks whether it will not also shield them from hell’s guards.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r3.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r4.claim: In a story, Umar sends Caesar a cap with Bismillah inside; wearing it relieves Caesar’s headache, which returns when he removes it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r4.anchor: كتب قيصر إلى عمر رضي الله عنه أن بي صداعا لا يسكن فابعث لي دواء

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r5.claim: A report says invoking God’s name in ablution purifies the whole body, while invoking Him from the heart should purify the heart of unbelief and innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r5.anchor: السابعة عشرة : قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r6.claim: A story says Khalid ibn al-Walīd ate deadly poison after invoking Bismillah and survived by God’s permission, prompting the Magians to accept Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143/r6.anchor: إنك تدعي الإسلام فأرنا آية لنسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r1.claim: Jesus sees a sinner’s punishment replaced by mercy after the man’s child learns Bismillah; God says He is ashamed to punish below ground while His name is remembered above.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r1.anchor: فاستحييت من عبدي أن أعذبه بناري في بطن الأرض وولده يذكر اسمي على وجه الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r2.speaker: عمرة الفرغانية
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r2.claim: ʿUmra al-Farghāniyya explains that menstruating women and the ritually impure may be barred from Qur’an recitation but not from Bismillah, since a beloved is not barred from remembering the beloved.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r2.anchor: لأن التسمية ذكر اسم الحبيب والحبيب لا يمنع من ذكر الحبيب

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r3.claim: A gloss says al-Raḥīm shows mercy in six fearful stages: the grave, resurrection, scales, record, bridge, and Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r3.anchor: الرحيم هو تعالى رحيم بهم في ستة مواضع

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r4.claim: A knower puts Bismillah in his shroud so he can ask God to treat him according to the title of His book.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r4.anchor: بعثت كتابا وجعلت عنوانه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فعاملني بعنوان كتابك

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r5.claim: The formula’s nineteen letters are said to fend off the nineteen guardians of Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r5.anchor: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم تسعة عشر حرفا

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r6.claim: A second claim says its nineteen letters expiate sins committed during the nineteen hours left after five daily prayer hours are subtracted from twenty-four.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r6.anchor: خلق الله تعالى الليل والنهار أربعة وعشرين ساعة ثم فرض خمس صلوات في خمس ساعات

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r7.claim: Sūrat al-Tawba lacks Bismillah because it commands fighting; slaughter uses a shorter formula because naming mercy is unsuitable to killing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r7.anchor: لما كانت سورة التوبة مشتملة على الأمر بالقتال لم يكتب في أولها بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r8.claim: Reciting the merciful formula seventeen times daily in obligatory prayers indicates that God created people for mercy, favor, and beneficence rather than killing and punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p143#2/r8.anchor: فلما وفقك لذكر هذه الكلمة في كل يوم سبع عشرة مرة في الصلوات المفروضة دل ذلك على أنه ما خلقك للقتل والعذاب

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r1.speaker: ابن دريد
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r1.claim: Ibn Durayd says umm can mean a banner; the Fātiḥa is the believers’ rallying point as a banner is an army’s, while earth is called mother because all return to it and umm can mean a destination.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r1.anchor: الأم في كلام العرب الراية التي ينصبها العسكر

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r2.claim: One explanation of al-sabʿ al-mathānī is that half the sura is the servant’s praise and half God’s gift to the servant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r2.anchor: نصفها ثناء العبد للرب ونصفها عطاء الرب للعبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r3.claim: Another explanation is that it is repeated in every prayer cycle.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r3.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها تثنى في كل ركعة من الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says no comparable sura occurs in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur’an, and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r4.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام صلى الله عليه وسلم : والذي نفسي بيده ما أنزل في التوراة

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r5.claim: A further explanation says each of its seven verses equals the recitation of seven portions of the Qur’an, so reciting it earns the reward of reciting all of it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r5.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها سبع آيات كل آية تعدل قراءتها قراءة سبع من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r6.speaker: جبريل
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r6.claim: Gabriel says the seven verses overlay Hell’s seven gates, so reciters pass them safely; he had feared punishment before the Fātiḥa was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r6.anchor: روي أن جبريل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r7.claim: It is called the oft-repeated because it is recited in prayer and then followed by another sura.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r7.anchor: لأنها تقرأ في الصلاة ثم إنها تثنى بسورة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r8.claim: Another explanation takes mathānī as praises and commendations of God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r8.anchor: سميت مثاني لأنها أثنية على الله تعالى ومدائح له

RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r9.claim: A final explanation says God revealed the sura twice, which is why it is called oft-repeated.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146/r9.anchor: سميت مثاني لأن الله أنزلها مرتين

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r1.claim: It is called the Foundation because it is the first sura, contains the noblest aims, and is indispensable to prayer, the greatest worship after faith.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r1.anchor: أنها أول سورة من القرآن فهي كالأساس

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r2.claim: The Prophet calls the Fātiḥa healing from every poison; a companion’s recitation cured an epileptic, and the Prophet also calls it healing from every disease.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r2.anchor: أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r3.claim: Rāzī explains the healing spiritually and physically: since unbelief is called a disease, the sura’s theology, duties, and spiritual unveilings heal all three domains.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r3.anchor: والدليل عليه أنه تعالى سمى الكفر مرضا

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r4.claim: It is called prayer because God says He divided the prayer between Himself and His servant in two halves, meaning this sura.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r4.anchor: الاسم التاسع : الصلاة قال عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r5.claim: A report says whoever is occupied with remembering God rather than asking receives more than those who ask; Abraham models praise followed by requests.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r5.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حكى عن رب العزة سبحانه وتعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r6.claim: Because the sura moves from praise to worship to a request for guidance, it teaches that religious guidance is the highest aim and the garden of knowledge surpasses the garden of pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أكمل المطالب هو الهداية في الدين وهو أيضا يدل على أن جنة المعرفة خير من جنة النعيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r7.claim: It is called the Sura of Gratitude because it praises God for His favor, generosity, and beneficence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r7.anchor: سورة الشكر وذلك لأنها ثناء على الله بالفضل والكرم والإحسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p146#2/r8.claim: It is called the Sura of Supplication because it includes the request for the straight path.

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Fātiḥa descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne; al-Thaʿlabī says most scholars agree.
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r1.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r2.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r2.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurayḥil says the first revelation was al-Ḥamd lillāh; after Muhammad confided his fear to Khadīja and consulted Waraqa, Gabriel instructed him to recite Bismillah and the Fātiḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r2.anchor: وروى أيضا بإسناده عن عمرو بن شرحبيل

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r3.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet recited Bismillah and Quraysh cursed him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r3.anchor: وبإسناده عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r4.claim: Mujāhid says it descended in Medina, but Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl rejects this as a lapse against scholarly consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r4.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن مجاهد أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r5.speaker: حسين بن الفضل
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r5.claim: Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl argues that the Meccan Sūrat al-Ḥijr already refers to the seven oft-repeated verses and that it is implausible for the Prophet to live in Mecca over a decade without the Fātiḥa.

RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r6.claim: A third view holds that the sura descended once in Mecca and again in Medina, its double revelation explaining its honorific name al-mathānī.
RAZI-FULL:v1p147/r6.anchor: هذه السورة نزلت بمكة مرة وبالمدينة مرة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports from the Prophet that the Fātiḥa heals poison.
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r2.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r2.claim: Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān reports that a child’s recitation of al-Ḥamd lillāh during a destined calamity leads God to lift it for forty years.

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r3.speaker: الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r3.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says knowledge flowed from 104 heavenly books through the four major books and the Qur’an until it was concentrated in the Fātiḥa, whose interpretation equals knowledge of all revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r3.anchor: أنزل الله تعالى مائة وأربعة كتب من السماء فأودع علوم المائة في الأربعة وهي التوراة والإنجيل والزبور والفرقان

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r4.claim: Rāzī explains that the Fātiḥa contains all divine aims because it fully treats theology, religious practice, and spiritual unveiling.
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r4.anchor: والسبب فيه أن المقصود من جميع الكتب الإلهية علم الأصول والفروع والمكاشفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r5.claim: The sura omits seven letters associated with torment: thāʾ with ruin, jīm with Hell, khāʾ with disgrace, zāy and shīn with breath, the tree or misery, ẓāʾ with shade and blazing fire, and fāʾ with separation or falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r5.anchor: أن هذه الحروف السبعة مشعرة بالعذاب فالثاء تدل على الويل والثبور

RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r6.claim: Rāzī answers that, although all letters can occur in words about punishment, these seven omitted initials correspond to Hell’s seven gates; understanding the sura protects readers from them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p148/r6.anchor: والله تعالى أسقط سبعة من الحروف من هذه السورة وهي أوائل ألفاظ دالة على العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i says the basmala is a verse of al-Fatiha and must be read; Malik and al-Awza'i exclude it except in the Quran's Naml passage, with a Ramadan-night exception, while Abu Hanifa orders quiet recitation without stating its status.
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r5.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية من أول سورة الفاتحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r6.speaker: يعلى
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r6.claim: The narrator reports asking Muhammad b. al-Hasan whether the basmala is Quran, introducing a discussion of its legal status.
RAZI-FULL:v1p160/r6.anchor: قال يعلى سألت محمد بن الحسن عن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فقال

RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr calls the basmala's Quranic status categorical: error is at least sinful, since its inclusion must be proved by mass transmission, not a solitary report.
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.anchor: وزعم القاضي أبو بكر أنها من المسائل القطعية قال : والخطأ فيها إن لم يبلغ إلى حد التكفير

RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali counters that denying the basmala's Quranic status faces the same proof dilemma; although absence is the default, its Quranic-script inscription requires separate evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.anchor: واعلم أن الشيخ الغزالي عارض القاضي فقال : نفي كون التسمية من القرآن إن ثبت بالتواتر

RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.claim: Razi says transmission establishes that the basmala was revealed to Muhammad and written in Quranic script; inclusion matters only for legal rulings such as prayer, recitation in impurity, and touching the codex, which are ijtihadi, so the issue is not categorical.
RAZI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.anchor: والذي عندي فيه أن النقل المتواتر ثابت بأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم كلام أنزله الله على محمد

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r1.claim: Razi calls the report from Umm Salama an explicit text supporting the basmala inclusion in al-Fatiha.

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha while counting the basmala as its first verse, followed by the rest of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: روى الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن مسلم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن أم سلمة أنها قالت

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r3.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet saying that al-Fatiha has seven verses and the first is the basmala.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r3.anchor: روى سعيد المقبري عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : فاتحة الكتاب سبع آيات أولاهن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r4.speaker: أبو بريدة عن أبيه عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r4.claim: In al-Tha'labi's report, the Prophet tells Abu Burda that he alone after Solomon received an ayah, then links it to the basmala used to begin Quran recitation and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r4.anchor: روى الثعلبي في تفسيره بإسناده عن أبي بريدة عن أبيه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the seven oft-repeated verses as al-Fatiha and answers that its seventh verse is the basmala.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r5.anchor: فأين السابعة ؟ فقال : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r1.claim: A report from Abu Huraira says the Prophet told believers not to omit the basmala when reciting the Mother of the Book because it is one of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r1.anchor: أنه قال إذا : قرأتم أم القرآن فلا تدعوا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فإنها إحدى آياتها

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: In the divided-prayer report, God calls the basmala glorification, al-Hamd praise, the two mercy names extolling, the Master of Judgment entrustment, and the remaining response a sharing and a request granted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: فإذا قال العبد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله سبحانه مجدني عبدي وإذا قال الحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r3.claim: Another report says the Prophet rebuked a worshipper who began al-Fatiha without the basmala: omitting a verse cuts the prayer, which is invalid without the whole surah.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r3.anchor: يا رجل قطعت على نفسك الصلاة أما علمت أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من الحمد

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever omits the basmala has omitted a verse from God's Book.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r1.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : من ترك بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.claim: Razi argues that if reading the basmala at the start of al-Fatiha is obligatory, it must be one of its verses; Quran 96:1 commands reading in God's name and the letter has meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r2.anchor: بيان الأول قوله تعالى : ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ [ العلق : 1 ] ولا يجوز أن يقال : الباء صلة زائدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.claim: Because the basmala is written in Quranic script, while headings and division marks were kept out to prevent mixing non-Quranic text, its inscription marks it as Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r3.anchor: التسمية مكتوبة بخط القرآن وكل ما ليس من القرآن فإنه غير مكتوب بخط القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.claim: Since Muslims agree that everything between the two covers is God's speech and the basmala is there, Razi counts it as divine speech; he notes this does not refute Abu Bakr al-Razi's view that it is Quran only as a surah divider.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r4.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أن ما بين الدفتين كلام الله والتسمية موجودة بين الدفتين

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.claim: The seven-verse count supports al-Shafi'i's division, with the basmala as one verse and the final phrase as one; Abu Hanifa denies the basmala verse and splits that final phrase, a weak view for Razi.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.anchor: وسنبين في مسألة مفردة أن قول أبي حنيفة مرجوح ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.claim: Because Abu Hanifa agrees the basmala is preferable and the Prophet likely recited it, following him makes it obligatory; with no accepted distinction, it must be part of al-Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r6.anchor: وإذا ثبت وجوب قراءتها ثبت أنها من السورة لأنه لا قائل بالفرق

RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: The Prophet's saying that an important matter begun without God's name is cut off implies that prayer, the greatest act after faith, is gravely deficient without the basmala; such acknowledged deficiency entails invalidity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر أو أجذم

RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r2.claim: The severity of abtar is shown by Quran 108:3, where God calls the Prophet's enemy cut off; thus prayer without the basmala is gravely defective and invalid.
RAZI-FULL:v1p163/r2.anchor: فلزم أن يقال : الصلاة الخالية عن قراءة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم تكون في غاية النقصان والخلل

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r1.claim: When Ubayy b. Ka'b names the basmala as the greatest ayah and the Prophet confirms him, Razi argues it must be a complete ayah somewhere other than its partial appearance in Solomon's letter, namely at al-Fatiha's start.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r1.anchor: ما روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب : ما اعظم آية في كتاب الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r2.claim: When Muawiya omitted the basmala aloud in prayer, the Migrants and Helpers rebuked him and he repeated the prayer; Razi takes this as Companion consensus that it is Quran and part of al-Fatiha, and that aloud recitation is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r2.anchor: فلما قضى صلاته ناداه المهاجرون والأنصار من كل ناحية أنسيت ؟ أين بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حين استفتحت القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r3.claim: Razi argues that Noah began boarding the Ark in God's name and Solomon's letter began with the basmala; following earlier prophets and then the Prophet makes its recitation obligatory for Muslims and part of al-Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r3.anchor: أن نوحا عليه السلام لما أراد ركوب السفينة قال : ﴿ اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r4.claim: Razi rejects the suggestion that Solomon put his own name before God's: the hoopoe laid the letter on the queen, who first identified its sender as Solomon and only after opening it read the basmala.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r4.anchor: فلما فتحت الكتاب رأت التسمية مكتوبة فقالت : وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r5.claim: Since God exists before all created things, rational propriety requires mentioning Him before others; what Muslims deem good is good before God, so the basmala should precede recitation and belongs to al-Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r5.anchor: والقديم الخالق يجب أن يكون سابقا على المحدث المخلوق وإذا ثبت أنه تعالى سابق على غيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r6.claim: Because the basmala unquestionably appears in Quran 27:30 and recurs in Quranic script, Razi argues every occurrence is Quran, by analogy with repeated Quranic refrains.
RAZI-FULL:v1p164/r6.anchor: أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لا شك أنه من القرآن في سورة النمل ثم إنا نراه مكررا بخط القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r1.claim: A report traces the written invocation from Quraysh’s باسمك اللهم through successive revealed forms until the full basmala was written after the verse in al-Naml.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r1.anchor: إنه من سليمان وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r2.claim: Because every component and the complete formula occur in Qur’anic revelation, its established fame and many proofs make exclusion an attack on the reliability of the rest of the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r2.anchor: أجزاء هذه الكلمة كلها من القرآن ومجموعها من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r3.claim: Mass transmission establishes that God revealed the formula and commanded its inscription in the codex; the dispute therefore concerns legal consequences such as reciting it and touching it while impure.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r3.anchor: ثبت بالتواتر أن الله تعالى كان ينزل هذه الكلمة على محمد

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r4.claim: Since inclusion settles disputed ritual rules more cautiously, he favors it under the Prophetic maxim to leave doubtful matters for secure ones.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r4.anchor: ثبوت هذه الأحكام أحوط فوجب المصير إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r5.claim: The report of prayer divided between God and the servant omits the basmala; opponents infer that it is not a verse of al-Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r5.anchor: قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فإذا قال العبد الحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r6.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r6.claim: Opponents identify the divided prayer with al-Fatiha: without the basmala its seven verses divide three-and-a-half to each side, whereas counting it gives God four-and-a-half and the servant two-and-a-half.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165/r6.anchor: التنصيف إنما يحصل إذا قلنا إن التسمية ليست آية من الفاتحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet began prayer with the takbir and recitation of al-Fatiha, which opponents take to show the basmala is not one of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r1.anchor: كان يفتتح الصلاة بالتكبير والقراءة بالحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r2.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r2.claim: Opponents argue that counting the basmala as a verse repeats الرحمن الرحيم within the sura, contrary to the evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r2.anchor: لزم التكرار في قوله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r3.claim: Al-Tha‘labi transmits a version in which the Prophet counted the basmala as a complete verse of al-Fatiha; when reports conflict, affirmation outweighs omission.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r3.anchor: رواية الإثبات مقدمة على رواية النفي

RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r4.claim: A variant transmitted by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani says God calls Malik yawm al-din a point between Himself and the servant, which supports three verses on either side when the basmala is counted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r4.anchor: إذا قال العبد مالك يوم الدين يقول الله تعالى مجدني عبدي

RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r5.claim: Half can describe a division of meaning rather than an exact count, as in calling inheritance law half of knowledge or saying half the people are angry.
RAZI-FULL:v1p165#2/r5.anchor: لفظ النصف كما يحتمل النصف في عدد الآيات فهو أيضا يحتمل النصف في المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r1.claim: The report’s examples show that half may describe a conceptual division: inheritance law concerns the dead, while life and death are two categories; Shurayh similarly calls half the people angry when some are pleased and others displeased.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r1.anchor: الفرائض نصف العلم وسماه بالنصف من حيث أنه بحث عن أحوال الأموات

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r2.claim: The explicit proofs that the basmala is in al-Fatiha outweigh a report whose purpose is another point; caution also favors his position.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r2.anchor: دلائلنا في أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية من الفاتحة صريحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r3.claim: Al-Shafi‘i explains Aisha’s phrase al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin as a title for the entire sura, not only its opening words.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r3.anchor: جعلت الحمد لله رب العالمين اسما لهذه السورة

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r4.claim: Repetition for emphasis is common in the Qur’an, and reaffirming that God is merciful is especially important.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r4.anchor: التكرار لأجل التأكيد كثير في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r5.claim: A rare report has al-Hasan al-Basri count al-Fatiha as eight verses, while the well-known view accepted by most counts seven and identifies them with the seven oft-repeated verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r5.anchor: في بعض الروايات الشاذة أن الحسن البصري كان يقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r6.claim: Those counting the basmala treat the final phrase from sirat alladhina through the end as one verse; Abu Hanifa, omitting the basmala, splits that ending into two verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r6.anchor: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين آية تامة

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r7.claim: Al-Shafi‘i’s count is preferable: the pause after an‘amta ‘alayhim does not match the sura’s verse endings, and verse endings elsewhere are either near-rhyming or matching.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r7.anchor: مقطع قوله صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم لا يشابه مقطع الآيات المتقدمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r8.claim: Starting a verse with ghayr separates a modifier or exception from what it qualifies, though each belongs syntactically with the preceding phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r8.anchor: هذا اللفظ إما أن يكون صفة لما قبله أو استثناء عما قبله

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r9.claim: The request to guide us to the path of the blessed is incomplete without excluding those under anger or astray; the whole qualified phrase should therefore be one verse.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r9.anchor: ما لم يضم إليه قوله غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين لم يصح قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r10.claim: Unlike the incomplete guidance request, al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin is a complete sentence by itself, so it can be a verse before الرحمن الرحيم.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r10.anchor: الحمد لله رب العالمين كلام تام بدون قوله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r11.claim: The leading authorities among al-Shafi‘i’s followers agree the basmala is Qur’an in every sura; their two opinions concern whether it is a full verse alone or joined to what follows.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r11.anchor: اتفقوا على أن بسم الله قرآن من سائر السور

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r12.claim: Some Hanafis accuse al-Shafi‘i of dissenting from consensus on the basmala at every sura’s opening; Razi answers that its Qur’anic-script placement in the codex proves it is Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r12.anchor: بسم الله مكتوب في أوائل السور بخط القرآن فوجب كونه قرآنا

RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r13.claim: Razi opens the objection concerning basmala verse status by citing Abu Hurayra’s report about the verse count of al-Mulk.
RAZI-FULL:v1p166/r13.anchor: واحتج المخالف بما روى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في سورة الملك

RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r1.claim: The verse-count objection disappears if the basmala and the words after it form one verse; a complete verse in al-Fatiha can be part of a longer verse elsewhere, and al-Kawthar’s count covers its distinctive content.
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r1.anchor: إذا قلنا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم مع ما بعده آية واحدة فهذا الإشكال زائل

RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r2.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r2.claim: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is reported to count the basmala as a verse of al-Fatiha while reciting it quietly in every rak‘a; al-Shafi‘i counts it and recites aloud, while Abu Hanifa does not count it but reads it quietly.
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r2.anchor: التسمية آية من الفاتحة إلا أنه يسر بها في كل ركعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r3.claim: Razi holds loud recitation to be Sunna: if the sura is recited aloud, its opening basmala should be too, rather than making only part of a sura audible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r3.anchor: السورة الواحدة إما أن تكون بتمامها سرية أو جهرية

RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r4.claim: Because the basmala praises and glorifies God, making its remembrance public is fitting; the Qur’an commands abundant remembrance, as one would publicly honor a beloved father.
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r4.anchor: قوله بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لا شك أنه ثناء على الله وذكر له بالتعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r5.claim: Open remembrance publicly shows pride in honoring God and indifference to objection; reason commends that, supported by the reported maxim about what Muslims deem good.
RAZI-FULL:v1p167/r5.anchor: الجهر بذكر الله يدل على كونه مفتخرا بذلك الذكر غير مبال بإنكار من ينكره

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r1.claim: Concealment suits a defect, not the greatest honor of remembering God; reports praise dying with a tongue moist in remembrance and Ali’s saying that God’s mention ennobles those who remember Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r1.anchor: طوبى لمن مات ولسانه رطب من ذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r2.claim: Ali is reported to recite the basmala aloud in all prayers, a practice Razi says strongly confirms public recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r2.anchor: كان مذهبه الجهر ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم في جميع الصلوات

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r3.claim: Al-Shafi‘i reports that when Muawiya omitted the basmala and bowing and prostration takbirs in Medina, the Emigrants and Helpers protested and he repeated prayer with them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r3.anchor: ثم إنه أعاد الصلاة مع التسمية والتكبير

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r4.claim: Since Muawiya was powerful, the Companions’ public protest shows that aloud basmala recitation was established among them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r4.anchor: كان كالأمر المتقرر عند كل الصحابة من المهاجرين والأنصار

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r5.speaker: البيهقي
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits Abu Hurayra’s report that the Prophet recited the basmala aloud, and reports the same practice from Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Ibn al-Zubayr.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r5.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر في الصلاة ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r6.claim: Razi says Ali’s loud recitation is established by mass transmission; he cites the report asking God to keep truth with Ali wherever he turns.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168/r6.anchor: كان يجهر بالتسمية فقد ثبت بالتواتر

RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r1.claim: The implied verb with the basmala means beginning acts with God’s help; hearing it teaches dependence on divine protection from sin and aid for good, making its recitation a call to the best good rather than an innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r1.anchor: يتعلق بفعل لا بد من إضماره والتقدير بإعانة اسم الله اشرعوا في الطاعات

RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r2.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman began prayer with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin; Muslim versions say they did not mention, or were not heard saying, the basmala aloud.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r2.anchor: صليت خلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وخلف أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وكانوا يستفتحون القراءة بالحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن المغفل
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mughaffal says his father warned him against introducing the basmala, recalling that the Prophet and first three caliphs began with al-hamdu lillah.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r3.anchor: يا بني إياك والحدث في الإسلام فقد صليت خلف رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r4.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r4.claim: Opponents cite Qur’anic commands to invoke God humbly and remember Him inwardly as proof that the basmala should be quiet; jurists infer this from the verses and earlier reports.
RAZI-FULL:v1p168#2/r4.anchor: وبسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ذكر الله فوجب إخفاؤه

RAZI-FULL:v1p169/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169/r1.speaker: أبو حامد الإسفراييني
RAZI-FULL:v1p169/r1.claim: Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini groups six Anas reports: three support the Hanafi position by omitting the basmala, while three contrary reports recount the protest against Muawiya, loud recitation, or Anas’s uncertainty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169/r1.anchor: روي عن أنس في هذا الباب ست روايات أما الحنفية فقد رووا عنه ثلاث روايات

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.claim: Conflicting and unstable Anas reports leave the evidence balanced; possible Umayyad pressure against Ali’s practice may explain Anas’s hesitation, and Ali’s lifelong practice should prevail.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r1.anchor: عظم فيها الخبط والاضطراب فبقيت متعارضة

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.claim: If reports conflict, Razi prefers Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Hurayra over Anas and Ibn al-Mughaffal because they were more knowledgeable and closer to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.anchor: كانوا اكثر علما وقربا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.claim: Razi invokes Abu Hanifa’s refusal of solitary reports that oppose analogy: the evident rational case favors openly reciting a phrase that honors God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.anchor: خبر الواحد إذا ورد على خلاف القياس لم يقبل

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar were more learned and eminent than Anas and Ibn al-Mughaffal; their likely proximity, the Prophet’s moderate voice, and gradual increase in volume explain who heard the basmala.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.anchor: كانوا أعلى حالا في العلم والشرف وعلو الدرجة

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.claim: Al-Shafi‘i interprets Anas’s phrase that the Prophet began with al-hamdu lillah as saying al-Fatiha, named by its opening, came before other suras.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.anchor: أنه كان قدم هذه السورة في القراءة على غيرها من السور

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mughaffal’s denial of loud recitation can mean only that the Prophet did not raise his voice excessively, as instructed by the Qur’an; an affirmative report outweighs a negative one.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r6.anchor: عدم المبالغة في رفع الصوت كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r7.claim: The verses about inward remembrance concern simple recollection; reciting God’s revealed words as worship is a different act for which audible reading is preferable.

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r8.speaker: الشيعة
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r8.claim: The Shi‘a hold that the basmala should be recited aloud in both loud and quiet prayers; most jurists disagree.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r8.anchor: السنة هي الجهر بالتسمية سواء كانت في الصلاة الجهرية أو السرية

RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r9.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r9.claim: Those denying that the basmala is part of each sura offer two explanations for its codex placement: it separates suras, or it is Qur’an as an independent verse revealed at each opening or once for insertion throughout.
RAZI-FULL:v1p169#2/r9.anchor: اختلفوا في سبب إثباتها في المصحف في أول كل سورة وفيه قولان

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r1.speaker: أم سلمة
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as a verse marking the separation between suras.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r1.anchor: كان يعد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية فاصلة

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r2.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r2.claim: Amr ibn Dinar rebukes al-Fadl al-Raqashi for claiming the basmala is not Qur’an, since it marks the end of one sura and start of another.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r2.anchor: علم أن تلك السورة قد ختمت وفتح غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak says omitting the basmala omits 113 verses; similar statements are attributed to Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayra.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r3.anchor: فقد ترك مائة وثلاث عشرة آية

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r4.claim: For those who do not count the basmala as a verse of al-Fatiha, Abu Hanifa and several other jurists require it quietly; Malik forbids it in obligatory prayer but permits a choice in voluntary prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r4.anchor: يقرأ التسمية سرا وقال مالك : لا ينبغي أن يقرأها في المكتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r5.claim: Al-Shafi‘i’s position entails reading the basmala in every rak‘a; Abu Hanifa is reported both to require it before al-Fatiha in every rak‘a and to require it only at the start of the prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r5.anchor: مذهب الشافعي يقتضي وجوب قراءتها في كل الركعات

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r6.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r6.claim: Al-Shafi‘i prefers repeating the basmala before every sura, citing the report that an important matter begun without it is cut off.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r6.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه ببسم الله فهو أبتر

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r7.claim: Razi’s school holds that a menstruating woman or a person in major ritual impurity may not recite the basmala.

RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r8.claim: Scholars agree that invoking God in ablution is recommended, and most do not require it because the ablution verse omits it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p170/r8.anchor: تسمية الله على الوضوء مندوبة وعامة العلماء على أنها غير واجبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r1.speaker: أهل الظاهر
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r1.claim: Literalists require the basmala in ablution, while Ishaq invalidates ablution for deliberate omission but excuses forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r1.anchor: قال أهل الظاهر إنها واجبة فلو تركها عمدا أو سهوا

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r2.claim: Whether meat from an animal slaughtered without the basmala is lawful is a famous dispute, with Qur’anic commands both to invoke God over offerings and not eat what was not named over.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r2.anchor: متروك التسمية عند التذكية هل يحل أكله أم لا

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r3.claim: Scholars recommend beginning every activity with the basmala, from sleep and waking to worship, entering and leaving home, eating, drinking, giving, and receiving; they also recommend it at birth, death, burial, resurrection, and the gathering.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r3.anchor: يستحب أن لا يشرع في عمل من الأعمال وإلا ويقول بسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r4.claim: The basmala at the gathering is said to distance the fire from the speaker by its blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r4.anchor: فتتباعد عنه النار ببركة قوله بسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r5.claim: Razi rejects translated Qur’an as sufficient for prayer for both able and unable reciters; Abu Hanifa allows it for either, while Abu Yusuf and Muhammad allow it only for the unable.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r5.anchor: ترجمة القرآن لا تكفي في صحة الصلاة لا في حق من يحسن القراءة

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r6.claim: Razi calls Abu Hanifa’s view far from sound; al-Samarqandi and al-Dabusi explicitly abandoned it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r6.anchor: مذهب أبي حنيفة في هذه المسألة بعيد جدا

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r7.claim: The Prophet prayed using the revealed Arabic Qur’an throughout his life, so believers must follow that practice; Razi notes the irony that Abu Hanifa treats habitual head-wiping as a condition but not habitual Arabic recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r7.anchor: إنما صلى بالقرآن المنزل من عند الله تعالى باللفظ العربي وواظب عليه طول عمره

RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r8.claim: The rightly guided caliphs prayed with Arabic Qur’an, so their practice binds believers under commands to follow Abu Bakr and Umar and the caliphs’ Sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v1p171/r8.anchor: أن الخلفاء الراشدين صلوا بالقرآن العربي فوجب أن يجب علينا ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r1.claim: The Prophet and Companions recited only Arabic in prayer; the saved group follows their practice. Muslims throughout Islamic lands agree on Arabic recitation, and departing from believers’ way is condemned.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r1.anchor: وجميع أصحابه كانوا متفقين على القراءة في الصلاة بهذا القرآن العربي

RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r2.claim: Prayer requires Qur’an recitation, and Persian words are not Qur’an: revelation is in clear Arabic, messengers speak their people’s language, and the challenge to produce its like would be contradicted if a Persian rendering counted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172/r2.anchor: إن الكلام المرتب بالفارسية ليس بقرآن لوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits Abu Hurayra’s report that prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening; a Persian rendering is either called Qur’an, which Razi deems ignorant and contrary to consensus, or not Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r1.anchor: لا تجزي صلاة لا يقرأ فيها بفاتحة الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r2.claim: When a man could not recite Qur’an, the Prophet taught him glorification, praise, and takbir instead of a translation, showing the alternative for inability.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r2.anchor: إني لا أستطيع أن أحفظ القرآن كما يحسن في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r3.claim: If Qur’an could be translated as Qur’an, Christians could claim its opening was copied from the Gospel’s matching formula; no one makes that claim.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r3.anchor: أول الإنجيل هو قوله بسم إلاها رحمانا ومرحيانا

RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r4.claim: A Persian rendering of the cave passage or insults and requests becomes ordinary human speech, barred in prayer; the Arabic original remains distinct through its miraculous arrangement.
RAZI-FULL:v1p172#2/r4.anchor: من جنس كلام الناس لفظا ومعنى فوجب أن لا تجوز الصلاة به

RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r1.claim: If every language’s translation were Qur’an, revelation would have more than the seven canonical forms, contradicting the report that it came in seven forms.
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r1.anchor: أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف كلها شاف كاف

RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r2.claim: The Hanafi principle would also validate prayer with matching verses from Torah, Gospel, or ordinary writings, an outcome Razi says is alien to Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r2.anchor: الصلاة صحيحة بقراءة الإنجيل والتوراة وبقراءة زيد وإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r3.claim: A translation of al-Fatiha reduces it to generic praise found in any sermon; allowing this would make prayer valid with all sermons, an unacceptable result.
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r3.anchor: لا خطبة إلا وقد حصل فيها هذا القدر فوجب أن يقال الصلاة صحيحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r4.claim: If translation were permitted, the Prophet would have authorized Persians, Romans, and Ethiopians to pray in their languages; such a popular, easier permission would have spread and erased the Arabic Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r4.anchor: قد أذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لسلمان الفارسي في أن يقرأ القرآن بالفارسية

RAZI-FULL:v1p173/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
