WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r5.claim: The written alif is dropped from bism Allāh because the familiar phrase is unmistakable and Arabic favors brevity when meaning is clear; unlike the less frequent formula in al-Wāqiʿa, al-Ḥāqqa.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r5.anchor: وحذفت الألف من بسم الله؛ لأنها وقعت (¬3) في موضع معروف، لا يجهل القارئ معناها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r6.claim: The alif remains when ism is attached to something other than God or when a different preposition precedes it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r6.anchor: ولا تحذف الألف إذا أضيف (الاسم) إلى غير (¬5) الله، ولا مع غير الباء من الحروف،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r7.claim: The alif is also absent in pronunciation because it is a connecting hamza, for which the preceding bāʾ suffices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p436/r7.anchor: هذا في سقوطها في الكتابة، وأما سقوطها # في اللفظ، فلأنها (¬1) للوصل، وقد استغنى عنها بالباء

WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r1.claim: The formula begins or opens by naming God, seeking blessing and good auspices.
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r1.anchor: أي أبدؤوا أو افتتحوا بتسمية الله تيمنا وتبركا

WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r2.claim: Allah is a name unique to the Creator, functioning like a proper name and having no known derivation.
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r2.anchor: و الله اسم تفرد الباري به سبحانه يجري في وصفه مجرى أسماء الأعلام لا يعرف له اشتقاق

WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r3.claim: One reported derivation understands Allah as the possessor of worship by which the All-Merciful is sought.
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه ذو العبادة التي بها يقصد الرحمن الرحيم

WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r4.claim: The two divine names mean possessing mercy: mercy is God's abiding will of good, and the names differ in form, not meaning.
WAHIDI-QT:1:1/r4.anchor: الرحمن الرحيم صفتان لله تعالى معناهما ذو الرحمة أي الرحمة لازمة له وهي إرادة الخير ولا فرق بينهما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r1.claim: The basmala directs people to begin by naming God, seeking blessing through it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r1.anchor: ابدؤوا أو افتتحوا بتسمية الله تيمنا وتبركا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r2.claim: Allah is God's unique proper name, functioning like a proper name among His names, with no known derivation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r2.anchor: اسم تفرد الباري به سبحانه، يجري في وصفه مجرى أسماء الأعلام، لا يعرف له اشتقاق.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r3.claim: An alternative explanation derives Allah's meaning from being the one worshipped and sought through worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه: ذو العبادة التي بها يقصد.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.claim: The two divine attributes mean possessing mercy, an abiding divine quality understood as willing good; the names do not differ in meaning, like nadmān and nadīm.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:1-4/r4.anchor: وهي إرادة الخير، ولا فرق بينهما، مثل: ندمان ونديم.

ELMALILI:1:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r1.claim: The basmala in 27:30 is plainly part of that verse and certainly Qurʾān by explicit, unanimously established transmission; surah-opening basmalas raise a separate question.
ELMALILI:1:1/r1.anchor: Sûre-i Neml’in bu âyetinin bir cüz’ü olduğu kemâl-i sarâhatle mâlumdur

ELMALILI:1:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r2.claim: Whether the basmala written before surahs is a verse within them, a verse-part, or an independent Qurʾānic unit is a scholarly issue tied to faith, prayer, and recitation.
ELMALILI:1:1/r2.anchor: bu besmelenin ta‘yîn-i Kur’ânîsi tefsirde ve ilm-i usûlde bir mes’ele-i ilmiye teşkil etmiştir

ELMALILI:1:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r3.speaker: Saîd b. Cübeyr, Zührî, Atâ, İbn Mübârek
ELMALILI:1:1/r3.claim: These early authorities hold that every surah-opening basmala is one verse of that surah, yielding 113 such verses in the Qurʾān.
ELMALILI:1:1/r3.anchor: Saîd b. Cübeyr, Zührî, Atâ, İbn Mübârek hazerâtı besmelenin başında bulunduğu her sûreden birer âyet

ELMALILI:1:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r4.speaker: İmam Şâfiî ve ashâbı
ELMALILI:1:1/r4.claim: In his later position al-Shāfiʿī and his followers adopt the view that each surah-opening basmala is a verse.
ELMALILI:1:1/r4.anchor: Kavl-i cedîdinde İmam Şâfiî hazretleri ve ashâbı bu mezheb üzerindedirler

ELMALILI:1:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r5.claim: On this view the basmala is al-Fātiḥa’s first verse, while anʿamta ʿalayhim is not a verse ending, so they recite the basmala aloud in prayer.
ELMALILI:1:1/r5.anchor: O hâlde Fâtiha’nın yedi âyetinden birincisi besmeledir

ELMALILI:1:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r6.claim: Their argument is that the early community wrote the basmalas in the muṣḥafs while preserving the Qurʾān’s purity and excluding even Āmīn.
ELMALILI:1:1/r6.anchor: selef bu besmeleleri mushaflarda tesbit etmişler, bununla beraber Kur’ân’ın tecrîdini tavsiye eylemişler

ELMALILI:1:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r7.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:1:1/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says that omitting the basmala omits 114 verses from God’s Book.
ELMALILI:1:1/r7.anchor: Besmele’yi terk eden Kitâbullah’dan yüz on dört âyet terk etmiş olur

ELMALILI:1:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r8.speaker: Ebû Hüreyre
ELMALILI:1:1/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet counted al-Fātiḥa as seven verses and named the basmala as its first.
ELMALILI:1:1/r8.anchor: Fâtihatü’l-Kitâb yedi âyettir, bunların evveli بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ

ELMALILI:1:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r9.speaker: Ümmü Seleme
ELMALILI:1:1/r9.claim: A report from Umm Salama says the Prophet counted the basmala together with al-ḥamdu lillāh as one verse.
ELMALILI:1:1/r9.anchor: Resûlullah Fâtiha’yı okudu ve بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ’i bir âyet saydı

ELMALILI:1:1/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r10.claim: The Shāfiʿī argument concludes that even if the basmala is not a whole verse of al-Fātiḥa, it is part of a verse, making its recitation obligatory and audible in prayer.
ELMALILI:1:1/r10.anchor: Fâtiha’dan bir âyet değilse cüz’-i âyettir. Ve binâen‘aleyh namazda kıraati farzdır ve cehr olunur

ELMALILI:1:1/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r11.speaker: Ahmed b. Hanbel
ELMALILI:1:1/r11.claim: Like al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal has two transmitted positions, reflecting uncertainty between the two hadith reports.
ELMALILI:1:1/r11.anchor: Ahmed b. Hanbel hazretlerinden de bu iki hadis beyninde tereddüdle iki rivayet mevcuddur

ELMALILI:1:1/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r12.speaker: İmam Mâlik
ELMALILI:1:1/r12.claim: Mālik holds that opening basmalas are neither part of al-Fātiḥa or other surahs nor a separate Qurʾānic portion; they are written for separation and blessing and are not recited in prayer.
ELMALILI:1:1/r12.anchor: besmelelerin ne Fâtiha ve ne sâir sûrelerden, ne de bütün Kur’an’dan bir cüz’-i mahsus olmadığına

ELMALILI:1:1/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r13.speaker: İmam Mâlik
ELMALILI:1:1/r13.claim: Mālik bases his view on the need for Qurʾānic status to be explicit and mutawātir at every locus and on the practice of Medina’s people.
ELMALILI:1:1/r13.anchor: ehl-i Medine’nin teâmülüne istinad ederek sûre evvellerindeki besmelelerin

ELMALILI:1:1/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r14.claim: The sound Ḥanafī position reconciles the other arguments: each opening basmala is an independent Qurʾānic verse, revealed to separate surahs and for blessing, and belongs to none of them.
ELMALILI:1:1/r14.anchor: Evâil-i süverdeki besmele başlı başına bir âyet-i münferide olarak Kur’an’dandır

ELMALILI:1:1/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r15.claim: Because the basmala is independent rather than part of al-Fātiḥa, reciting it in every prayer is not obligatory like al-Fātiḥa, though beginning each recitation and important undertaking with it is sunnah.
ELMALILI:1:1/r15.anchor: her kıraatin ve her emr-i mühimmin bidâyetinde okunması sünnettir

ELMALILI:1:1/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r16.claim: Ḥanafīs say it at the start of each prayer unit’s recitation, not in the middle, and recite it silently even in audible prayers so it will not appear part of the surah.
ELMALILI:1:1/r16.anchor: namazın her rekatında, kıraatin evvelinde okuruz, ortasında okumayız

ELMALILI:1:1/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r17.claim: Outwardly the basmala has four words, but in reality and legal reckoning it has seven because bāʾ and the two definite articles count as words, while bāʾ also implies a verb and its agent.
ELMALILI:1:1/r17.anchor: Besmele zâhirde بِسْمِ، اللّٰهِّٰ، الرَّحْمٰنِ، الرَّح۪يمِ dört kelimedir. Hakikaten ve hükmen ise yedi kelimedir

ELMALILI:1:1/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r18.claim: In the basmala’s special orthography the alif of ism is omitted and the opening bāʾ is lengthened; frequent use explains this abbreviation, while the writing also hints at the force of connection.
ELMALILI:1:1/r18.anchor: besmeleye mahsus olarak hemze hazf olunup söylendiği gibi yazılır ve ‘ivaz olarak ب’nin başı uzatılır

ELMALILI:1:1/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r19.claim: Certain hadith allusions read the letters bāʾ, sīn, and mīm as signs of God’s splendor, radiance, and sovereignty.
ELMALILI:1:1/r19.anchor: بَاء بَهَاءُ اللّٰهِّٰ، سِين سَنَاءُ اللّٰهِّٰ، مِيم مَمْلَكَةُ اللّٰهِّٰ gibi telmihler

ELMALILI:1:1/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r20.claim: The Qurʾānic wisdom concerns the relation of God to the world, especially people and their acts; the basmala’s bāʾ expresses this relation of divinity and servitude.
ELMALILI:1:1/r20.anchor: alâkasında hulâsa olunan ve evvelen Fâtiha’da, sâniyen bütün Kur’ân’da ‘ale’t-tedrîc tafsil edilen bu nisbet tamamen besmeledeki

ELMALILI:1:1/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1/r21.claim: The basic meaning of bāʾ is attachment, with senses such as accompaniment, assistance, connection, and oath; commentators read it here as accompaniment or assistance, with an omitted verb meaning begin, read, or the like.
ELMALILI:1:1/r21.anchor: besmelede müfessirîn yalnız musâhabet veya isti‘âne mânalarından birini gösterirler

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r1.claim: An ism is originally a sign that brings something to mind and conventionally is a word denoting a meaning understood on its own; the denoted meaning or its instance is the musammā.

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r2.claim: The preferred derivation traces ism to the root سمو, though derivation from وسم is also possible; its plurals asmāʾ and asāmī are ordinary Arabic loanwords in Turkish.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r2.anchor: Mezheb-i muhtâra göre aslı سمو maddesidir, وسم’den olması da mümkindir

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r3.claim: Names include both proper and common nouns and names of entities and attributes; the distinctions matter when discussing God’s beautiful names.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r3.anchor: ism-i hâs veya ‘alem, ism-i cins veya âm diye taksim olunduğu gibi ism-i zât veya ism-i sıfat diye de tefrik olunur

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r4.claim: Turkish isim, ad, and nâm overlap but are not interchangeable in every idiom: one may say doing something in someone’s name, while some contexts favor isim for a person.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r4.anchor: lisânımızda biz bunları ince farklarla kullanırız

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r5.claim: Allah is the proper personal name of the true object of worship; through this name and the divine attributes the Qurʾān introduces God and our relation to Him.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r5.anchor: Ma‘bûd-ı Hakk’ın ism-i hâssıdır. Daha doğrusu ism-i zâttır ve ism-i ‘alemdir

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r6.claim: The divine name is the highest organizing principle: without unity in existence, truth, and causality, the sciences remain fragmented and cannot establish even a partial truth.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r6.anchor: Vücûd, hak, nisbet-i illiyet, bütün fenlere hâkim olan mebâdî-i tasavvuriye ve tasdîkiyedir

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r7.claim: The necessary existent is the first origin and ultimate cause of both knowledge and existence; nothing that acts upon or subdues a person can be conceived without God behind it.

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r8.claim: Every person has an innate, simple, unbounded inner assent to God that is more truthful and powerful than finite senses, consciousness, reason, and thought because it encompasses them.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r8.anchor: bütün ilimlerimizin kökü olan bu hiss-i bâtın, mütenâhî hislerimizin, şuurlarımızın, akıllarımızın, fikirlerimizin hepsinden daha hak, hepsinden daha kuvvetlidir

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r9.claim: People’s forgetfulness of this primordial awareness is a source of error; the universe is full of divine signs and the Qurʾān recalls them with miraculous eloquence, hence its name al-Dhikr.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r9.anchor: bize bu âyâtı bir belâgat-i i‘câz ile ihtar ve tezkir ettiği için

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r10.claim: Trying to make the encompassing divine reality into a finite object of vision is impossible: imposing a bounded endpoint on it would cut off consciousness and existence rather than yield clear vision.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r10.anchor: muhîti muhâta kalb etmeye çalışmak gibi bir nokta-i imtinâ‘vardır

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r11.claim: Those who cannot humble their pride before God’s infinite manifestation and say they searched for God but did not find Him proclaim failure in the name of science and philosophy.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r11.anchor: fen ve felsefe nâmına hüsranlarını ilân etmiş olurlar

ELMALILI:1:1#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r12.claim: Sensing God requires the heart to discern Him and apprehend the realized relation between them.
ELMALILI:1:1#2/r12.anchor: Allah’ı sezmek için kalb ile aynı temyîz ve aralarındaki nisbet-i tahakkuku idrak edebilmelidir

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r1.claim: Allah denotes the divine essence as a special name or proper name: it can signify a mental concept that points to God or name the uniquely specified reality itself.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r1.anchor: Hak teâlâ’nın zâtına delâlet eden bir ism-i hâs veya bir ism-i ‘alemîdir

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r2.claim: If a name is established before proving its referent, it is a proper name rather than a direct proper designation; once established after proof, it directly names the reality, illustrated by the name Ülker for blind and sighted people.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r2.anchor: ism-i hâssı olursa da ism-i ‘alemi olmaz. Fakat isbattan sonra vaz‘edilmiş ise bizzat ism-i ‘alem olur

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r3.claim: The discussion of whether God’s essence-name can be a proper designation distinguishes manifestations of essence, attributes, and effects; divine names are restricted to revelation, and direct self-manifestation is possible at least to God Himself.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r3.anchor: İsm-i zât, tecellî-i zâtı ifade eden bir isim olmak lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r4.claim: Humans cannot assign a direct proper name before experiencing a manifestation of the essence; the Qurʾān first introduces God through name-manifestations, and Rahmān and Rahīm initially unfold the name Allah.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r4.anchor: Kur’an dahi bize Allah teâlâ’yı evvelâ tecelliyât-ı ismiyesiyle anlatıyor

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r5.claim: The spiritual progression passes from divine names to effects, from effects to attributes, and toward direct vision of the essence, culminating in longing for the divine encounter.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r5.anchor: Tecellî-i esmâdan tecellî-i âsâra geçeceğiz, kâinatı dolaşacağız. Tecellî-i âsârdan tecellî-i sıfâta ereceğiz

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r6.claim: He links this hoped-for encounter to the call for the tranquil soul to return to its Lord and to faces looking toward their Lord on Resurrection Day.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r6.anchor: يَٰٓأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةًۭ مَّرْضِيَّةًۭ

ELMALILI:1:1#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r7.claim: A concise conceptual definition of Allah is the necessary existent comprising all attributes of perfection; saying only necessary existent is sufficient because that phrase implies the perfection-attributes.
ELMALILI:1:1#3/r7.anchor: O Zât-ı vâcibu’l-vücûd ki bütün sıfât-ı kemâliyeyi

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r1.claim: Allah may be glossed as the true object of worship or creator of all, yet the unified meaning people hear in Allah is clearer and more complete than those definitions, making the proper-name analysis compelling.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r1.anchor: ma‘nâ-yı vahîd, bu mefhumların hepsinden daha vâzıh ve daha ekmeldir

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r2.claim: No other object of worship is called Allah, and the name has no dual or plural; many divine names are allowed, and a proper divine name in another language is possible, though familiar Turkish names are not equivalent.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r2.anchor: Allah’tan mâ‘adâ hiçbir mâbud yâd olunmamıştır

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r3.claim: Tanrı, hudā, ilāh, rabb, and maʿbūd are common nouns that can refer to false or multiple gods, so these terms cannot translate the unique proper name Allah.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r3.anchor: demek olsa yine ism-i hâs değildir

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r4.claim: Pluralizing Allah is false and irreverent; unlike common names for gods or revered human names, the name signifies divine unity.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r4.anchor: ism-i celâlinde böyle bir tâbir bilakis maksad-ı ta‘zîme münâfî olduğundan hem hilâf-ı hak

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r5.claim: French dieu is a generic, pluralizable noun; translating the declaration of faith with it yields an apparent tautology or contradiction and fails to distinguish Allah from a god, despite capitalization or Christian usage.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r5.anchor: Allah ile ilâhı temyiz edememişlerdir. Ve ikisini de ism-i hâs gibi yazmalarına rağmen

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r6.claim: Linguistic and religious historians ask whether Allah is Arabic, borrowed, derived, or primordial; the author turns to those questions while acknowledging their limits.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r6.anchor: Bu kelime esasen Arabî mi değil mi? Menkul mü mürtecel mi, müştak mı, gayr-i müştak mı?

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r7.claim: Human knowledge cannot encompass God’s essence or proper name, and Arabic has no comparable word from which its origin can be securely identified.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r7.anchor: ilmimiz Ma‘bûd-ı hakk’ın zâtını muhît olmadığı gibi ism-i hâssına karşı da öylece kāsırdır

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r8.claim: The Qurʾān shows that Arabs knew the name Allah and answered that Allah created the heavens and earth; its use dates at least to Ishmael, while the author finds no evidence it was borrowed from Hebrew.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r8.anchor: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُ

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r9.claim: Although the name’s presence before Abraham may invite a Hebrew or Syriac borrowing theory, its circulation among ancient Arab peoples and earlier prophets supports an old Arabic history, with no proof of foreign borrowing.

ELMALILI:1:1#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r10.speaker: Basriyyûn
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r10.claim: An important Basran group derives Allah from laah, a noun associated with hiding or elevation and used for divinity; the author cites Arabic poetic usage as evidence.
ELMALILI:1:1#4/r10.anchor: Basriyyûn’un bir kısm-ı mühimmi bundan nakle kāil olmuştur

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r1.claim: The distinctive Arabic use of the name Allah supports its status as a unique proper name, though whether the initial alif-lām is an inseparable article and how its hamza behaves remain debated.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r1.anchor: ism-i şerîfinin lisân-ı Arab’daki hususiyeti ve binâen‘aleyh bir ism-i ‘alem olduğu anlaşılıyor

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib invoked God at the Kaaba during the Elephant event with laahumma, illustrating pre-Islamic use of the name; the author points readers to Sūrat al-Fīl.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r2.anchor: Abdulmuttalib hazretleri Vak‘a-i Fîl’de Kâbe kapısının halkasına yapışarak

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r3.speaker: Ebû Yezîd-i Belhî
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r3.claim: Abū Yazīd al-Balkhī regards laah as foreign because Jews and Christians say laha, and some relate it to Hebrew Elohim; the author says chronology cannot establish borrowing and cognate forms may share an older source.

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r4.speaker: Kûfiyyûn
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r4.claim: The Kufans derive Allah from al-ilāh, with the article becoming integral and its hamza compensating for the elided hamza of ilāh; ilāh is linked to worship, awe, tranquility, or release from fear.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r4.anchor: Kûfiyyûn bunun لاه’dan değil الاه ism-i cinsinin mürâdifi olan الاله’dan menkul olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r5.speaker: Zemahşerî, Kādî Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Bayḍāwī, and other investigators accept the al-ilāh analysis; its meanings are gathered in the true object of worship, and the plural pattern āliha supports the proposed root.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r5.anchor: Zemahşerî, Kādî Beyzâvî gibi bir hayli muhakkikīn bu tedkīki kabul etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r6.claim: The two derivational analyses both preserve an original Arabic meaning in the name, though some posit a foreign origin followed by complete Arabization.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r6.anchor: bu iki tedkīke göre ismullah iştikāk-ı kebîr ile müştak olan bir ism-i Arabî’den menkuldür

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r7.speaker: Ebû Hayyân-ı Endelüsî
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the majority consider Allah an un-derived, primordial proper name for the true God.

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r8.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī’s preferred position is that Allah is God’s proper name and not originally derived; al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, many legal theorists, and jurists agree.

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r9.claim: The author concludes that Allah is neither derived nor transferred but was assigned primordially as a proper name; God precedes all names and attributes, and His worship-worthiness derives from Himself rather than from being worshipped.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r9.anchor: gayr-i müştak ve gayr-i menkul olup bi’l-irticâl vaz‘-ı evvelde bir ism-i ‘alemdir

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r10.claim: Unlike idols, fire, the sun, rulers, or other things made into gods by worshippers, God remains intrinsically worthy of worship whether people recognize Him or not; even deniers are compelled to serve Him unknowingly.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r10.anchor: Allah mâbud olduğu için Allah değil, Allah olduğu için mâbuddur

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r11.claim: By inductive reasoning proper names precede common nouns, which later arise from shared traits; therefore the claim that Allah’s name was transferred from a common noun or attribute is untenable.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r11.anchor: ism-i ‘alemler velev kısmen olsun ism-i cinslerden evvel vaz‘olunur

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r12.claim: A proposed compound of Hebrew El and Syriac or Arabic laah fails linguistic tests: a foreign or compound word should be indeclinable, and the proposed hamza and vowel do not match Allah’s form.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r12.anchor: kelimenin ‘ucme ve ‘alemiyetten veya terkib ve ‘alemiyetten dolayı gayr-i munsarif

ELMALILI:1:1#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r13.claim: Borrowing or derivation of Allah from another language cannot be determined; like its referent, the name remains veiled in eternity, and the most basic response to it is awe and greatness.
ELMALILI:1:1#5/r13.anchor: bu ism-i celâl, lisan nokta-i nazarından da müsemmâsı gibi bir ezeliyet nikābı içindedir

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r1.claim: Rahmān is an exclusive divine name and a dominant adjective of essence rather than action; it can occur with or without its described noun, but does not take a preposition as a verb would.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r1.anchor: Bu da Allah teâlâ’ya has bir isimdir. Bunun bir mefhûm-ı mahsûsu vardır. Fakat ism-i zât değil, ism-i sıfattır

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r2.claim: Derived from raḥm and raḥma, Rahmān is an intensive adjective meaning possessing very abundant and enduring mercy; although analogically applicable to anyone, actual use is reserved for God.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r2.anchor: devam ve mübalağa ifade eden bir sıfat-ı müşebbehe sîgasıdır

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r3.claim: A flattering poet once called Musaylima rahmāna without the article, but the author says this was wrong even linguistically and all the more so religiously.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r3.anchor: Müseylimetü’l-Kezzâb’a bir kere müfrit ve müdâhin bir şâir lâmsız olarak لاَ زِلْتَ رَحْمٰنَا tâbirini kullanmış

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r4.claim: Rahmān can be explained as very merciful but cannot be translated as a proper divine name; esirgeyici wrongly suggests withholding or jealousy, while acıyıcı lacks the positive sense of mercy.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r4.anchor: Bu ismi belleriz ve tercemesiyle değil tefsîriyle rahmet mefhûmundan anlamaya çalışırız

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r5.claim: Older Turkish speakers used yarlığayıcı for mercy’s gracious result, but this remains an adjective; divine mercy itself is not an emotional inclination but the will of good or unlimited bestowal.

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r6.claim: Rahmān also cannot be translated as bağışlayıcı, since that confuses it with names such as Vehhāb or ʿAfūvv, which are not exclusive to God.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r6.anchor: hâs değildir. Binâen‘aleyh Rahmân, Vehhâb veya Afüvv mânalarını ifade eden

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r7.claim: Rahīm is a second divine attribute, best understood here as an intensive active participle meaning very merciful or much showing mercy.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r7.anchor: iki sıfatın farkı daha bâriz olmak için burada ikincisi daha muvâfıktır

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r8.claim: Unlike Rahmān, Rahīm is a pure adjective, requires a described noun, can be used of others, functions verbally, and has a definite article of reference.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r8.anchor: Bu dahi Cenâb-ı Allah’ın sıfatlarından biridir. Fakat sıfat-ı mahzadır, mevsufsuz kullanılmaz

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r9.claim: The phrase moves from the pure name Allah to the name-and-attribute Rahmān and then the pure attribute Rahīm, gradually unfolding God’s name in the heart as the first manifestation of divine beauty.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r9.anchor: evvelâ bir ism-i mahz, sâniyen hem isim hem sıfat, sâlisen mahz-ı sıfat olan üç kelimeden müteşekkil olarak husustan umuma doğru inbisat etmiştir

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r10.claim: Commentators distinguish Rahmān as looking to pre-eternity and Rahīm to endless duration: creatures benefit from the former through an initial relation and from the latter through actual action at the end.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r10.anchor: lâyezâle nâzırdır. Binâen‘aleyh mahlûkât, merhamet-i Rahmâniyeden

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r11.claim: A transmitted explanation calls God the Rahmān of this world and Rahīm of the afterlife, or the Rahmān of believers and unbelievers but Rahīm only of believers; the author clarifies that God is both names in both realms.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r11.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah dünyanın da, âhiretin de hem rahmânı hem rahîmidir

ELMALILI:1:1#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r12.claim: Because Rahmān is God’s exclusive name, its kind of mercy and beneficence cannot issue from creatures; Rahīm is not exclusive and can describe mercy and generosity from creatures.
ELMALILI:1:1#6/r12.anchor: rahmet-i Rahmân bir şart ile meşrut değil iken rahmet-i Rahîm bir şart ile meşruttur

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r1.claim: Rahman is a divine attribute exclusive to God whose relation is not a particular act; its primordial grace extends universally without condition.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r1.anchor: Rahmâniyetin Allah’a ihtisâsı ve mâ‘adâya ta‘alluk-ı fi‘lî ifade etmeyip ancak bi’l-izâfe âmil olması ekvânda bilâ-şart-ı şey’ bir umum ifade eder

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r2.claim: Every creature's original gifts and existence arise from Rahman's grace, received without anyone's earned choice.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r2.anchor: Her şeyin ilk halk ve îcâdında almış olduğu bütün mevâhib-i fıtriye rahmâniyetin izâfeti eseridir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r3.claim: Primordial creation is compelled and bestowed: stones, trees, and humans have their kinds through this unchosen mercy.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r3.anchor: Taşın taş, ağacın ağaç, insanın insan olması böyle bir rahmet-i cebriyenin eseridir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r4.claim: All realms and beings, from obedient and believing to rebellious and idolatrous, are immersed in Rahman's mercy and freed from fear in that respect.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r4.anchor: âlemlerin hepsi rahmet-i Rahmân’a müstağraktır ve bu haysiyetle mehâfetten âzâdedir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r5.claim: If this universal grace were all, distinctions between knowledge and ignorance, life and death, effort and idleness, obedience and disobedience, and faith and unbelief would disappear.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r5.anchor: Lâkin bu kadarla kalsa idi, ilim ile cehlin, hayât ile mevtin, sa‘y ile atâletin, itaat ile isyanın

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r6.claim: Without a further mercy enabling agency, people would be determinists and compelled beings, unable to act on what they know or desire.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r6.anchor: hep tabîî olurduk, tabi‘iyyûndan, cebriyyûndan olurduk

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r7.claim: God's wisdom requires that He display His own will and create creatures who possess will, rather than make all action compulsory.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r7.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’ın kendi irade ve ihtiyârını göstermesi ve onun eseri olarak sâhib-i irâde mahlûkāt halk etmesi

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r8.claim: God advances creatures according to good choices and grants enjoyment of mercy, while bad choices bring deprivation, pain, and punishment; this harmonizes their wills with His.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r8.anchor: hüsn-i irade ve ihtiyarlarına göre terakki ettirerek rahmetinden mütena‘‘im ve müstefid ve bilakis sû’-i irade ve kesblerine göre mahrûmiyetle, elem ve ‘ikāb ile mu‘âteb

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r9.claim: Rahman is the instinctive grace seen in mother birds beating their wings over their young.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r9.anchor: Ana kuşlar eser-i rahmâniyet olan sevk-i fıtrî ile yavrularının başında kanat çırpar

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r10.claim: Rahim is the grace through which ethical people compete in compassion and good works.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r10.anchor: ahlâklı insanlar da eser-i rahîmiyetle vücûh-ı hayr üzerinde rahm u şefkatle müsâbaka ederler

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r11.claim: Rahman's first mercy brings everyone into existence and sustains them regardless of effort.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r11.anchor: İbtidâ çalışana çalışmayana bakmadan vücûda sevk ve o suretle idare etmek bir rahmet-i rahmâniyedir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r12.claim: Rahim's further mercy grants the goals achieved by those who work.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r12.anchor: Bilâhare çalışanlara çalıştıkları gayeleri de ayrıca bahş etmek bir rahmet-i rahîmiyedir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r13.claim: Rahman gives absolute hope and prevents universal despair; without it humans would lack existence and essential natural gifts.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r13.anchor: Rahmâniyet ye’s-i mutlaka, umûmî bedbinliğe imkân bırakmayan bir ümîd-i mutlak

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r14.claim: Rahim answers particular despair, sustains specific aims and effort, and rewards responsibility.

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r15.claim: Under Rahman's universal grace believers and unbelievers, and this world and the next, are equal; Rahim's grace sharply distinguishes them, as the two groups in 42:7 show.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r15.anchor: rahmâniyetin karşısında dünya ve âhiret, mü’min ve kâfir müsâvî iken rahîmiyetin karşısında bunlar bir fark-ı bâriz ile ayrılıyor

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r16.claim: Thus the inherited formulations call God Rahman of this world and the next but Rahim of the next, or Rahman of believer and unbeliever but Rahim of the believer.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r16.anchor: “dünya ve âhiretin Rahmân’ı ve âhiretin Rahîm’i” yahut “mü’min ve kâfirin Rahmân’ı, mü’minin Rahîm’i”

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r17.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r17.claim: Abduh neglects the inherited distinction because he assumes the lexicon does not support it; Elmalılı says this is mistaken.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r17.anchor: Şeyh Abduh merhûmun lügatta bunlara işaret yoktur zannıyla eslâfın bu tâbirlerle gösterdikleri farkları ihmâl etmesi doğru değildir

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r18.claim: Lexically Rahman is a predominant attribute specific to God, without an active relation and suggestive of eternity and the beginning; Rahim has an active relation and continues without end.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r18.anchor: gālibedendir ve ta‘alluk-i fi‘lîsi yoktur. Ezeliyeti müş‘ir ve mebde’e nâzırdır

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r19.claim: Rahman's mercy is an essential attribute of willing good at the outset, while Rahim's is an active attribute of doing good at the end.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r19.anchor: Rahmet-i Rahmân, ibtidâen irâde-i hayra râci‘bir sıfat-ı zâtiye

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r20.claim: Rahman and Rahim are not repeated merely for emphasis: each has its own foundational meaning and distinct mode of intensification.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r20.anchor: “Rahmân” ile “Rahîm” başka başka birer ma‘nâ-yı rahmeti hâiz

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r21.claim: Rahman is more emphatic in encompassing every creature, while Rahim is more emphatic in actual beneficence, which also operates through servants.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r21.anchor: Bir cihetten rahmet-i Rahmân eblağdır, çünkü her mahlûka muzâf olur. Diğer cihetten rahmet-i Rahîm eblağdır

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r22.speaker: Bazı tefsirler
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r22.claim: Some commentaries associate Rahman's mercy with great blessings and Rahim's with the subtleties of blessings.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r22.anchor: Bazı tefsirlerde de buna işâreten “rahmet-i Rahmân celâil-i ni‘am, rahmet-i Rahîm ise dekāik-i ni‘am ile alâkadardır” derler

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r23.claim: The grammatical pattern distinguishes them: Rahman's subject is restricted while its object is general; Rahim's subject is general while its object is restricted.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r23.anchor: “Rahmân”ın mevsûfu hâs, müte‘allakı âmdır. “Rahîm”in mevsûfu âm, müte‘allakı hâstır

ELMALILI:1:1#7/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r24.claim: Together these attributes replace pessimism with boundless optimism, the spirit of faith; the first benefit received from the basmala is this hope, affirmed by 28:83.
ELMALILI:1:1#7/r24.anchor: Rahmân-ı Rahîm’i münkir olan kâfir istediği kadar bedbin olsun, fakat mü’minin bedbinliğine hiçbir sebep yoktur

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r1.claim: The basmala has an apparent structure of one genitive relation, two adjectival relations, and an initial attachment; its hidden relation makes it a complete, concise statement.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r1.anchor: Besmele zâhirde bir nisbet-i izâfiye ile iki nisbet-i vasfiyye ve başında bir nisbet-i ta‘alluktan mürekkeb

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r2.claim: Ism Allah may be read as a genitive meaning either Allah's name or the name Allah.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r2.anchor: beyâniye olabilir ki evvelkinde “Allah’ın ismi”, ikincide “Allah ismi” demek olur

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r3.claim: On the lamiyya reading the adjectives can be construed before or after the genitive; on the bayaniyya reading the whole epitheted name is cited as one name and then explains ism.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r3.anchor: “Rahmân ve Rahîm sıfatlarıyla muttasıf bulunan Cenâb-ı Allah’ın ismiyle”

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r4.claim: The bayaniyya analysis treats the genitive inflection as distributed over three words to stress the divine proper name, a necessary inflection rather than ordinary narration grammar.

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r5.speaker: Müfessirînin çoğu
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r5.claim: Most commentators prefer the lamiyya construction because its parsing is explicit and the meanings of the names and attributes are directly intended.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r5.anchor: Müfessirînin çoğu evvelkini tercih ediyorlar. Çünkü onda hem i‘râb zâhir ve hem esmâ ve sıfâtın mânası bizzat maksud olur

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r6.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r6.claim: Some prefer the bayaniyya construction, citing Labid's line using ism al-salam; the Mevlid author also reflects it with Allah adı.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r6.anchor: Bazıları ise Lebîd’in السَّلَاَمِ عَلَيْكُمَا إِلَى الْحَوْلِ ثُمَّ اسْمُ mısrâ‘ındaki اِسْمُ السَّلَاَمِ gibi beyâniyeyi tercih etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r7.claim: The omitted verb is the action the speaker is about to undertake, such as reading, writing, eating, or beginning, and the opening ba attaches the name to it.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r7.anchor: fiil besmele diyen kimsenin teşebbüs edeceği

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r8.claim: The verb and subject are omitted to let anyone connect the basmala to any intended act; ba and the speaker's situation identify the ellipsis, as in Turkish formulas like devletle selâmetle.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r8.anchor: cümlenin erkânı olan fiil ve fâil hazf edilmişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r9.claim: Although Arabic normally delays a complement, placing the ba phrase first gives emphasis and exclusivity; compared with 96:1, basmala foregrounds Allah's name rather than the act of reading.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r9.anchor: böyle hakkı muahhar olan tetimmenin takdîmi bir ihtimam ve ihtisas ifade eder

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r10.claim: This fronting makes the beginning exclusive to Allah's name, rejecting the pagan practice of starting with Lat or Uzza and expressing tawhid.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r10.anchor: Arap müşrikleri de sözlerine veya işlerine بِاسْمِ اللَاَّتِ بِاسْمِ الْعُزَّی gibi putlarından birinin ismiyle başlarlardı

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r11.claim: Turkish word order cannot readily preserve the Arabic exclusivity and the direct joining of the spoken formula to the act; an implied construction can show tawhid but is awkward and loses concision.
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r11.anchor: Bunda ise fi‘l-i kavlînin, fi‘l-i hakīkīye mukāreneti temin edilmemiş olur

ELMALILI:1:1#8/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#8/r12.claim: He proposes eight possible Turkish renderings, using both lamiyya and bayaniyya forms such as Allah's name with the two attributes or Allah, Rahman, Rahim as one name.

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r1.claim: Combining Allah with Rahman and Rahim as one name foregrounds Allah but still fails to connect the act directly with mercy.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r1.anchor: doğrudan doğru Allah ismi mebde’ yapılmış olacak ve ma‘amâfîh vasl-ı rahmet yine temin edilemeyecektir

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r2.claim: Removing the participle still leaves Allah's proper name insufficiently foregrounded and separates it from the mercy attributes; listing three names may imply three divine essences, though singular ismiyle helps avert that implication.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r2.anchor: “ismiyle” denilip, “isimleriyle” denilmemesi bu îhâmı def‘e kâfi

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r3.claim: The basmala's words, composition, rhetoric, sound, and even its sweet pattern of letters cannot be fully carried into Turkish, so it should be recited in Arabic and understood through explanation.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r3.anchor: ne müfredâtını ve ne terkiblerini tamamen terceme mümkin olmayan ve hele vücûh-ı belâgati, âheng-i beyânı hiçbir suretle kābil-i nakl olmayan

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r4.claim: He rejects corrupting the tawhid key with a rendering like esirgeciyi bağışlayıcı tanrı adıyla.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r4.anchor: bir miftâh-ı kül ve bir âyet-i tevhîd olan

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r5.claim: The basmala's interpretive pivot is ba, which connects Allah's name, the first source and ultimate object of existence and progress, to the intended act.

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r6.claim: Human acts are not their own complete cause: will is a moment in the stream of existence, and success depends on the outpouring between the First Cause and human will, first Rahmani and finally Rahimi.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r6.anchor: muvaffakiyetlerimiz, illet-i ûlâ ile iradelerimiz arasındaki nisbetin feyzine tâbi‘dir ki bu feyz ibtidâen Rahmânî, intihâen Rahîmîdir

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r7.claim: The basmala's ba makes this universal relation conscious; its secret is said to lie in the ba's dot, and Hâkânî's poem links the basmala's continuity to the existence of things.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r7.anchor: Olmasa besmele resmi memdûd Cins-i eşyâda olur muydu vücûd

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r8.speaker: E‘âzım-ı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r8.claim: The great commentators say ba here means either attachment and accompaniment or seeking aid; the former makes the basmala circumstantial, the latter an indirect object.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r8.anchor: E‘âzım-ı müfessirîn diyorlar ki: “Bâ”nın buradaki ma‘nâ-yı ilsâkı

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r9.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r9.claim: Abduh says customary in the name of means acting for an authority, by its command and on its behalf; the Muslim's basmala can express beginning an act for Allah and by His command.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r9.anchor: Şeyh Abduh merhum Fâtiha tefsîrinde zikre şâyan bir mâna daha kaydetmiştir

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r10.claim: Elmalılı says Abduh's deputyship reading amounts to acting as God's representative and self-effacement, appropriate only to special stations such as prophethood, sainthood, rule, and authority.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r10.anchor: ancak risalet, velâyet, hâkimiyet, tasarruf gibi makāmât-ı mahsûsada cârî olur

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r11.claim: That meaning cannot apply generally: saying one eats in God's name is improper, though saying one eats food God bestowed would be sound; worship is for God but not done as His deputy.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r11.anchor: Çünkü ibadet Allah’a olursa da Allah nâmına niyâbeten değil

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r12.claim: Reports that the basmala is the key to every book and every important act imply a general meaning for lawful acts; one of the commentators' attachment or seeking-aid senses supplies it.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r12.anchor: bize besmelenin meşrû olan her işimizin küşâdında miftah olabilecek bir ma‘nâ-yı şâmilini ihtar etmektedir

ELMALILI:1:1#9/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r13.claim: Abduh's explanation is sound for the Quran's revelation, recitation, and writing because of the basmala's position at their beginnings, and it matters in special settings too.
ELMALILI:1:1#9/r13.anchor: Kur’ân’ın, süver-i Kur’ân’ın nüzûlü, kıraati, kitabeti itibariyle evvelinde bulunması haysiyetinden besmelenin mânasında Şeyh Abduh’un îzâhı doğru olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r1.claim: Stopping after only bism is defective; stopping after Bismillah or after Rahman is sufficient and sound, and the complete stop follows Rahim.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r1.anchor: Besmele derken بِسْمِ üzerinde durmak nâkıs ve kabih, بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ deyip durmak kâfi ve sahih

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r2.claim: When writing a mushaf, writing the basmala at each surah opening except Bara'a is obligatory.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r2.anchor: Mushaf yazarken Berâe’den mâ‘adâ sûre başlarında بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ yazmak farzdır

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r3.claim: For slaughter or shooting game, saying Bismillah alone is obligatory; deliberate omission makes the animal unlawful, but forgetfulness is excused.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r3.anchor: Hayvan zebh ederken veya ava silah atarken sadece بسم اللّٰه demek de farzdır. Kasden terk edilirse o hayvan yenmez

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r4.claim: In slaughter and similar settings, omitting Rahman and Rahim is sunnah.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r4.anchor: Bunda ve bu gibi bazı mevâki‘de الرَّحْمٰن الرَّحِيم denilmemek sünnettir

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r5.speaker: Cumhûr
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r5.claim: Outside prayer, beginning a surah recitation with isti'adha and basmala is sunnah according to the majority, while some imams such as Ata consider it obligatory.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r5.anchor: demek cumhûra göre sünnet, ezcümle Atâ gibi bazı e’immeye göre vâcibdir

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r6.claim: There is no basmala at Bara'a's opening; in the Asim reading, reciting it between two surahs is recommended, and starting midway or at the end also recommends isti'adha and basmala.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r6.anchor: Yalnız Berâe’de besmele denmez. Sûreteyn beyninde iki kıraat vardır. Bizim Âsım kıraatinde okumak mendubdur

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r7.speaker: Hanefîler
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r7.claim: In prayer before al-Fatiha, Hanafis recommend silently reciting isti'adha and basmala.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r7.anchor: namazda biz Hanefîlere göre Fâtiha’dan evvel sırren eûzü-besmele sünnet

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r8.speaker: Şâfiiyye
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r8.claim: Shafi'is require basmala in prayer, either silently or aloud.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r8.anchor: Şâfiiyye’ye göre sırren veya cehren besmele farz

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r9.speaker: Mâlikîler
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r9.claim: Malikis recommend omitting basmala in prayer.

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r10.claim: Beginning other important, lawful affairs with Bismillah, with or without Rahman and Rahim, is recommended, sunnah, or obligatory according to circumstances.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r10.anchor: Kıraatten mâ‘adâ sâir umûr-i mühimme ve meşrû‘aya بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ veya بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ile başlamak derecâtına göre mendub veya sünnet veya vâcibdir

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r11.claim: He directs readers to later discussions of isti'adha at 16:98, general naming at al-Alaq, slaughter at al-Anam, and basmala again at al-Naml.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r11.anchor: İsti‘âze meselesi فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r12.claim: The Prophet's moral character and mission as mercy to the worlds ground his selection and training; God taught him to begin with the divine name and its exclusive relation.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r12.anchor: evvelemirde onun ıstıfâsına, tehzîb ve te’dîbine ‘inâyet-i rabbâniyesini izhâr

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r13.claim: God gave the community the basmala as a universal key and made its use at the start of books, writing, recitation, speeches, and needs a prophetic sunnah.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r13.anchor: mebde’-i ümîdi ve müntehâ-yı âmâli olan ‘inâyet-i Rahmâniye ve rahmet-i Rahîmiyeyi

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r14.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r14.claim: A prophetic hadith calls the basmala the key to every book.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r14.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem Efendimiz’in hadîs-i şerîflerinde de şöyle vârid olmuştur: بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ مِفْتَاحُ كُلِّ كِتَابٍ

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r15.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r15.claim: Another prophetic hadith says an important matter not begun with Allah's name is abtar, truncated; without it a work cannot be presented before God and remains deficient.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r15.anchor: Her mühim iş ki bismillah ile başlanmamıştır güdüktür vesselâm

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r16.claim: The basmala summarizes the Quran's subject and aim; al-Fatiha and the successive surahs unfold its inexhaustible detail and wise ordering, beyond merely measurable length or poetic feeling.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r16.anchor: biz bunda ilm-i Kur’ân’ın mevzû‘unu, gayesini icmâlen bulacağız ve evvelâ Fâtiha’da sâniyen peyderpey sûreleriyle bütün Kur’an’da bunun

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r17.claim: The Quran is not a chance or merely poetic anthology but a coherent true discourse like a single comprehensive sentence, beginning with basmala and ending with al-Nas.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r17.anchor: Kur’ân’ın sûreleri, âyetleri keyfemettefak bir tesadüfün veya sade bir hiss-i şâirânenin sevkiyle serilivermiş bir dîvân-ı mahlût değil

ELMALILI:1:1#10/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r18.claim: The Quran's whole discourse links Allah to all creatures, especially humans, and their return relation to Him; recitation permutations at completion, transmitted from Ali, are called hal-murtahil and signify no total break in existence.
ELMALILI:1:1#10/r18.anchor: ki bu bize vücudda inkıtâ‘-ı tâm olmadığını ifade eder

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r1.claim: Astronomy studies universal gravitation as one unified subject, yet it does not encompass all existence or even all scientific fields.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r1.anchor: Bugün biliyoruz ki bütün bir ilm-i hey’et bir câzibe kanununun ifadesidir

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r2.claim: Gravity does not cover particle attraction, chemical cohesion, organic nourishment and reproduction, affective attraction and aversion, sensory images, rational truth, spiritual will, or social bonds.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r2.anchor: onda ne ecsâmın zerrâtı veya eczâ-i ferdiyesi arasındaki câzibe-i zerreviye veya cüz’-i ferdiyeyi, temâsük ve telâsuk gibi alâka-i kimyeviyeyi

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r3.claim: The Quran's subject unifies every physical and spiritual kind of attraction under absolute lordship and God's relation to the world, especially humanity; gravity is only one partial sign.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r3.anchor: rubûbiyet kanununu, Allah ile âlem ve bilhassa insanlar beynindeki nisbet ve izâfet-i mutlakanın

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r4.claim: Quranic composition unites scientific order and aesthetic beauty, surpassing the system of sciences in firmness and literature in variety and resemblance.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r4.anchor: Nazm-ı Kur’an nesak-ı ilmî ile nesak-ı bedî‘înin vahdetgâhıdır

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r5.claim: The Quran's integrated order supports its divine origin: if it came from other than God, much inconsistency would be found, as 4:82 says.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r5.anchor: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَٰفًا كَثِيرًا

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r6.claim: Human science has not measured even the order of the three-body system, so it cannot certify the absence of scientific, logical, or aesthetic flaws in cosmic order.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r6.anchor: yalnız ecsâm-ı selâse nazariyesi dâhilindeki nizam ve nisbetini bile henüz ölçmemiş olan fennimiz

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r7.claim: Nature's order is both manifest and hidden; the Quran's surah and verse order is similarly, and even more, manifest and hidden, manifest through perfection and hidden through inexhaustibility.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r7.anchor: Fıtratın bu nizâmı, nazarımızda nasıl böyle hem zâhir ve hem bâtın ise, Kur’ân’ın sûreleri ve âyetleri beynindeki nizâm-ı ilmî ve bedî‘î dahi onun gibi ve hatta ondan ziyade zâhir ve ondan ziyade bâtındır

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r8.claim: A poet says the cosmos' maiden thought has been torn open while the Quran's meaning still remains veiled in its purity.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r8.anchor: Bikr-i fikri kâinâtın çâk çâk oldu fakat Perde-i ‘ismette kaldı ma‘nî-i Kur’ân henüz

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r9.claim: People often sacrifice aesthetic relations when thinking logically and logical relations when thinking aesthetically; although they cannot chart all Quranic relations, they can experience their perfection by living it.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r9.anchor: bu tenâsübü bütün kadrosuyla bir cetvel çizer gibi fikren ölçemiyor isek o fıtratı yaşarken bu zevk-i kemâli vecd ile duyabiliriz

ELMALILI:1:1#11/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r10.claim: To live the universal attraction, readers should seek refuge from distraction and satanic whispering, then take the basmala as key and begin al-Fatiha in gratitude.
ELMALILI:1:1#11/r10.anchor: diyelim ve o câzibe-i külliyeyi yaşamak için

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r1.claim: The Basmala was probably prefixed to all suras from the middle Meccan period onward, retrospectively including suras already proclaimed.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Invokationsformel, mit dem Akronym »Basmala« benannt, wird – wohl ab mittelmekkanischer Zeit – allen Suren vorangestellt

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r2.claim: Its use resembles the Christian Trinitarian formula placed before public and official messages, reformulated here as a statement about one God.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r2.anchor: Ihr Gebrauch entspricht dem der Trinitätsformel »Im Namen des Vaters und des Sohnes und des Heiligen Geistes« in christlichen Texten

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r3.claim: The only occurrence inside a sura is in Solomon’s letter to the Queen of Sheba, raising the possibility that suras were treated as written documents from then on.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r3.anchor: Innerhalb eines Surentexts begegnet die Basmala einzig in der spätmittelmekkanischen Sure Q 27:30

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r4.claim: Al-Raḥmān marks a middle Meccan usage that replaced the previously frequent rabb/rabbuka in a named group of suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r4.anchor: Auf die mittelmekkanische Herkunft der Basmala verweist vor allem der Gottesname ar-Raḥmān

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r5.speaker: Ludwig Ammann
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r5.claim: Ammann reads the introduction of al-Raḥmān as softening frequent earlier threats of hell and emphasizing assurance of salvation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r5.anchor: Ludwig Ammann (2001:38) sieht in der Einführung von ar-raḥmān ein Mittel der Milderung der vorher frequenten Höllendrohungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r6.claim: Here al-Raḥmān joins Allāh, a divine name used only occasionally earlier and common from late Meccan times.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r6.anchor: In Q 1:1 verbindet er sich mit dem ab Spätmekka üblichen Gottesnamen Allāh

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r7.claim: The Jewish liturgical and epigraphic name ha-raḥamān probably entered north Arabian liturgical language through South Arabia.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r7.anchor: Der auch in zentralen jüdischen liturgischen und in epigraphischen Texten geläufige Gottesname (hebr. ha-raḥamān) ist mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit über Südarabien

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r8.claim: The semantically related raḥīm renders the encountered name again in ordinary Arabic.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r8.anchor: Die etymologisch und semantisch eng verwandte Prädikation raḥīm ›übersetzt‹ den vorgefundenen Namen noch einmal in das gebräuchliche Arabisch

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r9.claim: The name’s dominance is not explained by its genealogy alone; liturgical experience likely shaped the focus on divine mercy, perhaps echoing kyrie eleēson and Christian salvation history.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r9.anchor: so möchte man auch hier einen Anstoß aus liturgischer Richtung vermuten

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r10.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r10.claim: The Basmala’s merciful divine attribute reflects the emotional dimension of divine and exemplary human conduct newly foregrounded in middle Meccan theology.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r10.anchor: Das mit dem Gottesnamen ar-Raḥmān und der Basmala insgesamt herausgehobene Attribut Gottes als »barmherzig« trägt der in Mittelmekka neu in den Vordergrund gestellten emotionalen Dimension

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r11.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r11.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r11.claim: Counting the Basmala as a verse derives from Q 15:87’s seven repeated elements; seven is a round number below ten, so the identification does not require exactly seven verses.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r11.anchor: Die Zahl Sieben ist hier jedoch, wie Rubin (1993) gezeigt hat, nicht als präzise numerische Angabe zu verstehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r12.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r12.speaker: Rubin
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r12.claim: Rubin interprets seven in Q 15:87 as a round number under ten rather than an exact count.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:1:kommentar/r12.anchor: wie Rubin (1993) gezeigt hat, nicht als präzise numerische Angabe zu verstehen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r1.claim: Since the Qur’an’s collection excluded non-Qur’anic material, each surah-opening basmala is a separate verse outside that surah’s verse count; the author says Hanafi jurists agree.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r1.anchor: her sûrenin başındaki besmeleyi, sûrenin âyet sayılarına dahil olmayan ayrı bir âyet olarak kabul etmek gerekmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r2.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r2.claim: Shafi‘i counts the Fatiha basmala as one of its verses; two views are reported for other surahs, with inclusion in each surah recorded as the more sound report from him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r2.anchor: İmam Şâfiî Fâtiha sûresinin başındaki besmeleyi bu sûreden bir âyet olarak kabul etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r3.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r3.claim: Because basmalas are separate opening verses, Abu Hanifa says to recite one silently before Fatiha in prayer, but not before the additional surah or verses after it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r3.anchor: Ebû Hanîfe’ye göre besmeleler sûrelerin başında ayrı âyetler olduğu için namazda yalnızca Fâtiha’dan önce sessiz olarak okunur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r4.claim: The common Turkish rendering is Rahman and Rahim Allah’s name; because an implicit verb depends on the activity intended, the author also proposes rendering it as invoking Allah’s name and seeking His help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r4.anchor: maksadı doğru anlatabilmek için besmeleyi “Rahmân ve rahîm olan Allah adına, ... adını anarak, ... Allah’tan yardım dileyerek ...” şekillerinde çevirmek de uygun olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r5.claim: Beginning with refuge and basmala acknowledges human dependence, success from God, stewardship in His dominion, and the duty not to betray entrusted limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r5.anchor: başarı ve gücün ancak Allah’tan gelebileceğini, Allah’ın yeryüzünde halife kıldığı bir varlık olarak O’nun mülkünde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r6.claim: The refuge and basmala implicitly enact tawhid: first removing false powers and obstacles to worship, then establishing the one true God and opening a sound bond with Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r6.anchor: önce kulluk ilişkisine engel olan kirli çevre temizleniyor, sonra da bu ilişkinin en uygun anahtarı kullanılmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r7.claim: Rahman is an exclusive divine name for limitless, undeserved grace toward every creature throughout all time, like rain falling and sunlight warming all things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r7.anchor: Rahmân “en uzak geçmişe doğru bütün yaratılmışlara sonsuz ve sınırsız lutuf, ihsan, rahmet bahşeden” demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r8.claim: Rahim means abundant mercy and may describe humans; for God it especially denotes limitless mercy, grace, and compassion creatures will merit in the future, of which protecting and forgiving are only facets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:1/r8.anchor: Allah’ın rahîm sıfat-ismi O’nun, daha ziyade kullarının gelecekte elde etmek üzere hak ettikleri, lâyık oldukları sınırsız rahmetini

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r1.claim: The bāʾ can mark attachment, instrument, oath, cause, circumstance, location, or transfer; Abū Ḥayyān illustrates each usage with Arabic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r1.anchor: باء الجر تأتي لمعان: للإلصاق، والاستعانة، والقسم، والسبب، والحال، والظرفية، والنقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r2.claim: The bāʾ may also be emphatic or mark substitution, exchange, separation, superposition, and elevation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r2.anchor: وتأتي زائدة للتوكيد: شربن بماء البحر. والبدل: فليت لي بهم قوما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r3.claim: The Basran derivation of ism from sīn-mīm-wāw is preferable to the Kufan wāw-sīn-mīm analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r3.anchor: والبصري يقول: مادته سين وميم وواو، والكوفي يقول: واو وسين وميم، والأرجح الأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r4.claim: The article al- has several definite uses, including reference to an individual or class, presence, an allusive quality, dominance, and relative-clause use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r4.anchor: أل للعهد في شخص أو جنس، وللحضور، وللمح الصفة، وللغلبة، وموصولة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r5.claim: Grammarians also distinguish obligatory and non-obligatory extra al- and debate whether it consists of one letter or two and whether the hamza is extra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r5.anchor: وزائدة لازمة، وغير لازمة، فاللازمة: كالآن، وغير اللازمة: باعد أم العمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r6.speaker: الأكثرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r6.claim: Most authorities treat Allah as a proper name for the true deity and regard it as non-derived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p27/r6.anchor: والله علم لا يطلق إلا على المعبود بحق مرتحل غير مشتق عند الأكثرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Reported derivations of Allah include roots meaning rising, concealment, refuge or bewilderment, worship, rest, and ecstatic longing; Abū Ḥayyān surveys these competing analyses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: قيل: لام وياء وهاء، من لاه يليه، ارتفع. قيل: ولذلك سميت الشمس إلاهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq derives Allah from a root meaning to seek refuge, with the hamza omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r2.anchor: من أله أي فزع، قاله ابن إسحاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r3.speaker: أبو عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r3.claim: Abū ʿUmar derives Allah from a root meaning to be bewildered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r3.anchor: أو أله تحير، قاله أبو عمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r4.speaker: النضر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r4.claim: Al-Naḍr derives Allah from a root meaning to worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r4.anchor: وأله عبد، قاله النضر، أو أله سكن، قاله المبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r5.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives Allah from a root meaning to be at rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r5.anchor: قاله النضر، أو أله سكن، قاله المبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: الخليل والقناد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl and al-Qannād propose derivation from walh, ecstatic longing, with hamza replacing wāw; Abū Ḥayyān calls this weak because the replacement would be obligatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: وقيل: مادته واو ولام وهاء، من وله، أي طرب، وأبدلت الهمزة فيه من الواو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r7.claim: If Allah derives from ilāh, its article is either dominant, like al-Najm for the Pleiades, or a necessary extra article under other derivations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r7.anchor: وأل في الله إذا قلنا أصله الإلاه، قالوا للغلبة، إذ الإله ينطلق على المعبود بحق وباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r8.claim: The claim that al- belongs intrinsically to Allah is mistaken: it would leave an unexplained form and unexplained absence of tanwīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r8.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن أل في الله من نفس الكلمة، ووصلت الهمزة لكثرة الاستعمال، وهو اختيار أبي بكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r9.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي والسهيلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r9.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī and al-Suhaylī chose the view that al- is part of the word Allah and its hamza was connected because of frequent use.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r9.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي بكر بن العربي والسهيلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r10.speaker: أبو يزيد البلخي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r10.claim: Abū Yazīd al-Balkhī says Allah is foreign, citing Jewish and Christian use of lāhā and an Arabic poetic example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r10.anchor: قال أبو يزيد البلخي: هو أعجمي، فإن اليهود والنصارى يقولون لاها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r11.claim: A rare theological-linguistic position calls Allah an attribute rather than a proper name, since the divine essence is not grasped directly and is known through attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r11.anchor: ومن غريب ما قيل في الله أنه صفة وليس اسم ذات، لأن اسم الذات يعرف به المسمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p28/r12.speaker: author
