BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r8.anchor: ثم ولى السادس المفتتح به القرآن الخامس المحكم كم وجه في قوله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r1.claim: The Qur'an's recited order differs from revelation order: the first revelation to the Prophet was the clear command to read, while the first public warning was the command to rise and warn of the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r1.anchor: وأما تنزيله يفي ترتيب البيان فإن أ , ل ما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو حرف المحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r2.claim: The warning came first for the community because afterlife reform is most important and also sets worldly affairs right; the Prophet rendered warning and prohibition with one sense, though the first addresses instinct and the second understanding.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r2.anchor: فابتدأ سبحانه وتعالى ترتيل الأمة بإصلاح المعاد الأهم لأن عليه يصلح أمر الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r3.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr argues that the disconnected letters challenge opponents to use the remaining half of the alphabet to produce a rival discourse; al-Zarkashi transmits the claim.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r3.anchor: نقل ذلك الزركشي في البرهان عن القاضي أبي بكر قال : وقد علم ذلك بعض أرباب الحقائق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r4.claim: Abu Bakr says every book has an essence and the Qur'an's essence lies in the opening letters of its surahs; Ali likewise calls the alphabetic openings the Qur'an's selected core.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r4.anchor: وعن أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه : في كل كتا بسر وسر الله في القرآن أوائل السور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r5.speaker: ابن القيم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim reads Alif-Lam-Mim as the three articulation zones in order, symbolizing creation, worldly life and its laws, and resurrection; the Qur'an gathers what all humanity needs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r5.anchor: وأبدى الإمام شمس الدين ابن فقيم الجوزيه الدمشقي الحنبلي يفي كتاب به كالتذكرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r6.claim: Al-Harali gives metaphysical senses to Alif, Lam and Mim: encompassing authority, the link between hidden and manifest, and the perfected manifestation, with examples including Adam, angels and Muhammad.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r6.anchor: وقال الحرالي في تفسيره : ' الف ' اسم للقائم الأعلى المحيط ثم لكل مستخلف في القيام كآدم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r7.claim: Al-Harali says these signs are names when pronounced as alif, lam and mim; they are called letters only as word-parts without separate meaning, following al-Khalil's account of their names.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p29/r7.anchor: فينبغي أن يقال فيها أسماء وإن كانمت غير معلومة الدلالة كحروف ألف باء تاء فإنها كلها أسماء على ما فهمه الخليل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the alphabetic openings are the roots of God's first speech, translated into Arabic words and composed as the clear Qur'an; in heavenly scripture they signify the whole before its detailed unfolding.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r1.anchor: وأما حقيقتها فهي جوامع أصلها في ذمر أول من كلام الله تعالى فنزلت إلى الكلم العربية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r2.claim: Their comprehensive signs span existence from its hidden center to visible and audible revelation, and they did not appear in earlier books because creation was then incomplete; the final, complete Book fulfills their promised appearance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r2.anchor: ولأجل ما اقتضته من الجمع لم تنزل يفي كتاب متقدم لأن كتا بكل وقت مطابق بحال الكون فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r1.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r1.claim: The Prophet recited al-Fatiha one verse at a time and counted the basmala among its verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r1.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r2.claim: In a weak report, the Prophet promised Burayda a unique revealed verse or surah and identified the basmala when asked how to begin Quran recitation in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r2.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن بريدة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أخرج من المسجد حتى أخبرك بآية

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the basmala as a verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} آية

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan caused people to overlook the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: استرق الشيطان من الناس

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the basmala was revealed only to the Prophet, apart from its revelation to Solomon.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أغفل الناس آية من كتاب الله لم تنزل على أحد سوى النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r6.claim: In a weak report, Gabriel began delivering revelation to the Prophet with the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r6.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كان جبريل إذا جاءني بالوحي

DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r7.claim: Ibn Umar says the basmala was revealed in every surah.
DURR-FULL:v1p19#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: نزلت {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} في كل سورة

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r1.claim: The Prophet did not know where one surah ended until the basmala came; another wording says he then knew the next surah had begun.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r2.claim: Muslims recognized a surah's ending when the basmala was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r2.anchor: انقضاء السورة حتى تنزل {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r3.claim: In the Prophet's time, revelation of the basmala signaled that one surah had ended and another had come down.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه في عهد النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r4.claim: When Gabriel recited the basmala to the Prophet, he knew it was a surah.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا جاءه جبريل فقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} علم أنها سورة

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says people did not know the boundary between surahs until the basmala was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r5.anchor: السورتين حتى تنزل {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r6.claim: Ibn Umar recited the basmala in prayer at a surah's end, saying it was written in the codex to be recited.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه كان يقرأ في الصلاة {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فإذا ختم السورة قرأها

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet taught prayer and recited the basmala aloud in every rakah.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r7.anchor:
عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله علمني جبريل
الصلاة فقام فكبر لنا ثم قرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p20/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r8.claim: A report says Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Ibn al-Zubayr began recitation aloud with the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p20/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسجد إذ دخل رجل يصلي

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: The report says leaving the basmala means leaving a verse and thereby invalidating one's prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor:
فمن تركها فقد ترك آية
ومن ترك آية فقد أفسد عليه صلاته

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: Ali recited the basmala when beginning a surah in prayer and said omitting it diminishes the prayer; it completes the seven oft-repeated verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: عن علي أنه كان إذا افتتح السورة في الصلاة يقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} وكان يقول من ترك قراءتها فقد نقص

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Talha reports the Prophet saying that whoever leaves the basmala has left a verse of God's Book.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من ترك {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فقد ترك آية

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: معاوية
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: When Muawiya omitted the basmala and takbirs in prayer, the Emigrants and Helpers rebuked him; he then recited the basmala for al-Fatiha and the following surah and made the prostration takbir.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: يا معاوية أسرقت صلاتك أين {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} وأين التكبير

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri calls reciting the basmala part of prayer's sunnah and says Amr ibn Said ibn al-As was the first in Medina to recite it quietly, out of modesty.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: عن الزهري قال: من سنة الصلاة أن تقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} وإن أول من أسر

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet began prayer with the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يفتتح صلاته

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r7.speaker: علي وعمار
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r7.claim: Ali and Ammar say the Prophet recited the basmala aloud in obligatory prayers at the opening of al-Fatiha.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r7.anchor: أبي الطفيل قال: سمعت علي بن أبي طالب وعمار يقولان: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يجهر

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r8.speaker: نافع
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r8.claim: Nafi reports Ibn Umar's practice of reciting the basmala in al-Fatiha and the following surah, which Ibn Umar traced to hearing the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r8.anchor:
عن نافع
أن ابن عمر إذا افتتح الصلاة يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet recited the basmala aloud in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: كان رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p21/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r10.speaker: نعيم المجمر
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r10.claim: Nuaim heard Abu Hurayra recite the basmala and al-Fatiha through its end, say amin, and describe his prayer as resembling the Prophet's.
DURR-FULL:v1p21/r10.anchor: عن نعيم المجمر قال: كنت وراء أبي هريرة فقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} ثم قرأ (بأم القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet recited the basmala aloud in both surahs.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: كان النبي يجهر

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: The Prophet told Ali to say the basmala when beginning prayer instead of beginning directly with al-hamd.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: قال النبي كيف تقرأ إذا قمت إلى الصلاة قلت {الحمد لله رب العالمين} قال: قل {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: The Prophet similarly instructed Jabir to say the basmala when beginning prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف تقرأ إذا قمت إلى الصلاة قلت: أقرأ {الحمد لله رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar recited the basmala aloud.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: صليت خلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر وعمر فكانوا يجهرون

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Al-Numan ibn Bashir says Gabriel led the Prophet in prayer at the Kaaba and recited the basmala aloud.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال: قال رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: الحكم بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: Al-Hakam ibn Umayr says the Prophet recited the basmala aloud in night, dawn, and Friday prayers.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: عن الحكم بن عمير وكان بدريا قال صليت خلف النبي

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r7.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet recited the basmala aloud.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r7.anchor: عن عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يجهر

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi counts the basmala as part of al-Fatiha's seven verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: فاتحة الكتاب سبع آيات

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r9.claim: A report says the basmala is a name of God, nearly as close to His greatest name as the pupil is to the white of the eye.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r9.anchor: عن {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فقال هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v1p22/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r10.speaker: عيسى
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r10.claim: In a very weak report, Jesus explains the letters of the basmala: ba is God's majesty, sin His splendor, mim His dominion, and the names describe divine lordship and mercy.
DURR-FULL:v1p22/r10.anchor: بسند ضعيف جدا عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن عيسى بن مريم أسلمته أمه إلى الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the first revelation began with Gabriel telling Muhammad, “Bismillah”; the command means to read in God's name.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r1.anchor:
عن ابن عباس قال أول ما نزل جبريل على محمد قال له جبريل {بسم الله} يا محمد
يقول: اقرأ بذكر الله

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r2.claim: Allah means the one possessing divinity and worship, worshipped by all creation.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r2.anchor: ذو الألوهية والمعبودية على خلقه أجمعين

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r3.claim: Al-Rahman and al-Rahim describe mercy, with al-Rahim kind to those God wills to show mercy and severe toward those He wills to punish.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r3.anchor: الرفيق الرقيق بمن أحب أن يرحمه

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Allah as God's greatest name.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس قال: اسم الله الأعظم
هو الله

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r5.speaker: جابر بن يزيد
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r5.claim: Jabir ibn Yazid also says Allah is the greatest name, since the Quran places it before every other name.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r5.anchor:
عن جابر بن يزيد قال: اسم الله الأعظم
هو الله ألا ترى أنه في جميع
القرآن يبدأ به قبل كل اسم

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r6.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r6.claim: Al-Shabi identifies the greatest name as “Ya Allah.”
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r6.anchor:
الشعبي قال: اسم الله الأعظم
يا الله

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says al-Rahman is a name reserved for God.

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says al-Rahman applies to all creation, while al-Rahim is especially for believers.

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas describes al-Rahman as gentle and al-Rahim as caring for creation through provision; both names are subtle, one more so than the other.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال {الرحمن} وهو الرفيق {الرحيم} وهو العاطف على خلقه بالرزق

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r10.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r10.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says that when the name al-Rahman was separated from God's name, it became “al-Rahman al-Rahim.”
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r10.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال: كان الرحمن فلما اختزل الرحمن من اسمه كان {الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r11.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r11.claim: In a weak report, Aisha's father taught her a prophetic supplication asking the Merciful of this world and the next to relieve grief and need.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r11.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن عائشة قالت: قال لي أبي: ألا أعلمك دعاء علمنيه رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p23/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r12.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r12.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit says the Prophet taught a supplication seeking relief, response to the distressed, and mercy that makes one independent of others.
DURR-FULL:v1p23/r12.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو بهؤلاء الكلمات ويعلمهن

DURR-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: In the report that divides al-Fatiha between God and servants, God says the basmala invokes two gentle names, with al-Rahim gentler than al-Rahman.
DURR-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor:
فإذا قال العبد {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} قال الله: عبدي دعاني باسمين رقيقين
أحدهما أرق من الآخر

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r6.claim: Jabir reports that the basmala's revelation made clouds flee east, stilled the wind, stirred the sea, drew animals to listen, and caused devils to be pelted; God promised blessing on anything named with it.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} هرب الغيم إلى المشرق وسكنت الريح

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says reciting the basmala protects a person from each of the nineteen keepers of Hell, one shield for each letter.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: من أراد أن ينجيه الله من الزبانية التسعة عشر فليقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r8.claim: A marfu report promises the teacher, child, and child's parents immunity from the Fire when the teacher teaches the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا إن المعلم إذا قال للصبي قل {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} كتب للمعلم

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r9.speaker: البيهقي
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r9.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says “raqiqan” here is likely a scribal corruption for “rafiqan,” and al-Rafiq is one of God's names.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r9.anchor:
قال البيهقي: قوله: رقيقان
قيل هذا تصحيف وقع في الأصل وإنما هو رفيقان
والرفيق: من أسماء الله

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r1.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri says the basmala should not be written before poetry; al-Shabi reports dislike and consensus on that practice.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r1.anchor: عن الزهري قال: قضت السنة أن

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r2.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Shabi disliked a ritually impure person writing the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد والشعبي أنهما كرها أن يكتب الجنب {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r3.claim: A weak report says God forgives one who writes the basmala beautifully out of reverence for Him.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r3.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كتب {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} مجودة

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r4.claim: Ali says a man was forgiven for taking care over the writing of the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: تنوق رجل في {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فغفر له

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet instructs scribes not to extend the ba to the mim before raising the sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r6.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r6.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Prophet prohibited extending the basmala in writing.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r6.anchor: عن الزهري قال: نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تمد {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r7.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin disliked connecting the ba directly to the mim before writing the sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r7.anchor:
عن محمد بن سيرين
أنه كان يكره أن يمد الباء إلى الميم حتى يكتب السين

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r8.speaker: يزيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r8.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet tells scribes to make the sin distinct in the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r8.anchor: عن يزيد بن ثابت قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كتبت {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فبين السين فيه

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r9.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r9.claim: A report from Anas attributes to the Prophet an instruction to extend the writing of al-Rahman.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r9.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي قال إذا كتب أحدكم {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فليمد الرحمن

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r10.speaker: معاوية
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r10.claim: A report gives Muawiya detailed calligraphic directions: shape the ba, distinguish the sin, form the mim, beautify Allah and al-Rahim, and extend al-Rahman.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r10.anchor: ألق الدواة وحرف القلم وانصب الباء وفرق السين

DURR-FULL:v1p27/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r11.speaker: مطر الوراق
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r11.claim: Matar al-Warraq says the Prophet directed Muawiya to connect the ba and sin and forbade lengthening any divine name in writing or recitation.
DURR-FULL:v1p27/r11.anchor: عن مطر الوراق قال كان معاوية بن أبي سفيان كاتب رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Muslim ibn Yasar disliked writing “bm” in place of the basmala because that drops the sin; other reports describe reprimands and punishment for the same omission.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: عن مسلم بن يسار أنه كان يكره أن يكتب (بم) حين يبدأ

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r2.speaker: ابن عون
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r2.claim: When Ibn Awn wrote “bm” for Ibn Sirin, Ibn Sirin demanded that he write the sin, warning against unwitting sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r2.anchor:
عن ابن عون أنه كتب لابن سيرين (بم) فقال: مه
اكتب سينا
اتقوا أن يأثم أحدكم

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r3.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r3.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz punished and dismissed a scribe for writing the mim before the sin or omitting the sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r3.anchor:
عن عمران بن عون
أن عمر بن عبد العزيز ضرب كاتبا كتب الميم قبل السين

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin strongly opposed extending the ba to the mim without first writing the sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين أنه كان يكره أن يكتب الباء ثم يمدها إلى الميم حتى يكتب السين

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r5.speaker: الليث
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r5.claim: Al-Layth objected when a writer lengthened the ba so much that it resembled a lam and changed the meaning.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن صالح قال: كتبت {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} ورفعت الباء فطالت فأنكر ذلك الليث

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: A mursal report says the Prophet condemned writing the basmala on the ground and instructed that it be placed in its proper place.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على كتاب في الأرض فقال لفتى معه ما في هذا

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r7.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r7.claim: A marfu report promises that one who lifts a paper bearing the basmala out of reverence is counted among the truthful and brings relief to parents, even if unbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r7.anchor: عن أنس مرفوعا من رفع قرطاسا من الأرض فيه {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} إجلالا له أن يداس

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r8.speaker: أم خالد بن خالد بن سعيد بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r8.claim: Umm Khalid claims she was the first to write the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r8.anchor: عن أم خالد بن خالد بن سعيد بن العاص

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r9.claim: A report says Quraysh mocked the Prophet in Mecca when he pronounced the basmala.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة فقال {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فقالت قريش

DURR-FULL:v1p28/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r10.claim: A mursal report says Meccans mocked the Prophet's aloud basmala by associating al-Rahman with Musaylima, so he ordered it concealed and did not recite it aloud again.
DURR-FULL:v1p28/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجهر {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} بمكة

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r1.claim: The report continues that Meccans said Muhammad called on the Yamama deity and that the Prophet then concealed the basmala until his death.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r1.anchor: فقالوا: إن محمدا يدعو إلى إله اليمامة فأمر رسول الله بإخفائها فما جهر بها حتى مات

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the polytheists mocked the basmala because Musaylima called himself al-Rahman, after which the Prophet was ordered not to recite it aloud.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} هزأ منه المشركون

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r3.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar recited the basmala quietly.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r3.anchor: عن أنس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يسر {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} وأبو بكر وعمر

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r4.claim: Ibn Mughaffal called his son's aloud basmala a new practice and said he never heard the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, or Uthman recite it aloud.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r4.anchor: عن ابن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: سمعني أبي وأنا أقرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فقال: أي بني محدث

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas calls aloud recitation of the basmala the Bedouin style of recitation.

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r6.claim: Ibrahim says an imam's aloud recitation of the basmala is an innovation.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r6.anchor:
عن إبراهيم قال: جهر الإمام {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}
بدعة

DURR-FULL:v1p29/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r7.claim: Al-Hasan instructed scribes to write the basmala at the start of the codex and put a line between surahs.
DURR-FULL:v1p29/r7.anchor: عن يحيى بن عتيق قال: كان الحسن يقول: اكتبوا في أول الإمام {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as verse one, al-hamd as two, al-Rahman al-Rahim as three, Malik yawm al-din as four, then indicated five for the next verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في الصلاة {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} فعدها آية {الحمد لله رب العالمين} آيتين

RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r1.claim: The opening formula marks the beginning of all good deeds and commanded acts.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r1.anchor: نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies Sūrat al-Fātiḥa as Meccan and says it has seven verses.

RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r2.claim: He notes the widely held report that God has 1,001 sacred names found in the Qur’an and Sunna, and says studying each name is a noble discipline requiring knowledge of the named entity, proofs for its existence, and responses to objections, collectively thousands of questions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r2.anchor: قد اشتهر عند العلماء أن لله تعالى ألفا وواحدا من الأسماء المقدسة المطهرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r3.claim: The bāʾ in the basmala expresses adhesion and attaches to an elided verb understood as I begin performing acts of obedience in God’s name; unpacking this involves true beliefs, pure deeds, proofs, and answers to objections, perhaps over ten thousand questions.

RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r4.claim: Seeking refuge in God signifies rejecting improper beliefs and deeds, while saying in God’s name signifies adopting proper beliefs and deeds; sound reason confirms this order.
RAZI-FULL:v1p17/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى نفي ما لا ينبغي من العقائد والأعمال

TAB:1:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r1.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies al-Fātiḥa as a Meccan sūra consisting of seven verses.

TAB:1:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:1/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī calls the report sound: the Prophet names al-Fātiḥa the Mother of the Qurʾān, the Opening of the Book, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
TAB:1:1/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قال : هي أمّ القرآن ، وهي فاتحة الكتاب

TAB:1:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r3.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r3.claim: It is called the Opening of the Book because it begins written Qurʾāns and is recited in prayers, opening the following sūras in writing and recitation.
TAB:1:1/r3.anchor: يفتتح بكتابتها المصاحف ، ويُقرأ بها في الصلوات ، فهي فواتح لما يتلوها من سور القرآن

TAB:1:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r4.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r4.claim: It is the Mother of the Qurʾān because it precedes the other sūras in reading and writing, while they follow it.
TAB:1:1/r4.anchor: لتقدمها على سائر سور القرآن غيرها ، وتأخُّر ما سواها خلفها في القراءة والكتابة .

TAB:1:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r5.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r5.claim: Arab usage calls a comprehensive or leading thing with dependent followers an “umm”; examples include the membrane around the brain and an army’s gathering banner.
TAB:1:1/r5.anchor: كل جامع أمرًا -أو مقدِّمٍ لأمر إذا كانت له توابعُ تتبعه ، هو لها إمام جامع- " أمًّا "

TAB:1:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r6.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r6.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s banner poem uses “umm” for the standard around which companions gather for travel and battle.
TAB:1:1/r6.anchor: يعني بقوله : " على رأسه أمٌّ لنا " ، أي على رأس الرمح رايةٌ يجتمعون لها

TAB:1:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r7.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r7.claim: Two explanations are reported for Mecca as “Mother of the Towns”: it precedes and gathers the towns, or the earth was spread out from it.
TAB:1:1/r7.anchor: وقد قيل إن مكة سميت " أمّ القُرى " ، لتقدُّمها أمامَ جميعِها ، وجَمْعِها ما سواها . وقيل

TAB:1:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r8.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r8.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Thawr’s verse calls fifty one’s “mother” because it encompasses all numbers below it.
TAB:1:1/r8.anchor: قولُ حُميد بن ثَوْر الهلاليّ : إذا كانتِ الخمسُونَ أُمَّكَ ، لم يكنْ *** لِدائك ،

TAB:1:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r9.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r9.claim: All Qurʾān readers and scholars agree that al-Fātiḥa has seven verses; they disagree over which words make the count seven.
TAB:1:1/r9.anchor: فإنها سبعُ آيات ، لا خلاف بين الجميع من القراء والعلماء في ذلك . وإنما اختلفوا

TAB:1:1/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r10.speaker: عُظْم أهل الكوفة
TAB:1:1/r10.claim: Most Kufan authorities count the basmala as one of al-Fātiḥa’s seven verses; this view is also transmitted from a group of Companions and Successors.
TAB:1:1/r10.anchor: فقال عُظْم أهل الكوفة : صارت سبع آيات ب { بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ } ورُوي ذلك عن جماعة

TAB:1:1/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r11.speaker: عظم قرأة أهل المدينة ومتقنيهم
TAB:1:1/r11.claim: Most leading Medinan reciters exclude the basmala from the seven and count “those You favored” as the seventh verse.
TAB:1:1/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون : هي سبع آيات ، وليس منهن { بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ } ولكن السابعة " أنعمت عليهم " . وذلك قول عُظْم قَرَأةِ أهل المدينة

TAB:1:1/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r12.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says he has treated the correct count elsewhere and will give the full disagreement in another legal work, without resolving it in this passage.
TAB:1:1/r12.anchor: قال أبو جعفر : وقد بيّنا الصواب من القول عندنا في ذلك في كتابنا : ( اللطيف في أحكام شرائع الإسلام )

TAB:1:1/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r13.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r13.claim: The seven are “oft-repeated” because al-Fātiḥa is recited in every prayer, obligatory or voluntary.
TAB:1:1/r13.anchor: فلأنها تثنى قراءتها في كل صلاة وتطوع ومكتوبة

TAB:1:1/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r14.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB:1:1/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the seven oft-repeated verses as al-Fātiḥa and explains that it is repeated in every recitation—or, as the narrator hesitates, every prayer.
TAB:1:1/r14.anchor: عن أبي رجاء ، قال سألت الحسن عن قوله : { وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ سَبْعًا مِنَ الْمَثَانِي

TAB:1:1/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r15.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r15.claim: Abū al-Najm’s verse pairs al-Fātiḥa’s praise with the Qurʾān and the “oft-repeated,” supporting the name’s association with al-Fātiḥa.
TAB:1:1/r15.anchor: قصد أبو النجم العجلي بقوله : الحمد لله الذي عافاني *** وكل خير بعده أعطاني

TAB:1:1/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r16.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r16.claim: An anonymous rajaz verse likewise calls the Mother of the Book seven oft-repeated verses, describing them as doubled from the Qurʾān’s verses.
TAB:1:1/r16.anchor: وكذلك قول الراجز الآخر : نشدتكم بمنزل الفرقان *** أم الكتاب السبع من مثاني ثنين من آي من القرآن

TAB:1:1/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r17.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r17.claim: Calling al-Fātiḥa the seven oft-repeated does not prevent the whole Qurʾān, or the sūras following the hundred-verse group, from also being called “mathānī” for another understood reason.
TAB:1:1/r17.anchor: وليس في وجوب اسم " السبع المثاني " لفاتحة الكتاب ، ما يدفع صحة وجوب اسم " المثاني " للقرآن كله

TAB:1:1/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r18.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r18.claim: “Seeking refuge” means seeking protection or asylum.
TAB:1:1/r18.anchor: قال أبو جعفر : والاستعاذة : الاستجارة . وتأويل قول القائل :

TAB:1:1/r19.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r19.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r19.claim: The refuge formula means asking God alone to protect one from Satan harming one’s religion or diverting one from a duty owed to the Lord.
TAB:1:1/r19.anchor: وتأويل قول القائل : { أَعُوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ } أستجيرُ بالله - دون غيره من سائر خلقه - من الشيطان

TAB:1:1/r20.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r20.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r20.claim: In Arabic, “Satan” can mean any rebellious being among jinn, humans, animals, or anything else; the Qurʾān accordingly speaks of human and jinn satans.
TAB:1:1/r20.anchor: والشيطان ، في كلام العرب : كل متمرِّد من الجن والإنس والدوابِّ وكل شيء

TAB:1:1/r21.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r21.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB:1:1/r21.claim: When a bucking barẕawn kept prancing despite ʿUmar’s blows, he dismounted and called it a satan that had made him lose himself.
TAB:1:1/r21.anchor: وقال عمر بن الخطاب رحمة الله عليه ، وركب بِرذَوْنًا فجعل يتبختر به ، فجعل يضربه فلا يزداد إلا تبخترًا

TAB:1:1/r22.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r22.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r22.claim: A rebel is called a satan for departing from its kind’s usual character and deeds and for being far from good; another proposed derivation connects the word with “being distant.”
TAB:1:1/r22.anchor: شيطانًا ، لمفارقة أخلاقه وأفعاله أخلاقَ سائر جنسه وأفعاله ، وبُعدِه من الخير . وقد قيل

TAB:1:1/r23.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r23.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r23.claim: Al-Nābigha’s “shatūn” means distant, supporting a derivation of “Satan” as fayʿāl from shatana.
TAB:1:1/r23.anchor: ومن ذلك قول نابغة بني ذبيان : نأتْ بسُعادَ عنك نوى شطونُ *** فبانت ، والفؤاد بها رهينُ

TAB:1:1/r24.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r24.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r24.claim: Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s “shāṭin” supports shatana yashṭunu; if the word came from shāṭa yashīṭ, the form would be “shāʾiṭ.”
TAB:1:1/r24.anchor: ومما يدل على أن ذلك كذلك ، قول أمية ابن أبي الصلت : أيما شاطن عصاه عكاه *** ثم يلقى في السجن والأكبال

TAB:1:1/r25.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r25.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r25.claim: “Rajīm” is a passive faʿīl form meaning accursed or reviled; “stoning” can be verbal abuse or physical throwing.
TAB:1:1/r25.anchor: وأما الرجيم فهو : فعيل بمعنى مفعول ، كقول القائل : كف خضيب ، ولحية دهين ، ورجل لعين ، يريد بذلك : مخضوبة ومدهونة وملعون . وتأويل الرجيم : الملعون المشتوم

TAB:1:1/r26.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r26.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r26.claim: Abraham’s father uses “stone you” as a verbal threat, illustrating that rajm can be done with speech.
TAB:1:1/r26.anchor: ومن الرجم بالقول قول أبي إبراهيم لإبراهيم صلوات الله عليه : { لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ لأرْجُمَنَّكَ }

TAB:1:1/r27.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r27.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r27.claim: Satan may also be called “the stoned” because God expelled him from heaven and pelted him with piercing meteors.
TAB:1:1/r27.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون قِيل للشيطان رجيمٌ ، لأن الله جل ثناؤه طرَده من سَمواته ، ورجمه بالشُّهب الثَّواقِب .

TAB:1:1/r28.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r28.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB:1:1/r28.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Gabriel first taught Muhammad to seek refuge, then say the basmala, then recite 96:1; Ibn ʿAbbās calls this the first sūra revealed through Gabriel.
TAB:1:1/r28.anchor: عن الضحّاك ، عن عبد الله بن عباس ، قال : أول ما نزل جبريلُ على محمد قال : " يا محمد استعذ ، قل : أستعيذ بالسميع العليم

TAB:1:1/r29.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r29.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r29.claim: God taught the Prophet to put His beautiful names before all actions and made this instruction a practice for everyone beginning speech, letters, books, or needs.
TAB:1:1/r29.anchor: أدّب نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بتعليمه تقديم ذكر أسمائه الحسنى أمام جميع أفعاله

TAB:1:1/r30.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r30.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r30.claim: The preposition bāʾ requires a governing verb, omitted here; the listener supplies it from the act underway, just as an answer like “food” can omit an already evident verb.
TAB:1:1/r30.anchor: وذلك أن الباء من «بسم الله » مقتضيةٌ فعلاً يكون لها جالبا ، ولا فعل معها ظاهر

TAB:1:1/r31.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r31.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r31.claim: Before reciting, standing, sitting, or another action, the phrase means beginning that act by naming and remembering God.
TAB:1:1/r31.anchor: وإنما معنى قوله «بسم الله » : أبدأ بتسمية الله وذكره قبل كل شيء ، أو أقرأ بتسمية الله

TAB:1:1/r32.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r32.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB:1:1/r32.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās’s report, Gabriel glosses the basmala as reading, standing, and sitting in remembrance of God.
TAB:1:1/r32.anchor: قال له جبريل : قل بسم الله يا محمد . يقول : اقرأ بذكر الله ربك ، وقم واقعد بذكر الله

TAB:1:1/r33.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r33.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r33.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects construing the phrase as “by God” in every act: it means beginning with God’s naming and remembrance, not claiming that an action is performed by God.
TAB:1:1/r33.anchor: وإنما معنى قوله «بسم الله » : أبدأ بتسمية الله وذكره قبل كل شيء ، أو أقرأ بتسمية الله

TAB:1:1/r34.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r34.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r34.claim: The scholarly consensus that saying “by God” at slaughter does not fulfill the prescribed “in the name of God” supports his distinction between the formula and “by God.”
TAB:1:1/r34.anchor: ولا خلاف بين الجميع من علماء الأمة ، أن قائلاً لو قال عند تذكيته بعض بهائم الأنعام : «بالله » ، ولم يقل «بسم الله »

TAB:1:1/r35.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r35.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r35.claim: Here “name” stands for “naming”: Arabic often uses a verbal noun in a form different from its regular pattern, as in karāmah for ikrām and kalām for taklīm.
TAB:1:1/r35.anchor: فجعل الاسم مكان التسمية ، كما جعل الكلام مكان التكليم ، والعطاء مكان الإعطاء

TAB:1:1/r36.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r36.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r36.claim: Poetic examples use ʿaṭāʾ for iʿṭāʾ, ṭawl for iṭāla, and muṣāba for iṣāba, supporting the unusual verbal-noun form in the basmala.
TAB:1:1/r36.anchor: قول الشاعر : أكفرا بعد ردّ الموت عنّي *** وبعد عطائك المائة الرّتاعا

TAB:1:1/r37.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r37.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:1/r37.claim: A report has Jesus explain the letters of “bism” as God’s glory, splendor, and kingdom; al-Ṭabarī suspects a transmitter’s error and thinks separate alphabet letters may have been run together, since the gloss makes no sense in the full basmala.
TAB:1:1/r37.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إن عيسى ابن مريم أسلمته أمه إلى الكتّاب ليعلّمه ، فقال له المعلم : اكتب بسم

TAB:1:1/r38.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r38.speaker: مقدم في العلم بلغة العرب
TAB:1:1/r38.claim: An unnamed authority in Arabic usage reads Lubayd’s “then the name of peace be upon you” as simply “then peace be upon you”; al-Ṭabarī rejects that reading as linguistically unsound.
TAB:1:1/r38.anchor: فقد تأوّله مقدم في العلم بلغة العرب ، أنه معنيّ به : ثم السلام عليكما

TAB:1:1/r39.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r39.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r39.claim: If “name” could simply mean its referent, Arabic would also permit “I ate the name of honey”; the unanimous rejection of such usage undermines that reading of Lubayd.
TAB:1:1/r39.anchor: لو جاز ذلك وصح تأويله فيه على ما تأوّل ، لجاز أن يقال : رأيت اسم زيد ، وأكلت اسم الطعام

TAB:1:1/r40.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r40.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r40.claim: Al-Ṭabarī’s likelier reading of Lubayd is an exhortation to keep God’s name and remembrance after a delayed exhortative word, while leaving off remembering and grieving for the dead.
TAB:1:1/r40.anchor: يعني : عليكما اسم السلام ، أي : الزما ما ذكر الله ، ودعا ذكري والوجد بي

TAB:1:1/r41.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r41.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r41.claim: A second possible reading of Lubayd invokes God’s name for protection over the two people.
TAB:1:1/r41.anchor: ثم اسم الله عليكما من السوء

TAB:1:1/r42.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r42.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r42.claim: To support the delayed exhortation reading, al-Ṭabarī cites Arabic word order that places the thing urged before the delayed “take it” command.
TAB:1:1/r42.anchor: ومن ذلك قول الشاعر : يا أيها المائح دلوي دونكا *** إني رأيت الناس يحمدونكا

TAB:1:1/r43.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r43.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB:1:1/r43.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains Allah as the one worshipped by every thing and served by all creation.
TAB:1:1/r43.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس ، قال : الله ذو الألوهية والمعبودية على خلقه أجمعين

TAB:1:1/r44.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r44.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r44.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives Allah from al-ilāh by inference rather than direct attestation; ilāh means the worshipped one, supported by Arab use of taʾallaha for worship and seeking God.
TAB:1:1/r44.anchor: أما سماعا من العرب فلا ، ولكن استدلالاً

TAB:1:1/r45.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r45.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r45.claim: Ruʾba’s “min taʾalluhī” means devotion and seeking God through worship, showing the root’s sense.
TAB:1:1/r45.anchor: قول رؤبة بن العجاج : لله در الغانيات المدة *** سبحن واسترجعن من تألهي

TAB:1:1/r46.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r46.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TAB:1:1/r46.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd Allāh, and Mujāhid read “wa-ilāhataka” at 7:127 as “your worship”; Pharaoh was worshipped rather than worshipping.
TAB:1:1/r46.anchor: حدثنا به سفيان بن وكيع ، قال حدثنا أبي ، عن نافع بن عمر ، عن عمرو بن دينار ، عن ابن عباس ، أنه قرأ : «وَيَذَرَكَ وَإلاهَتَكَ » قال : عبادتك

TAB:1:1/r47.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r47.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:1/r47.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet has Jesus gloss Allah as “the god of gods,” which al-Ṭabarī uses in explaining how God is worshipped by the servant and worships the servant in the stated idiom.
TAB:1:1/r47.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إنّ عيسى أسلمته أمه إلى الكتّاب ليعلّمه ، فقال له المعلم : اكتب الله ، فقال له عيسى : أتدري ما الله ؟ الله إله الآلهة »

TAB:1:1/r48.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r48.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r48.claim: Allah’s form comes from al-ilāh: the initial hamza is dropped, then the two lām sounds meet and assimilate into one doubled lām.
TAB:1:1/r48.anchor: فكذلك الله ، أصله الإله ، أسقطت الهمزة ، التي هي فاء الاسم ، فالتقت اللام

TAB:1:1/r49.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r49.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r49.claim: The contraction is comparable to “lākinn huwa Allāh rabbī” from “lākinn anā huwa Allāh rabbī,” and to the poem’s “lākinn iyyāki” from “lākinn anā iyyāki.”
TAB:1:1/r49.anchor: كما جاز أن يكون قوله : لكن هو الله ربي أصله : «لكن أنا هو الله ربي »

TAB:1:1/r50.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r50.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r50.claim: “Al-Raḥmān” follows faʿlān from raḥima, like ghaḍbān, sakrān, and ʿaṭshān from their verbs.
TAB:1:1/r50.anchor: أما الرحمن ، فهو «فعلان » ، من رحم ، والرحيم فعيل منه . والعرب كثيرا ما تبني الأسماء من فعل يفعل على فعلان

TAB:1:1/r51.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r51.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r51.claim: “Raḥīm” follows faʿīl as a form of praise; Arabic uses faʿīl for praise or blame even when the verb’s vowel differs, as in ʿālim/ʿalīm and qādir/qadīr.
TAB:1:1/r51.anchor: ومن شأن العرب أن يحملوا أبنية الأسماء إذا كان فيها مدح أو ذم على فعيل

TAB:1:1/r52.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r52.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r52.claim: In Arabic, al-Raḥmān is farther from the ordinary faʿila yafʿalu pattern than al-Raḥīm, and that greater departure intensifies praise.
TAB:1:1/r52.anchor: أن قول القائل «الرحمن » عن أبنية الأسماء من «فَعِلَ يَفْعَل » أشدّ عدولاً من قوله «الرحيم »

TAB:1:1/r53.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r53.speaker: العرزمي
TAB:1:1/r53.claim: Al-ʿArzami says al-Raḥmān extends mercy to all creation, while al-Raḥīm is mercy toward believers.
TAB:1:1/r53.anchor: سمعت العرزمي يقول : «الرحمن الرحيم » قال : الرحمن بجميع الخلق . «الرحيم » قال : بالمؤمنين

TAB:1:1/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r54.speaker: عيسى ابن مريم
TAB:1:1/r54.claim: A report says Jesus distinguished al-Raḥmān as mercy in this world and the next, and al-Raḥīm as mercy in the next world.
TAB:1:1/r54.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إنّ عيسى ابن مريم قال : الرحمن : رحمن الآخرة والدنيا ، والرحيم : رحيم الآخرة »

TAB:1:1/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r55.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both transmitted distinctions: al-Raḥmān denotes God’s mercy to all creation, while al-Raḥīm denotes mercy specified for some, whether in this life, the next, or both.
TAB:1:1/r55.anchor: لجميعهما عندنا في الصحة مخرج ، فلا وجه لقول قائل : أيهما أولى بالصحة

TAB:1:1/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r56.claim: God’s universal worldly mercy includes provision, rain-bearing clouds, plants, bodily and mental health, and countless other blessings shared by believers and unbelievers.
TAB:1:1/r56.anchor: في البسط في الرزق ، وتسخير السحاب بالغيث ، وإخراج النبات من الأرض ، وصحة الأجسام والعقول

TAB:1:1/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r57.claim: In the hereafter, universal mercy means God’s just judgment: He wrongs no one even by an atom’s weight and repays each soul for what it earned.
TAB:1:1/r57.anchor: تسويته بين جميعهم جل ذكره في عدله وقضائه ، فلا يظلم أحدا منهم مثقال ذرة

TAB:1:1/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r58.claim: God’s special mercy to believers in this life is the gracious aid that enables obedience, faith, following revelation, and avoiding sin, which He withholds from those He leaves astray.
TAB:1:1/r58.anchor: ما وصفنا من اللطف لهم في دينهم ، فخصهم به دون من خذله من أهل الكفر به

TAB:1:1/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r59.claim: In the next life, special mercy to believers is the lasting bliss, triumph, and honor prepared for them rather than unbelievers.
TAB:1:1/r59.anchor: ما أعدّ لهم دون غيرهم من النعيم والكرامة التي تقصر عنها الأماني

TAB:1:1/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r60.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB:1:1/r60.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-Raḥmān as tender toward those God wills to show mercy, and al-Raḥīm as gentle toward those He wills to treat gently, but severe toward those He wills to chastise.
TAB:1:1/r60.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس ، قال : الرحمن الفعلان من الرحمة ، وهو من كلام العرب . قال : الرحمن الرحيم : الرقيق الرفيق بمن أحب أن يرحمه

TAB:1:1/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r61.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r61.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the Prophet-attributed and al-ʿArzami distinctions to Ibn ʿAbbās’s account, while acknowledging that Ibn ʿAbbās also gives the words distinguishable meanings.
TAB:1:1/r61.anchor: والقول الذي رويناه في تأويل ذلك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكرناه عن العرزمي ، أشبه بتأويله

TAB:1:1/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r62.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
TAB:1:1/r62.claim: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says God’s name was al-Raḥmān, then paired it with al-Raḥīm after the impostor Musaylima appropriated al-Raḥmān.
TAB:1:1/r62.anchor: سمعت عطاء الخراساني ، يقول : كان الرحمن ، فلما اختزل الرحمن من اسمه كان الرحمن الرحيم

TAB:1:1/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r63.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r63.claim: Al-Ṭabarī considers ʿAṭāʾ’s explanation plausible: God uniquely combines the two names to distinguish His name, even if their individual meanings differ or overlap.
TAB:1:1/r63.anchor: بل جائز أن يكون جل ثناؤه خص نفسه بالتسمية بهما معا مجتمعين إبانة لها من خلقه

TAB:1:1/r64.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r64.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r64.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the claim that Arabs did not know “al-Raḥmān”: denial by polytheists does not prove ignorance, just as people who know Muhammad can still reject him.
TAB:1:1/r64.anchor: وقد زعم بعض أهل الغباء أن العرب كانت لا تعرف الرحمن ولم يكن ذلك في لغتها

TAB:1:1/r65.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r65.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r65.claim: Pre-Islamic verses by an unnamed poet and Salāma ibn Jandal use “al-Raḥmān,” demonstrating that the name was known among Arabs.
TAB:1:1/r65.anchor: وقال سلامة بن جندل الطهوي : عجلتم علينا عجلتينا عليكم *** وما يشاء الرحمن يعقد ويطلق

TAB:1:1/r66.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r66.speaker: بعض من ضعفت معرفته بتأويل أهل التأويل
TAB:1:1/r66.claim: An unnamed, weakly informed interpreter equates al-Raḥmān with “possessor of mercy” and al-Raḥīm with “merciful,” then inconsistently treats the pair as equivalent forms like nadmān and nadīm.
TAB:1:1/r66.anchor: أن «الرحمن » مجازه «ذو الرحمة » ، و«الرحيم » مجازه «الراحم » . ثم قال : قد يقدرون اللفظين من لفظ والمعنى واحد

TAB:1:1/r67.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r67.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r67.claim: Al-Ṭabarī objects that “possessor of mercy” asserts an established attribute, whereas “merciful” can describe past, present, or future action; the terms therefore do not simply mean the same thing.
TAB:1:1/r67.anchor: أن ذا الرحمة هو الذي ثبت أن له الرحمة وصح أنها له صفة ، وأن الراحم هو الموصوف بأنه سيرحم

TAB:1:1/r68.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r68.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r68.claim: Arabic normally names the subject first and follows it with attributes, so the sequence places the referent before its descriptions.
TAB:1:1/r68.anchor: من شأن العرب إذا أرادوا الخبر عن مخبر عنه أن يقدموا اسمه ، ثم يتبعوه صفاته ونعوته

TAB:1:1/r69.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r69.speaker: author
TAB:1:1/r69.claim: The order puts Allah first because worship belongs to Him alone, al-Raḥmān next because it is also reserved for Him, and al-Raḥīm last because creatures may share some quality of mercy.
TAB:1:1/r69.anchor: فبدأ الله جل ذكره باسمه الذي هو الله لأن الألوهية ليست لغيره جل ثناؤه بوجه من الوجوه

TAB:1:1/r70.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:1/r70.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB:1:1/r70.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says al-Raḥmān is a name barred from use by others; al-Ṭabarī adds that the community’s consensus on the prohibition suffices as proof.
TAB:1:1/r70.anchor: حدثنا محمد بن بشار ، قال : حدثنا حماد بن مسعدة ، عن عوف ، عن الحسن ، قال : الرحمن اسم ممنوع .

TAB:1:7/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r54.speaker: أهل الإلحاد الطاعنون في القرآن
TAB:1:7/r54.claim: Critics ask why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses when, they argue, the meaning of its remaining verses is already contained in “Master of Judgment Day” and “You alone we worship and ask for help.”
TAB:1:7/r54.anchor: فما الوجه إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفت في إطالة الكلام بمثل سورة أم القرآن بسبع آيات

TAB:1:7/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r55.claim: Earlier scriptures each contain some meanings found together in the Qur'an: the Torah gives admonitions and detail, the Psalms praise and glorify, and the Gospel admonishes and reminds; the Qur'an gathers these and adds more.
TAB:1:7/r55.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل ، والزّبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد ، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير

TAB:1:7/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prior books lack a miracle certifying their recipients, whereas the Qur'an's unmatched composition defeats all attempts to produce even a short surah and proves Muhammad's prophethood.
TAB:1:7/r56.anchor: نظمه العجيب ، ورصفه الغريب ، وتأليفه البديع ، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB:1:7/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r57.claim: The Qur'an's varied contents—encouragement, warning, commands, prohibitions, stories, argument, and parables—also make its extended expression purposeful.

TAB:1:7/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Fātiḥa's inimitable arrangement proves prophethood, while its praise and glorification direct people to recognize God's greatness, sovereignty, power, and dominion and to thank Him for His favors.
TAB:1:7/r58.anchor: ليذكروه بآلائه ويحمدوه على نعمائه ، فيستحقوا به منه المزيد ويستوجبوا عليه الثواب الجزيل

TAB:1:7/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r59.claim: The account of those favored through knowledge of God and His enabling teaches that every religious and worldly blessing comes from Him, directing requests to God rather than idols or rivals.
TAB:1:7/r59.anchor: تعريف عباده أن كل ما بهم من نعمة في دينهم ودنياهم فمنه ، ليصرفوا رغبتهم إليه

TAB:1:7/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r60.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r60.claim: Recounting punishments for disobedience warns people away from sin and from incurring God's anger, whose consequences lead to destruction.
TAB:1:7/r60.anchor: ترهيب عباده عن ركوب معاصيه ، والتعرض لما لا قبل لهم به من سخطه

TAB:1:7/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r61.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r61.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God answers the worshipper's recitation: He calls al-ḥamdu praise, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm commendation, Mālik Yawm al-Dīn glorification, and the rest of the surah the servant's share.
TAB:1:7/r61.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله : حمدني عبدي

TAB:1:7/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r62.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:1:7/r62.claim: A second Abū Hurayra version gives the same recitation exchange but is not attributed to the Prophet.
TAB:1:7/r62.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله ، فذكر نحوه ، ولم يرفعه

TAB:1:7/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r63.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r63.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the divine saying that the prayer is divided between God and His servant, with the servant receiving what he asks; the first three praises are God's, and what follows is for the servant.
TAB:1:7/r63.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.speaker: بعض النصارى
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.claim: He also quotes a Christian's parody of al-Fatiha as another failed counter-imitation.

BURHAN:v1p73/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the basmala and makes the rest of 1:7 one verse; Abu Hanifa omits the basmala and divides its two phrases. Both count seven verses, but al-Shafiʿi's division better preserves the endings because anʿamta ʿalayhim does not match prior endings.
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.anchor: وبهذا يترجح مذهب الشافعى على مذهب أبى حنيفة فى عد الفاتحة سبع آيات مع البسملة

BURHAN:v1p348/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p348/r6.speaker: أم سلمة
BURHAN:v1p348/r6.claim: A report from Umm Salama says the Prophet divided his recitation verse by verse; some later scholars therefore objected to stopping mid-verse for meaning.
BURHAN:v1p348/r6.anchor: وهكذا روت أم سلمة أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقطع قراءته آية آية ومعنى هذا الوقف على رءوس الآي

BURHAN:v1p390/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.claim: The omitted alif in bism signals the name’s elevated, unique rank and its connection to God, whose name gathers all names; the spelling also evokes manifestation and hiddenness.
BURHAN:v1p390/r1.anchor: تنبيها على علوه فى أول رتبة الأسماء وانفراده

BURHAN:v1p390/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p390/r2.claim: The omitted alif in al-Rahman reflects that people know mercy’s effects but entrust knowledge of its full reality to God.
BURHAN:v1p390/r2.anchor: وكذلك حذفت الألف قبل النون من اسمه الرحمن حيث وقع بيانا لأنا نعلم حقائق تفصيل رحمته

BURHAN:v1p390/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.speaker: علماء الظاهر
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.claim: The outward scholars explain the omission as abbreviation from frequent use: the alif of ism is dropped only when appended to Allah and preceded by ba according to the majority.
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.anchor: وعلماء الظاهر يقولون للاختصار وكثرة الاستعمال وهو من خصائص الجلالة الشريفة

BURHAN:v1p390/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi does not require the preceding ba and permits deletion in forms such as bism al-malik; the majority requires ba.
BURHAN:v1p390/r4.anchor: ولم يشترط الكسائى الثانى فجوز حذفها كما تحذف فى بسم الملك والجمهور على الأول

BURHAN:v1p390/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p390/r5.claim: Alif is also omitted from some active-participle forms such as qadara and ʿalima because it lies inside the word.
BURHAN:v1p390/r5.anchor: وكذلك حذف الألف فى كثير من أسماء الفاعلين مثل قدر وعلم وذلك أن هذه الألف فى وسط الكلمة

BURHAN:v1p390/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p390/r6.claim: In sound and broken plurals, a surplus alif is deleted when the detailed meaning is latent and retained when it is manifest.
BURHAN:v1p390/r6.anchor: فإنها كلها وردت لمعنى مفصل يشتمل عليه معنى تلك اللفظة فتحذف حيث يبطن التفصيل وتثبت حيث يظهر

BURHAN:v3p110/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p110/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p110/r3.claim: The preposition in بسم الله requires a complement; the activity begun supplies it, such as أقرأ or آكل. Grammarians differ whether it is a verb or noun and whether general or specific.
BURHAN:v3p110/r3.anchor: فإن اللفظ يدل على أن فيه حذفا لأن حرف الجر لا بد له من متعلق ودل الشروع على تعيينه

BURHAN:v1p194#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك ومقاتل وعطاء
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, and Ata classify al-Fatiha as Meccan, while Mujahid classifies it as Medinan.
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r4.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب قال ابن عباس والضحاك ومقاتل وعطاء إنها مكية وقال مجاهد مدنية

BURHAN:v3p199/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r2.speaker: البصريون
BURHAN:v3p199/r2.claim: The Basrans analyze بسم الله as part of a nominal sentence, meaning my beginning is in God's name.
BURHAN:v3p199/r2.anchor: فقال البصريون الجملة اسمية أي ابتدائي بسم الله

BURHAN:v3p199/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v3p199/r3.claim: The Kufans analyze بسم الله as part of a verbal sentence.
BURHAN:v3p199/r3.anchor: وقال الكوفيون الجملة فعلية وتابعهم الزمخشري

BURHAN:v3p199/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p199/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p199/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari follows the Kufans but puts the implied verb after God's name and varies it by context; the author prefers this for contextual fit and foregrounding God's name.
BURHAN:v3p199/r4.anchor: ولكن خالفهم في موضعين أحدهما أنهم يقدرون الفعل مقدما وهو يقدره مؤخرا والثاني أنهم يقدرونه فعل البداية وهو يقدره في كل موضع بحسبه

BURHAN:v1p207/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r1.speaker: أبو ميسرة
BURHAN:v1p207/r1.claim: An account through Abū Isḥāq from Abū Maysara says al-Fātiḥa was the first revelation; it describes the Prophet hearing a voice, fleeing, and then the angel's descent and the opening of the sūra.
BURHAN:v1p207/r1.anchor: من طريق أبى إسحاق عن أبى ميسرة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سمع الصوت

BURHAN:v1p207/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p207/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr calls the report that al-Fātiḥa came first disconnected.
BURHAN:v1p207/r2.anchor: وقال القاضى أبو بكر فى الانتصار وهذا الخبر منقطع

BURHAN:v1p207/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.claim: The views can be reconciled: اقرأ was the first verses, المدثر the first preaching commands, and al-Fātiḥa the first complete sūra revealed.
BURHAN:v1p207/r4.anchor: أن أول ما نزل من الآيات ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ وأول ما نزل من أوامر التبليغ ﴿ يا أيها المدثر ﴾

BURHAN:v1p438/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p438/r3.speaker: ابن حبان
BURHAN:v1p438/r3.claim: Ibn Hibban reads the report comparing al-Fatiha with the Torah and Gospel as a difference in reward granted by God’s favor, not as intrinsic superiority within the Quran.
BURHAN:v1p438/r3.anchor: قال ابن حبان فى حديث أبى بن كعب رضى الله عنه ما أنزل الله فى التوارة ولا فى الإنجيل مثل أم القرآن

BURHAN:v1p438/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p438/r4.speaker: ابن حبان
BURHAN:v1p438/r4.claim: Ibn Hibban says calling al-Fatiha the greatest surah means greatest in reward, not that one part of the Quran is intrinsically superior.
BURHAN:v1p438/r4.anchor: قال وقوله أعظم سورة أراد به فى الأجر لا أن بعض القرآن أفضل من بعض

BURHAN:v1p439/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p439/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p439/r1.claim: Abu Said reports the Prophet calling al-Fatiha the greatest surah in a Bukhari narration; al-Zarkashi says this does not conflict with Ayat al-Kursi’s rank among verses, since the comparisons concern surahs and verses respectively.
BURHAN:v1p439/r1.anchor: وهذا لا يعارض ما قبله بأفضلية الفاتحة لأن تلك باعتبار السور وهذه باعتبار الآيات

ITQAN:v4p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v4p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ITQAN:v4p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

ITQAN:v4p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

ITQAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

ITQAN:v4p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

ITQAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

ITQAN:v1p114/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.claim: Among the material granted to Muhammad but not to any earlier prophet are al-Fatiha, Ayat al-Kursi, and the conclusion of al-Baqara.
ITQAN:v1p114/r1.anchor: من الثاني الفاتحة وآية الكرسي وخاتمة البقرة كما تقدم في الأحاديث قريبا

ITQAN:v1p210/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p210/r1.claim: Treating the basmala merely as a separator between sūras is an unsafe claim; if that were its sole function, it would not appear between al-Anfal and Bara'a.
ITQAN:v1p210/r1.anchor: بأن هذا فيه تغرير ولا يجوز ارتكابه لمجرد الفصل ولو كانت له لكتبت بين براءة والأنفال

ITQAN:v1p210/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p210/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet counted the basmala as a verse in his recitation of the opening sūra, but did not count عليهم as one.
ITQAN:v1p210/r2.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين ﴾ . . . الحديث وفيه وعد ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾ آية ولم يعد ﴿ عليهم ﴾

ITQAN:v1p210/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p210/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan concealed from people the Quran’s greatest verse, the basmala.
ITQAN:v1p210/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال إسترق الشيطان من الناس أعظم آية من القرآن ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾

ITQAN:v1p210/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p210/r4.claim: In a report through Mujahid, Ibn Abbas says people neglected a verse revealed only to Muhammad, perhaps also Solomon: the basmala.
ITQAN:v1p210/r4.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال أغفل الناس آية من كتاب الله لم تنزل على أحد سوى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p210/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p210/r5.claim: A weak report through Burayda has the Prophet identify the basmala as the verse given to him after Solomon and recited at the opening of prayer.
ITQAN:v1p210/r5.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا أخرج من المسجد حتى أخبرك بآية لم تنزل على نبي بعد سليمان غيري

ITQAN:v1p210/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p210/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet learned a sūra’s boundary when the basmala was revealed; al-Bazzar adds that it marked a completed sūra and the next one.
ITQAN:v1p210/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يعرف فصل السورة حتى تنزل عليه ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾

ITQAN:v1p210/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p210/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims knew a sūra had ended when the basmala descended; al-Hakim’s chain meets the standards of the two Sahih collections.
ITQAN:v1p210/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان المسلمون لا يعلمون انقضاء السورة حتى تنزل ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾ فإذا نزلت علموا أن السورة قد انقضت إسناده على شرط الشيخين

ITQAN:v1p210/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p210/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p210/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Gabriel recited the basmala, the Prophet knew it was a sūra; al-Hakim grades the chain sound.
ITQAN:v1p210/r8.anchor: عن سعيد عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا جاءه جبريل فقرأ ﴿ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ﴾ علم أنها سورة إسناده صحيح

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r6.speaker: المالكية
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r6.claim: Malikis and others who deny the basmala’s Quranic status argue that it was not mutawatir at surah openings and therefore is not Quran.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r6.anchor: المالكية وغيرهم ممن قال بإنكار البسملة

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r7.claim: The author denies that the basmala lacked tawatur: its unmarked inclusion in Companion and later codices proves its Quranic status, since they prohibited writing non-Quranic material there and would not mislead Muslims.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r7.anchor: وأجيب من قبلنا بمنع كونها لم تتواتر فرب متواتر عند قوم دون آخرين

ITQAN:v3p283/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r9.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v3p283/r9.claim: The most specialized form of a fine opening is barāʿat al-istihlāl, which signals the subject to come; al-Bayhaqi cites al-Hasan that knowledge of the earlier scriptures and Qur’an was concentrated into the Fatiha.
ITQAN:v3p283/r9.anchor: والعلم الأسنى في ذلك سورة الفاتحة التي هي مطلع القرآن فإنها مشتملة على جميع مقاصده كما قال البيهقي

ITQAN:v4p337/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p337/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p337/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi estimates Qur'anic sciences by multiplying its words by four—outer meaning, inner meaning, limit, and point of access—yielding vast totals, and says combinations and relations are beyond counting or human knowledge.
ITQAN:v4p337/r1.anchor: علوم القرآن خمسون علما وأربعمائة علم وسبعة آلاف علم وسبعون ألف علم على عدد كلم القرآن مضروبة في أربعة

ITQAN:v4p337/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p337/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p337/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi divides Qur'anic knowledge into monotheism (creatures and God's names, attributes, and acts), reminder (promise, threat, afterlife, and purification), and rulings (duties, benefits, harms, commands, prohibitions, and recommendations).
ITQAN:v4p337/r2.anchor: وأما علوم القرآن فثلاثة توحيد وتذكير وأحكام

ITQAN:v4p337/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p337/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p337/r3.claim: For Ibn al-Arabi, al-Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother because it contains all three domains, while al-Ikhlas is a third because it contains monotheism alone.
ITQAN:v4p337/r3.anchor: ولذلك كانت الفاتحة أم القرآن لأن فيها الأقسام الثلاثة وسورة الإخلاص ثلثه

ITQAN:v4p337/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p337/r5.speaker: علي بن عيسى
ITQAN:v4p337/r5.claim: Ali ibn Isa enumerates thirty Qur'anic subjects, including signs, analogy, commands and prohibitions, promise and threat, paradise and hell, divine names and acts, gratitude, argument, ethics, wisdom, praise, blame, and moral instruction.
ITQAN:v4p337/r5.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى القرآن يشتمل على ثلاثين شيئا الإعلام والتشبيه والأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v1p41/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p41/r1.claim: Most authorities consider al-Fātiḥa Meccan. Its identification with the seven oft-repeated verses in a Meccan sūra implies it was already revealed, and prayer was obligatory in Mecca with no known prayer omitting it.
ITQAN:v1p41/r1.anchor: الفاتحة الأكثرون على أنها مكية بل ورد أنها أول ما نزل كما سيأتي في النوع الثامن واستدل لذلك بقوله تعالى ﴿ ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني ﴾

ITQAN:v1p41/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ITQAN:v1p41/r2.claim: A report transmitted by al-Wāḥidī and al-Thaʿlabī says al-Fātiḥa descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne.
ITQAN:v1p41/r2.anchor: روى الواحدي والثعلبي من طريق العلاء بن المسيب عن الفضل بن عمرو عن علي بن أبي طالب قال نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش

ITQAN:v1p41/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v1p41/r3.claim: Mujāhid is reliably reported by al-Firyābī and Abū ʿUbayd to consider al-Fātiḥa Medinan; al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl calls this a slip, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya also names several who held it.
ITQAN:v1p41/r3.anchor: واشتهر عن مجاهد القول بأنها مدنية أخرجه الفريابي في تفسيره وأبو عبيد في الفضائل بسند صحيح عنه

ITQAN:v1p41/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v1p41/r4.claim: A good-chain report from Abū Hurayra says Satan groaned when al-Fātiḥa was revealed in Medina, but al-Suyūṭī allows that the Medina clause may be Mujāhid's insertion.
ITQAN:v1p41/r4.anchor: وورد عن أبي هريرة بإسناد جيد قال الطبراني في الأوسط حدثنا عبيد ابن غنام نبأنا أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة نبأنا أبو الأحوص عن منصور عن مجاهد عن أبي هريرة

ITQAN:v1p41/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p41/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v1p41/r5.claim: Some say al-Fātiḥa was revealed twice, once in Mecca and once in Medina, to magnify its honor; a fourth view divides it between the two cities.
ITQAN:v1p41/r5.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أنها نزلت مرتين مرة بمكة ومرة بالمدينة مبالغة في تشريفها وفيها قول رابع أنها نزلت نصفين نصفها بمكة ونصفها بالمدينة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r1.speaker: أبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r1.claim: The author's father thought the regular qunut supplication was Quran because he saw the Prophet repeat it in prayer, and held to this despite the Companions' disagreement.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r1.anchor: يدعو به في الصلاة دعاء دائما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba doubts the report that Abdullah omitted Fatiha from his codex and says no Muslim should infer that this learned, Quran-devoted Companion did not know it was Quran.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.anchor: فإني أشك فيما روي عن عبد الله من تركه إثباتها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.claim: The Prophet praised Abdullah's recitation, telling people who wanted the Quran fresh as revealed to follow Ibn Umm ʿAbd's reading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.anchor: النبي) صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول: «من أحب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.claim: Umar described Abdullah as a container filled with knowledge, supporting Ibn Qutayba's case for his learning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.anchor: وعمر يقول فيه: كنيف ملىء علما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.claim: The Prophet's statement لا صلاة إلا بسورة الحمد supports Fatiha's indispensable place in prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.anchor: رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يؤم بها، وقال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.claim: Fatiha is the seven oft-repeated and Mother of the Book, meaning its greatest and earliest part; Mecca is similarly called Mother of Villages because it is oldest.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.anchor: أم الكتاب، أي أعظمه، وأقدم ما نزل منه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.speaker: أهل النظر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.claim: The theorists explain that Abdullah did not write Fatiha because compilation guarded against doubt, forgetting, additions, and omissions, while it was short and repeated every prayer and rakʿa.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.anchor: أهل النظر، إلى القرآن إنما كتب وجمع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba concludes that Abdullah knew Fatiha was Quran but saw no need to write it, since no Muslim could neglect learning it or praying with it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.anchor: ترك كتابتها وهو يعلم أنها من القرآن

NASHR:v1p229/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p229/r1.claim: A pause on an incomplete fragment such as “bi-smi,” “al-ḥamdu,” or “rabbi” leaves the utterance unfinished and without an intelligible meaning.
NASHR:v1p229/r1.anchor: نحو الوقف على: بسم، وعلى: الحمد، وعلى: رب، وملك يوم، وإياك

ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس وعلي بن الحسين وقتادة وأبو العالية وعطاء وابن جبير ومحمد بن يحيى بن حبان وجعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r1.claim: These authorities hold that al-Fātiḥa is Meccan; Abū Ḥayyān says the claim is supported by the seven oft-repeated verses being mentioned in a Meccan sūra.
ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r1.anchor: قال علي ،   وابن عباس ،   وعلي بن الحسين ،   وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة وعطاء بن يسار ومجاهد وسواد بن زياد والزهري وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
ABUHAYYAN:1:1/r2.claim: These authorities hold that al-Fātiḥa is Medinan, contrary to the Meccan attribution.
