QURTUBI:1:1/r151.anchor: وأما أهل الكوفة من القراء والفقهاء فإنهم عدوا فيها " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

QURTUBI:1:1/r152.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r152.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r152.claim: Writing the basmala in muṣḥafs may mark a sūra boundary or blessing, rather than prove verse status.
QURTUBI:1:1/r152.anchor: ولكن لكونها قرآنا أو لكونها فاصلة بين السور

QURTUBI:1:1/r153.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r153.speaker: الصحابة
QURTUBI:1:1/r153.claim: The Companions reportedly knew a sūra had ended when the basmala was revealed; al-Ḥasan says it appeared in letters and only in al-Naml as Qurʾān.
QURTUBI:1:1/r153.anchor: كنا لا نعرف انقضاء السورة حتى تنزل " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

QURTUBI:1:1/r154.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r154.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r154.claim: Qurṭubī rejects reasoning as proof of Qurʾānic text and notes uncertainty about the basmala at each sūra.
QURTUBI:1:1/r154.anchor: والفيصل أن القرآن لا يثبت بالنظر والاستدلال

QURTUBI:1:1/r155.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r155.speaker: عائشة وأنس بن مالك
QURTUBI:1:1/r155.claim: Muslim’s reports say the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar began with al-Ḥamd and did not mention the basmala in recitation.
QURTUBI:1:1/r155.anchor: فكانوا يستفتحون بالحمد لله رب العالمين ، لا يذكرون " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

QURTUBI:1:1/r156.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r156.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r156.claim: Qurṭubī argues generations at the Prophet’s Medina mosque through Mālik’s era did not recite the basmala.
QURTUBI:1:1/r156.anchor: ولم يقرأ أحد فيه قط " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم " اتباعا للسنة

QURTUBI:1:1/r157.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r157.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI:1:1/r157.claim: Mālik’s well-known school does not count the basmala as a verse and omits it in obligatory prayer, but permits voluntary recitation.
QURTUBI:1:1/r157.anchor: أنها ليست عندهم آية من فاتحة الكتاب ولا غيرها

QURTUBI:1:1/r158.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r158.speaker: ابن نافع
QURTUBI:1:1/r158.claim: Another report from Mālik says to begin every obligatory and voluntary prayer with the basmala.
QURTUBI:1:1/r158.anchor: وروى عنه ابن نافع ابتداء القراءة بها في الصلاة الفرض والنفل

QURTUBI:1:1/r159.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r159.speaker: ابن عمر وابن شهاب
QURTUBI:1:1/r159.claim: Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Shihāb, with al-Shāfiʿī and others, require the basmala.
QURTUBI:1:1/r159.anchor: ومن أهل المدينة من يقول : إنه لابد فيها من " بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم "

QURTUBI:1:1/r160.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r160.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r160.claim: Qurṭubī says the basmala dispute is interpretive, not a basis for declaring Muslims unbelievers.
QURTUBI:1:1/r160.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن المسألة مسألة اجتهادية لا قطعية

QURTUBI:1:1/r161.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r161.speaker: أبو حنيفة والثوري
QURTUBI:1:1/r161.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Thawrī, Aḥmad, and others recite the basmala quietly with al-Fātiḥa.
QURTUBI:1:1/r161.anchor: وقد ذهب جمع من العلماء إلى الإسرار بها مع الفاتحة

QURTUBI:1:1/r162.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r162.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI:1:1/r162.claim: Anas reports not hearing the Prophet recite the basmala aloud; Qurṭubī prefers quiet recitation to reconcile the reports.
QURTUBI:1:1/r162.anchor: فلم أسمع أحداً منهم يجهر ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

QURTUBI:1:1/r163.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r163.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI:1:1/r163.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr links quiet basmala recitation to Musaylima’s claim to al-Raḥmān; the practice persisted after its cause passed.
QURTUBI:1:1/r163.anchor: سعيد بن جبير قال : هذا محمد يذكر رحمان اليمامة - يعنون مسيلمة -

QURTUBI:1:1/r164.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r164.speaker: الأمة
QURTUBI:1:1/r164.claim: The community agrees the basmala may begin books and letters; early authorities discouraged it before poetry, while others allowed it.
QURTUBI:1:1/r164.anchor: اتفقت الأمة على جواز كتبها في أول كل كتاب من كتب العلم والرسائل

QURTUBI:1:1/r165.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r165.speaker: أبو بكر الخطيب
QURTUBI:1:1/r165.claim: Abū Bakr al-Khaṭīb prefers writing the basmala at the start of poetry collections.
QURTUBI:1:1/r165.anchor: قال أبو بكر الخطيب : وهو الذي نختاره ونستحبه

QURTUBI:1:1/r166.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r166.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI:1:1/r166.claim: Al-Māwardī notes the coined verb basmala for saying “in God’s name”; linguists document related devotional abbreviations.
QURTUBI:1:1/r166.anchor: ويقال لمن قال بسم الله : مبسمل ، وهي لغة مولدة

QURTUBI:1:1/r167.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r167.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
QURTUBI:1:1/r167.claim: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa uses basmala as a verb in poetry, describing Laylā as having said it.

QURTUBI:1:1/r168.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r168.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r168.claim: The law recommends basmala at the start of eating, drinking, slaughter, intimacy, purification, travel, and other acts.
QURTUBI:1:1/r168.anchor: ندب الشرع إلى ذكر البسملة في أول كل فعل

QURTUBI:1:1/r169.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r169.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:1/r169.claim: The Prophet instructs householders to close doors, extinguish lamps, cover vessels, and tie waterskins while invoking God’s name.
QURTUBI:1:1/r169.anchor: أغلق بابك واذكر اسم الله وأطفئ مصباحك

QURTUBI:1:1/r170.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r170.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:1/r170.claim: The Prophet teaches a basmala supplication before intimacy, promising protection for a child conceived from Satan’s harm.
QURTUBI:1:1/r170.anchor: إذا أراد أن يأتي أهله قال بسم الله اللهم جنبنا الشيطان

QURTUBI:1:1/r171.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r171.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:1/r171.claim: The Prophet tells ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama to invoke God, eat with the right hand, and take food nearest him; Satan shares food without invocation.
QURTUBI:1:1/r171.anchor: يا غلام سم الله وكل بيمينك وكل مما يليك

QURTUBI:1:1/r172.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r172.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص
QURTUBI:1:1/r172.claim: For pain, the Prophet tells ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ to say the basmala three times and seek refuge in God’s power seven times.
QURTUBI:1:1/r172.anchor: ضع يدك على الذي تألم من جسدك وقل بسم الله ثلاثا

QURTUBI:1:1/r173.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r173.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI:1:1/r173.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet invoked God when using water for purification, then poured it over his hands.
QURTUBI:1:1/r173.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا مس طهوره سمى الله تعالى

QURTUBI:1:1/r174.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r174.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI:1:1/r174.claim: Qurṭubī says the basmala answers Qadarites: God commands invocation at the start of every act, showing people do not independently control actions.
QURTUBI:1:1/r174.anchor: وفيها رد على القدرية وغيرهم ممن يقول : إن أفعالهم مقدورة لهم

QURTUBI:1:1/r175.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r175.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r175.claim: Bismillah means “by God,” whose creation and decree enable acts; alternatively it means beginning with God’s aid, guidance, and blessing.

QURTUBI:1:1/r176.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r176.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:1:1/r176.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats ism as added, adducing Labīd’s verse where “name” appears to mean “peace.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r176.anchor: ذهب أبو عبيدة معمر بن المثنى إلى أن " اسم " صلة زائدة

QURTUBI:1:1/r177.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r177.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r177.claim: Qurṭubī’s scholars also use Labīd’s verse to argue name and named are identical.
QURTUBI:1:1/r177.anchor: وقد استدل علماؤنا بقول لبيد هذا على أن الاسم هو المسمى

QURTUBI:1:1/r178.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r178.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI:1:1/r178.claim: Quṭrub says ism is added to magnify and honor God’s remembrance.
QURTUBI:1:1/r178.anchor: فقال قطرب : زيدت لإجلال ذكره تعالى وتعظيمه

QURTUBI:1:1/r179.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r179.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI:1:1/r179.claim: Al-Akhfash says ism shifts the phrase from an oath to an invocation for blessing; the underlying phrase is bi-Allah.
QURTUBI:1:1/r179.anchor: وقال الأخفش : زيدت ليخرج بذكرها من حكم القسم إلى قصد التبرك

QURTUBI:1:1/r180.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r180.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:1:1/r180.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the bāʾ as an imperative: begin in God’s name.

QURTUBI:1:1/r181.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r181.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:1:1/r181.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads the bāʾ as a statement: I began in God’s name.

QURTUBI:1:1/r182.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r182.speaker: نحاة البصرة
QURTUBI:1:1/r182.claim: Basran grammarians parse bismillah as the predicate of an omitted beginning or as governed by “established” or “fixed.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r182.anchor: وقيل : الخبر محذوف ، أي ابتدائي مستقر أو ثابت باسم الله

QURTUBI:1:1/r183.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r183.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r183.claim: The alif in ism is omitted in the basmala through frequent use; it remains in the less common “Read in the name of your Lord.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r183.anchor: تكتب بغير ألف استغناء عنها بباء الإلصاق

QURTUBI:1:1/r184.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r184.speaker: الكسائي وسعيد الأخفش
QURTUBI:1:1/r184.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and Saʿīd al-Akhfash also omit the alif before al-Raḥmān and al-Qāhir; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb omits it only before Allah.
QURTUBI:1:1/r184.anchor: وقال يحيى بن وثاب : لا تحذف إلا مع " بسم الله " فقط

QURTUBI:1:1/r185.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r185.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r185.claim: Three explanations for the bāʾ’s kasra are matching its function, the genitive of nouns, or distinguishing it from kāf used as a noun.
QURTUBI:1:1/r185.anchor: واختلف في تخصيص باء الجر بالكسر على ثلاثة معان

QURTUBI:1:1/r186.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r186.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI:1:1/r186.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s phrase “like the water bird” illustrates kāf functioning as a noun rather than a particle.

QURTUBI:1:1/r187.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r187.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI:1:1/r187.claim: Ism has a lost wāw and pattern ifʿ; its plural and diminutive are preserved by usage and poetry.
QURTUBI:1:1/r187.anchor: اسم ، وزنه إفع ، والذاهب منه الواو ؛ لأنه من سموت

QURTUBI:1:1/r188.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r188.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
QURTUBI:1:1/r188.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā derives the form with ḍamma from samawtu and with kasra from samaytu; Arabic also uses sum and sim.
QURTUBI:1:1/r188.anchor: قال أحمد ين يحيى : من ضم الألف أخذه من سموت أسمو

QURTUBI:1:1/r189.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r189.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI:1:1/r189.claim: The Basrans derive ism from sumūw, elevation, explaining names as raising or distinguishing referents.
QURTUBI:1:1/r189.anchor: فقال البصريون : هو مشتق من السمو وهو العلو والرفعة

QURTUBI:1:1/r190.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r190.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI:1:1/r190.claim: The Kūfans derive ism from sima, a mark, because a name marks its referent.
QURTUBI:1:1/r190.anchor: وقال الكوفيون : إنه مشتق من السمة وهي العلامة

QURTUBI:1:1/r191.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r191.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r191.claim: Qurṭubī prefers the Basran derivation: diminutive sumayy and plural asmāʾ point to s-m-w rather than wasm.
QURTUBI:1:1/r191.anchor: والأول أصح ؛ لأنه يقال في التصغير سمي وفي الجمع أسماء

QURTUBI:1:1/r192.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r192.speaker: أهل السنة
QURTUBI:1:1/r192.claim: The Basran derivation entails God always possessed names and attributes independent of creation; Qurṭubī identifies this as Sunni doctrine.

QURTUBI:1:1/r193.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r193.speaker: المعتزلة
QURTUBI:1:1/r193.claim: The Kūfan derivation is linked to the Muʿtazilite claim that creatures assigned God names and attributes which disappear with creation.
QURTUBI:1:1/r193.anchor: وهذا قول المعتزلة وهو خلاف ما أجمعت عليه الأمة

QURTUBI:1:1/r194.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r194.speaker: أهل الحق
QURTUBI:1:1/r194.claim: The people of truth, including al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr and Ibn Fūrak, say name and named are identical.
QURTUBI:1:1/r194.anchor: فذهب أهل الحق فيما نقل القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب إلى أن الاسم هو المسمى

QURTUBI:1:1/r195.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r195.speaker: ابن الحصار
QURTUBI:1:1/r195.claim: Ibn al-Ḥaṣṣār contrasts those who say names designate only essence with those who say they denote attributes of the essence.
QURTUBI:1:1/r195.anchor: من ينفي الصفات من المبتدعة يزعم أن لا مدلول للتسميات إلا الذات

QURTUBI:1:1/r196.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r196.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r196.claim: Allah is the greatest, most comprehensive divine name, unique to God and not pluralized; 19:65 may mean no one bears that name.
QURTUBI:1:1/r196.anchor: هذا الاسم أكبر أسمائه سبحانه وأجمعها

QURTUBI:1:1/r197.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r197.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r197.claim: Allah means the true existent who gathers divine and lordly attributes, the one alone worthy of worship.
QURTUBI:1:1/r197.anchor: فالله اسم للموجود الحق الجامع لصفات الإلهية

QURTUBI:1:1/r198.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r198.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
QURTUBI:1:1/r198.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sibawayh derive Allah from ilāh, with the article replacing hamza, as nās derives from unās.
QURTUBI:1:1/r198.anchor: فروى سيبويه عن الخليل أن أصله إلاه ، مثل فعال

QURTUBI:1:1/r199.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r199.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
QURTUBI:1:1/r199.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ explain bismillah as bi-ism al-ilāh, with hamza deletion and lām assimilation.
QURTUBI:1:1/r199.anchor: فحذفوا الهمزة وأدغموا اللام الأولى في الثانية

QURTUBI:1:1/r200.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r200.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI:1:1/r200.claim: Another proposal derives ilāh from walah, bewilderment, because minds are overwhelmed by God’s attributes.
QURTUBI:1:1/r200.anchor: ثم قيل : هو مشتق من " وله " إذا تحير

QURTUBI:1:1/r201.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r201.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:1:1/r201.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God is called ilāh because creatures turn to Him with needs and plead in hardship.
QURTUBI:1:1/r201.anchor: لأن الخلق يتألهون إليه في حوائجهم

QURTUBI:1:1/r202.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r202.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
QURTUBI:1:1/r202.claim: Al-Khalīl says creatures worship God; the verb has two dialectal vowels.
QURTUBI:1:1/r202.anchor: لأن الخلق يألهون إليه ( بنصب اللام ) ويألهون

QURTUBI:1:1/r203.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r203.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:1:1/r203.claim: On the reading “your gods” in 7:127, Ibn ʿAbbās and others gloss it as “your worship.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r203.anchor: قالوا : فاسم الله مشتق من هذا ، فالله سبحانه معناه المقصود بالعبادة

QURTUBI:1:1/r204.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r204.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r204.claim: Other proposals derive Allah from elevation, worship, or the pronoun hāʾ extended by a possessive lām and article.
QURTUBI:1:1/r204.anchor: وقيل : إنه مشتق من الارتفاع ، فكانت العرب تقول

QURTUBI:1:1/r205.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r205.speaker: الشافعي وأبو المعالي والخطابي والغزالي
QURTUBI:1:1/r205.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, al-Juwaynī, al-Khaṭṭābī, and al-Ghazālī treat Allah as a non-derived proper name with inseparable alif-lām.
QURTUBI:1:1/r205.anchor: منهم الشافعي وأبو المعالي والخطابي والغزالي

QURTUBI:1:1/r206.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r206.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI:1:1/r206.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī argues the article belongs to Allah’s name because it accepts the vocative yā Allah, unlike al-Raḥmān or al-Raḥīm.
QURTUBI:1:1/r206.anchor: قال الخطابي : والدليل على أن الألف واللام من بنية هذا الاسم

QURTUBI:1:1/r207.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r207.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:1:1/r207.claim: Some say al-Raḥmān is not derived: if from mercy it would take an object, and Arabs would not ask “What is al-Raḥmān?”
QURTUBI:1:1/r207.anchor: قال بعضهم : لا اشتقاق له لأنه من الأسماء المختصة به سبحانه

QURTUBI:1:1/r208.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r208.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:1:1/r208.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says pagans knew the referent but not the attribute, asking what al-Raḥmān was rather than who.

QURTUBI:1:1/r209.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r209.speaker: ابن الحصار
QURTUBI:1:1/r209.claim: Ibn al-Ḥaṣṣār counters that 13:30 explicitly says the disbelievers rejected al-Raḥmān.
QURTUBI:1:1/r209.anchor: وكأنه رحمه الله لم يقرأ الآية الأخرى : " وهم يكفرون بالرحمن "

QURTUBI:1:1/r210.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r210.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI:1:1/r210.claim: Most scholars derive al-Raḥmān from mercy as an intensive form, uniquely divine and not dualized or pluralized.
QURTUBI:1:1/r210.anchor: وذهب الجمهور من الناس إلى أن " الرحمن " مشتق من الرحمة مبني على المبالغة

QURTUBI:1:1/r211.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r211.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
QURTUBI:1:1/r211.claim: A report graded ṣaḥīḥ by al-Tirmidhī quotes God saying “I am al-Raḥmān,” who created kinship and derived its name from His own.
QURTUBI:1:1/r211.anchor: أنا الرحمن خلقت الرحم وشققت لها اسما من اسمي

QURTUBI:1:1/r212.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r212.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI:1:1/r212.claim: Al-Mubarrad claims al-Raḥmān is Hebrew paired with Arabic al-Raḥīm; Qurṭubī rejects the claim.
QURTUBI:1:1/r212.anchor: زعم المبرد فيما ذكر ابن الأنباري في كتاب " الزاهر " له : أن " الرحمن " اسم عبراني

QURTUBI:1:1/r213.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r213.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:1:1/r213.claim: Qatāda says the basmala is God praising Himself; al-Zajjāj approves it as adjectival praise.

QURTUBI:1:1/r214.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r214.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI:1:1/r214.claim: Quṭrub says al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm are paired for emphasis; al-Zajjāj approves this rhetoric.
QURTUBI:1:1/r214.anchor: وقال قطرب : يجوز أن يكون جمع بينهما للتوكيد

QURTUBI:1:1/r215.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r215.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI:1:1/r215.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd explains the paired names as favor after favor, renewed blessing, and a promise sustaining hope.
QURTUBI:1:1/r215.anchor: قاله محمد بن يزيد : إنه تفضل بعد تفضل ، وإنعام بعد إنعام

QURTUBI:1:1/r216.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r216.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:1:1/r216.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm as synonyms, like nadmān and nadīm.
QURTUBI:1:1/r216.anchor: فقيل : هما بمعنى واحد ، كندمان ونديم

QURTUBI:1:1/r217.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r217.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI:1:1/r217.claim: The majority distinguish them: faʿlān marks overwhelming action, while faʿīl can be active or passive; al-Raḥmān is specific in name but broad in action.
QURTUBI:1:1/r217.anchor: ف " الرحمن " خاص الاسم عام الفعل . و " الرحيم " عام الاسم خاص الفعل

QURTUBI:1:1/r218.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r218.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
QURTUBI:1:1/r218.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says al-Raḥmān covers all mercy but is exclusive to God, while al-Raḥīm especially concerns believers.
QURTUBI:1:1/r218.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : " الرحمن " اسم عام في جميع أنواع الرحمة

QURTUBI:1:1/r219.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r219.speaker: العرزمي
QURTUBI:1:1/r219.claim: Al-ʿArzamī says al-Raḥmān’s mercy reaches all creation through rain and senses, while al-Raḥīm guides believers.
QURTUBI:1:1/r219.anchor: وقال العرزمي{[46]} : " الرحمن " بجميع خلقه في الأمطار ونعم الحواس

QURTUBI:1:1/r220.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r220.speaker: ابن المبارك
QURTUBI:1:1/r220.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak says al-Raḥmān gives when asked while al-Raḥīm is angered when not asked; hadith supports this.
QURTUBI:1:1/r220.anchor: وقال ابن المبارك : " الرحمن " إذا سئل أعطي ، و " الرحيم " إذا لم يسأل غضب

QURTUBI:1:1/r221.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r221.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:1:1/r221.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls the names soft, one softer than the other; al-Khaṭṭābī objects and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl corrects it to “gentle.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r221.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هما اسمان رقيقان ، أحدهما أرق من الآخر

QURTUBI:1:1/r222.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r222.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
QURTUBI:1:1/r222.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl says the narrator confused “gentler” with “softer”; gentleness is divine.
QURTUBI:1:1/r222.anchor: وإنما هما اسمان رفيقان أحدهما أرفق من الآخر

QURTUBI:1:1/r223.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r223.speaker: أكثر العلماء
QURTUBI:1:1/r223.claim: Most scholars reserve al-Raḥmān for God, citing 17:110 and 43:45; Musaylima’s self-title became attached to him as “the liar.”
QURTUBI:1:1/r223.anchor: أكثر العلماء على أن " الرحمن " مختص بالله عز وجل

QURTUBI:1:1/r224.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r224.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:1:1/r224.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī reports al-Raḥmān may be the greatest name of God.
QURTUBI:1:1/r224.anchor: وقد قيل في اسمه الرحمن : إنه اسم الله الأعظم

QURTUBI:1:1/r225.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r225.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r225.claim: Al-Raḥīm can describe creatures; al-Raḥmān precedes it because it is more comprehensive, matching Qurʾānic order.
QURTUBI:1:1/r225.anchor: ولما في " الرحمن " من العموم قدم في كلامنا على " الرحيم "

QURTUBI:1:1/r226.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r226.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:1/r226.claim: Another interpretation makes al-Raḥīm a description of Muḥammad, through whom people reach God’s favor by following his message.
QURTUBI:1:1/r226.anchor: ف " الرحيم " نعت محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:1:1/r227.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r227.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI:1:1/r227.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī calls the basmala a cure and aid; al-Raḥmān aids believers and al-Raḥīm belongs to the repentant righteous.
QURTUBI:1:1/r227.anchor: روي عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه أنه قال في قوله " بسم الله " : إنه شفاء من كل داء

QURTUBI:1:1/r228.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r228.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:1/r228.claim: An esoteric report interprets basmala letters and says al-Raḥmān shows compassion to all creation, while al-Raḥīm is gentle toward believers.
QURTUBI:1:1/r228.anchor: أما الرحمن فالعاطف على البر والفاجر من خلقه

QURTUBI:1:1/r229.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r229.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI:1:1/r229.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār assigns basmala letters to divine glory, majesty, and sovereignty; another reading maps each letter to a divine name.
QURTUBI:1:1/r229.anchor: الباء بهاؤه والسين سناؤه فلا شيء أعلى منه

QURTUBI:1:1/r230.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r230.speaker: أم سلمة
QURTUBI:1:1/r230.claim: A report from Umm Salama pauses after al-Raḥīm with a cut hamza at al-Ḥamd; some Kūfans read this way.
QURTUBI:1:1/r230.anchor: روي عن أم سلمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " الرحيم . الحمد " يسكن الميم

QURTUBI:1:1/r231.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r231.speaker: جمهور الناس
QURTUBI:1:1/r231.claim: Most readers connect al-Raḥīm to al-Ḥamd, using the genitive and connecting hamza.
QURTUBI:1:1/r231.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس : " الرحيم الحمد " ، تعرب " الرحيم " بالخفض

QURTUBI:1:1/r232.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r232.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI:1:1/r232.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reports an Arab reading al-Raḥīma al-ḥamdu; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says no reader transmitted it.
QURTUBI:1:1/r232.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن بعض العرب أنها تقرأ " الرحيمَ الحمد " بفتح الميم

QURTUBI:1:1/r233.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:1/r233.speaker: يحيى بن زياد
QURTUBI:1:1/r233.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes the final analogy to Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād’s analysis of alif-lām-mīm.
QURTUBI:1:1/r233.anchor: وهذا نظر يحيى بن زياد في قوله تعالى : " الَم الله "

RAZI:1:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r1.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
RAZI:1:1/r1.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI:1:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r2.claim: Razi says the Fātiḥa can yield ten thousand useful questions; he wrote the introduction to show that this claim is attainable, despite the scoffing of envious and ignorant opponents.
RAZI:1:1/r2.anchor: يمكن أن يستنبط من فوائدها ونفائسها عشرة آلاف مسألة

RAZI:1:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r3.claim: Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited act, including sins and wrong beliefs.
RAZI:1:1/r3.anchor: المراد منه الاستعاذة بالله من جميع المنهيات والمحظورات

RAZI:1:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:1:1/r4.claim: Razi cites as a famous prophetic report that the community will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one; he says this shows the other seventy-two hold false creeds.
RAZI:1:1/r4.anchor: ستفترق أمتي على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة : كلهم في النار إلا فرقة واحدة

RAZI:1:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r5.claim: Each deviant Muslim sect errs across many questions concerning God’s essence, attributes, rulings, acts and names, as well as compulsion, decree, justice, reward, resurrection, promises, threats, legal status and imamate.
RAZI:1:1/r5.anchor: مسائل كثيرة من المباحث المعلقة بذات الله تعالى ،   وبصفاته ،   وبأحكامه

RAZI:1:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r6.claim: Razi says the roughly seven hundred deviant sects outside the Muslim community add further errors in rational theology and questions of essences and attributes, all covered by seeking refuge.
RAZI:1:1/r6.anchor: فرق الضلالات من الخارجين عن هذه الأمة يقربون من سبعمائة

RAZI:1:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r7.claim: Prohibited actions include whatever the Qur’an, mass-transmitted or solitary reports, communal consensus, or sound analogy forbids; their number exceeds a thousand and the refuge formula encompasses them all.
RAZI:1:1/r7.anchor: فهي عبارة عن كل ما ورد النهي عنه : إما في القرآن

RAZI:1:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r8.claim: One can seek refuge from something only after knowing it and recognizing its falsehood and ugliness; thus this formula contains thousands of substantial, certain questions.
RAZI:1:1/r8.anchor: الاستعاذة من الشيء لا تمكن إلا بعد معرفة المستعاذ منه

RAZI:1:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r9.speaker: العلماء
RAZI:1:1/r9.claim: Razi reports the scholarly convention that God has 1,001 sacred names found in scripture and Sunna, and says inquiry into each name is a noble subject.
RAZI:1:1/r9.anchor: قد اشتهر عند العلماء أن لله تعالى ألفا وواحدا من الأسماء المقدسة المطهرة

RAZI:1:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r10.claim: Knowing a divine name presupposes knowing its referent, arguments for the referent’s existence, and answers to objections against it; these inquiries alone exceed a thousand questions.
RAZI:1:1/r10.anchor: العلم بالاسم لا يحصل إلا إذا كان مسبوقا بالعلم بالمسمى

RAZI:1:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r11.claim: The bāʾ is for attachment and governs an implied verb: “In God’s name I begin performing acts of obedience.”
RAZI:1:1/r11.anchor: الباء في قوله { بسم الله } باء الإلصاق ،   وهي متعلقة بفعل

RAZI:1:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r12.claim: Understanding the implied beginning requires surveying all obedience: true creeds and sincere deeds, their proofs, and answers to objections, a body of inquiry that may exceed ten thousand questions.
RAZI:1:1/r12.anchor: بعد الوقوف على أقسام الطاعات ،   وهي العقائد الحقة والأعمال الصافية مع الدلائل والبينات

RAZI:1:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r13.claim: The refuge formula negates improper beliefs and acts, while the basmala affirms what ought to be believed and done; sound reason and clear truth support this order.
RAZI:1:1/r13.anchor: أعوذ بالله } إشارة إلى نفي ما لا ينبغي من العقائد والأعمال ،   وقوله { بسم الله

BURHAN:v1p198/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p198/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p198/r7.claim: Other reports say al-Fatiha descended with eighty thousand angels, the Throne Verse and Yunus with thirty thousand each, and “Ask those We sent before you” with twenty thousand.
BURHAN:v1p198/r7.anchor: وفاتحة الكتاب نزلت ومعها ثمانون ألف ملك وآية الكرسي نزلت ومعها ثلاثون ألف ملك وسورة يونس نزلت

IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.claim: ʿUrwa reports that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd was the first after the Prophet to recite the Qurʾān publicly in Mecca; Quraysh beat him as he continued, but he returned ready to repeat it.
IBNHISHAM:v1p314#2/r1.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: كان أول من جهر بالقرآن بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة عبد الله بن مسعود

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r3.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r3.claim: Al-Ghazālī reads the Fātiḥa’s repeated mention of mercy as signaling both perfect creation and provision for each world and mercy in the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r3.anchor: قال الغزالي في أوائل كتاب الجواهر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.claim: Biqāʿī associates al-Raḥmān with lordship in the first and second creations, and al-Raḥīm especially with the second creation, preservation, recompense, and special mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p706#2/r4.anchor: وهي أن الرحمن مشير غلى ما قال من جهة الربوبية

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Companions recited al-Fatiha over a man bitten or stung by an animal and accepted sheep after he recovered; the Prophet said the Book of God is the most deserving basis for payment.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نفرا من أصحاب رسول الله مروا بماء فيه لديغ أو سليم فعرض لهم رجل من أهل الحي

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r2.claim: The Prophet approves taking payment for healing by recitation, saying the Book of God is the most deserving thing for which payment may be taken.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أحق ما أخذتم عليه أجرا كتاب الله

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن جابر
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Jabir reports that the Prophet called al-Fatiha the best sūra revealed in the Qurʾan; the narrator thinks he also said it contains a cure for every illness.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن جابر أن رسول الله قال له ألا أخبرك بأخير سورة نزلت في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r4.speaker: السائب بن يزيد
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r4.claim: Al-Saʾib ibn Yazid reports that the Prophet performed a saliva-blowing healing recitation for him using al-Fatiha; the report’s chain is called weak.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r4.anchor: عن السائب بن يزيد قال: عوذني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بفاتحة الكتاب تفلا

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports the Prophet saying that al-Fatiha is a cure for poison.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله قال فاتحة الكتاب شفاء من السم

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد وأبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r6.claim: A second report attributed to the Prophet through Abu Saʿid and Abu Hurayra repeats that al-Fatiha is a cure for poison.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة مرفوعا مثله

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r7.speaker: عبد الملك بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr reports the Prophet saying that al-Fatiha cures every disease; the report’s transmitters are described as reliable.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r7.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن عمير قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب شفاء من كل داء

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r8.speaker: أبو سلمان
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r8.claim: Abu Salman reports that Companions recited al-Fatiha into the ear of a man suffering a seizure and he recovered; the Prophet called it the Mother of the Book and a cure for every disease.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r8.anchor: عن أبي سلمان قال: مر أصحاب رسول الله في بعض غزوهم على رجل قد صرع

DURR-FULL:v1p14/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r9.speaker: خارجة بن الصلت التميمي
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r9.claim: Kharija ibn al-Salt reports that, following the Prophet’s visit, he recited al-Fatiha twice morning and evening for three days over a chained man described as mad; the man recovered and his family paid him one hundred sheep.
DURR-FULL:v1p14/r9.anchor: عن خارجة بن الصلت التميمي عن عمه أنه أتى رسول الله ثم أقبل راجعا من عنده

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r1.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r1.claim: Ibn Sirin disliked calling al-Fatiha Umm al-Qurʾan, citing the Qurʾanic phrase “Umm al-Kitab,” and preferred the name Fatihat al-Kitab.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r1.anchor: عن أيوب أن مجمد بن سيرين كان يقول: يكره أن يقول: أم القرآن ويقول: قال الله (وعنده أم الكتاب) ولكن فاتحة الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet instructing reciters of al-Hamd to recite the basmala, which he calls the Mother of the Qurʾan, the Mother of the Book, and the seven oft-repeated; he says the basmala is one of its verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأتم {الحمد} فاقرؤا {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم}

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet identifying Umm al-Qurʾan as the Mother of the Qurʾan, Fatihat al-Kitab, the seven oft-repeated, and the Magnificent Qurʾan.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لأم القرآن: هي أم القرآن وهي فاتحة الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r5.speaker: عبد الجبار بن العلاء
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r5.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbar reports that Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna called al-Fatiha al-Wafiya, the complete or all-sufficing sūra.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r5.anchor: عن عبد الجبار بن العلاء قال: كان سفيان بن عيينة يسمي فاتحة الكتاب: الوافية

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن يحيى بن أبي كثير
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Abi Kathir calls al-Fatiha al-Kafiya, the sufficient one: it suffices without another sūra, while nothing else suffices in its place.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r6.anchor: عن عفيف بن سالم قال: سألت عبد الله بن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن قراءة الفاتحة خلف الإمام فقال: عن الكافية تسأل

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r7.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi directs a man with pain in his side to the foundation of the Qurʾan and identifies it as al-Fatiha.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي أن رجلا شكا إليه وجع الخاصرة فقال: عليك بأساس القرآن

DURR-FULL:v1p11/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that al-Fatiha has seven verses, including the basmala, and is the seven oft-repeated, the Magnificent Qurʾan, the Mother of the Qurʾan, and the Fatiha of the Book.
DURR-FULL:v1p11/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {الحمد لله رب العالمين} سبع آيات {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} إحداهن
